Byဧကမောင် -Oct 28, 2024

A worker who could potentially become disabled after injuring their head in a workplace incident at the GTIG Guohua Glorygarment factory which locates at Watayar Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon region was given only 50 lakhs as compensation instead of being taken responsibility and delivered healthcare.

The injured worker started working at the factory in December 2017 as an Operator and fell off from the transportation bus in the evening of July 2023 and injured on head.

Due to the impact, the worker suffered nose bleeding, dizziness and a CT scan was taken at the Yangon General Hospital and received treatment for an injury to the brain’s capillaries.

The worker returned to work at August 2023 as the factory doesn’t extend medical leave and the all super of the production line humilate the worker with a speaker while they can’t deliever the demands due to their health conditions.

In March 2024, the worker underwent further surgery at the Kyimyindaing public hospital for the injury, but the factory did not provide financial support for treatment.

STUM also stated that the factory did not provide any support for the worker from July 22, 2023 to July 8, 2024 who was injured in the workplace incident.

The employer’s COC, manager, employer’s WCC and officials of factory general worker organizations went negotiation in the manger office on October 25, 2024 and it was said that the employer can’t take any responsibility and will give 50 lakhs as compensation.

The injured worker requested assistance from STUM to help resolve the absences of the employer.

STUM stated that “STUM seems this incident is an incident where the entrepreneur is unwilling to take responsibility for the worker who was injured in their workplaceSTUM will assist in obtaining the legal rights for those harms.”

The factory force the worker to lie the reason of the injury to say that it was caused by a slip and the worker lost their right such as social security leave and wages.

The factory which failed to take responsibility on injured worker is manufacturing UNITED COLORS OF BENETTON, Bestseller and ONLY brand apparels.

ByMin Ni Kyaw -Oct 28, 2024

Workers from J-Land Myanmar garment factory said that female and male workers who don’t work overtime on Sunday are verbally abused by the manager in public.

“They call overtime on Sunday but some workers were not able to come due to various reasons but the manager lady verbally abuse them and curse at them in public rudely,” said a worker.

The manager also transfer the workers to non-native departments for not working overtime on Sundays.

The worker said that they work every day without day off in the last month and worked on a Sunday in October. Workers were forced to sign agreement about overtime which is submitted to the labour office but the overtime period exceeds the legal limits.

“Overtime is only until 6:00 pm on the paper but they call until 7:00 pm saying that the orders are important. We are not informed about that in advanced. Our families worried about us as we cannot inform them. The nurse allow us to go back to house if we are sick but the manager denies. The same goes for leave,” a worker said.

Workers are not getting any types of leaves except social security leave and the wages equivalent for the seniority leave is given only after a year and a half.

“We don’t know what leave is. The manager lady verbally abuse us for submitting social security. We don’t get paid our bonus if we are labeled as absent. We lost around 40,000 kyats including the subsidies. The wages equivalent for the seniority leave is given only if we seek assistant from the workplace coordination committee.

“The employer doesn’t acknowledge the committee and they declared that. The manager is rampaging and the committee have difficulties to address every problem as they are also workers,” they said.

There are around 100 underage workers in the factory and they are not paid the same. A worker said that those underage workers are ordered to take a break if there is an investigation.

“There are underage workers from 12 to 17 and they are ordered to take a break 2 day before of any investigation. They only get paid 5,200 kyats per day and their hourly overtime wages are calculated upon that. The salary workers get paid 7,500 kyats per day as peak,” said a worker.

ByMa Ma -Oct 28, 2024

It was reported in the stated owned newspaper on October (27) that Workplace and Labor Law Inspection Department conducted educational discussions on labor law rights, workplace safety and health issues using mobile vehicles.

But the workers said that there are many violations of the rights of the labor law in the workplaces and , factories in various townships in practice and the relevant departments are ignoring these situations although they are filling complaints.

“They have authority to take action but they stand with the employer and can’t negotiate. They told us to file a case if we are not satisfied but that is not easy for a worker to processed. If a worker goes to the department to file a complaint, the factory already know who complaint before they arrive back, This is the current situation,” said a former trade union member.

Workers complain about situations of their rights being violated to the relevant department but the employers seem to know in advance before the inspection and pre-train some workers to lie the inspectors.

“They only inquire the workers who the employer pre-trained. The employer taught those workers to say that everything is fine. It is impossible that they don’t know the violations but they themselves don’t care the labour rights,” said a female worker from garment industry.

The officials of the Ministry of Labor often stand with the employers since after the coup d’état, In addition, there are claims by the victims that labour authorities only blame the workers without solving the problem according to the law.

The Workplace and Labor Law Inspection Department of the Ministry of Labour said that they are educating labour rights by investigating workplace incidents, forming workplace safety and healthcare committees, measuring workplace situations and using assistant vehicles.

The factories are causing grievances to workers’ social life by calling excessive overtime that exceeds the legal limit, illegally dismissing, denying legal benefits, sexually harassing, exploiting and ignoring workers health but the township labour departments take almost no actions.

Eternal Fashion garment factory is calling excessive overtime.

We have to work mid night overtime today (October 26). We also have to work all day on October 27, which is Sunday.

The working hours are from 8:30 am to 8:10 pm.

The transportation is insufficient and it is not available at nights.

Workers from Samaluk, Twantay and Mawbe arrives home at around 11:00 pm which is not convenient for cooking let alone to eat.

The HR manager scold us with a speaker if we delay to go back to work for a minute after having lunch. Workers have to sleep unproperly for around half an hour while waiting for bus and workplace accidents occur rapidly due to excessive overtime.

We have to go back at 5:00 am if we work all night overtime. A female worker from the factory who worked all-night overtime was hit by a car at the BOC bus stop today October 24 when they get out from the car and we don’t know her situation yet.

The overtime is called since May and we have to work until 6:10 pm on Saturdays. We also have to work until 8:10 pm on weekdays.

It has been countless that we were forced to work mid-night (until 12:00 am) and all night (until 4:00 am) overtimes.Other factories finish the work at 4:00 pm on pay day but ours finish at 5:10 pm. There is a workplace coordination committee but they don’t stand for the workers.

The manager and supervisors doesn’t let the factory know our problems. They are well paid. A manager got paid around 20 lakhs and an all super get paid more than 15 lakhs.

We, sewing workers get paid depends on how much we can manufacture. The super get paid more than 7 lakhs and leaders were get paid more than 6 lakhs. Those who are being scolded here are us, leaders and supers.

The all super and manager are getting paid just by complaining.

They are unconditionally biased and suppress the sub-ordinates. They flatter the foreigners and dehumanize us. The manager who manage line 1,2,3,4 and 5 is worse. They don’t pressure their friends and relatives but opposite for other workers.

They are pressuring us like something emergency is happening. We can only work overtime until 6:00 pm.

We are too tired and we want to rest on Sunday. But we have to come as we are discriminated if we don’t. The manager harass women if they don’t’ work overtime. We want day off on public holidays.

We are just working for our families.

The stuffs from office and superiors can drink purified drinking water but we drink unpurified one. It cause diarrhea to many workers every time we drink that water.

The township labour office came to investigate but nothing were changed and workers are still working poorly.

We want a certain inspection.

#Information - ETERNAL FASHION CO.LTD garment factory locates at Anawrahta Industrial Zone (behind township labour office, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region. The factory has 3 floors and hires more than 10,000 workers. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing  balabala, SEMIR, CN: L, EUR:M,US:M, EST.1990, MADE INCHINA and mini brand apparels.

The factory use TikTok to recruit with videos of workers receiving attractive salary but the details such as daily wages, overtime wages per hour, benefits and monthly overtime are not mentioned.

By  Ma Ma -Oct 24, 2024

48,000 candidates took EPS TOPIK exam to work at South Korea in manufacturing sector. According to the first list released by the government's foreign employment agency, the number of passed candidates is only (5,540), so onlyone-tenthof them are passed for now.

Currently, there are many people who want to go to work in South Korea, and the passing score was set with a record score of 97.5 out of 100.

“I was calmed as I scored 92.5 in the exam. I though I passed and didn’t worry and now I feel suffocate as the passing score is set to 97.5. I invested my time and money for this exam and expecting so high. I queued in early morning to get a form and I am depressing after I see the passing score,” said an exam candidate.

Some educational institutions have criticized the examination system due to the high passing score.

“Skill test will be tested as well and the passed candidates have to try it. Those who fail can chose weather they want to try again or go to another country. The passing score is not fair. We have to keep an eye on the upcoming situations and currently there are critics upon the exam system,” said a person working in language teaching field.The two governments collaborated to send male workers to work in agriculture, livestock and manufacturing industries in South Korea. Female workers are also being recruited to work in service industries.

South Korea is a country where many Myanmar people want to go and work, and they had to wait all night to pay the exam registration fee.

By Min Ni Kyaw -Oct 24, 2024

Workers from Myanmar Journey bag factory which locates at Watayar Industrial Zone said that the factory calls more than 20 hours overtime per week and they are even forced to sign for overtime agreement during the flood.

“They don’t ask our consents and call overtime until 8:00 pm on weekdays and also force us to sign agreement to work on Sunday,” the workers said.

The normal working hours are from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm and the2022 directive of the Workplace and Labor Law Inspection Department did not allow workers to work more than 20 hours of overtime per week, and the employer had to notify the department one week in advance and obtain approval if the workers were to work more overtime. In addition, employers are instructed to obtain the agreement of the workers in order to call for more overtime time.

“Not only the supervisors but also the manager call overtime. They don’t submit to the department and forced us to sign. We were summoned in the next day if we don’t work overtime and suspended from working normal overtimes. The new workers were forced to sign warning document and dismissed,” a worker said.

Workers are not allowed to take legal leaves and they had to enter the workplace 10 minutes earlier which they see as exploitation.

“We have to came 15 minutes earlier in the morning to attend meeting and we were not allowed to use restroom 15 minutes before the working hours finish. We can’t take any types of leaves and the veteran workers are also dismissed. We can’t take gate pass or go back home if we are sick,” they said.

The all super of the factory is a man and they discriminate the female workers, verbally abuse and intimidate the workers.

“The all super swears the female workers rudely and force us overtime. The rules are complicated and I think it is very unacceptable that we have to sign warning for not finishing the output demands.

Workers feel like inmates as they are monitored for using restrooms and forced to sign warning. The veteran workers are dismissed against the law and day laborers who are assigned the same tasks as permanent stuffs are also dismiss without regulations.

“Day laborers are not appointed for so long and dismissed if they don’t like. The same goes to veteran workers,” a worker explained.

Workers said that they have to submit resignation letter a month in advanced and the factory doesn’t pay the salary if they don’t and the salary can’t be taken by arepresentative person.

“We don’t get the salary if we don’t submit resignation letter. The manager pay the workers by third person for only who are confident with them. We have to come ourselves to get the salary. We don’t get gate pass for emergency or health reasons,” the worker explained about the discriminations.

Workers said that they request to go back as their houses are flooding but the factory denied. Workers are not allowed to take their phones inside the factory to prevent reporting the violations and workers who talk to each other are also forced to sign warnning.

The Myanmar Journey factory located at Road 2, Watayar Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon and owned by a Chinese national.The factory is manufacturing Solo brand bags with more than 300 workforce.

ByHsu Latt Phyu -Oct 23, 2024

Workers from Eternal Fashion garment factory which locates at Anawrahta Road, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region said that the labour office doesn’t take actions on their complaints relating workplace violations.

The violations are forcing overtime on day offs, not giving day off a day in the whole month, verbally abusing for refusing to work overtime, discriminations and intimidations to work overtime.

The factory is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing SEM/R, TOREAD THE WORLD, TOREVD and minibala brands apparels.

It is also said that the factory which is operating with more than 10,000 workers doesn’t have a trade union.

“We are being violated by called overtime on every Sunday and the super verbally abuse us and discriminate us if don’t want to,” said a worker who don’t wanted to be named.

Workers are working overtime until 12:00 am in addition of normal working hours and have to work all night overtime continuously for 4 days without a break time.

Workers are intimidated by their job stability and salary if they want to leave the factory with gate pass. Many workers are suffering from health issues due to mid-night and all-night overtimes every day.

Workers said they were complaint for taking medical leave and thus makes them difficult although it is approved.

Workers report the violations to Department of Labour but there were no changes and actions although the authorities came to investigated.

“The supervisors recruit on online with a attractive salary but workers have to work here like a robot and most of them usually resign before a week. Look how we are suffering from health issues due to excessive overtime. It would be difficult for us if something bad happens to our body,” said a worker.

The unpurified drinking water of the factory also cause the workers diarrhea problems.

“A transportation bus with 45 passenger capacity carried 60 of us and it is dangerous for female to stand and ride. The buses are sufficient in the morning as some workers came on their own plan but it is not convenient in evening but the factory officials are ignoring the risks,” a worker said.

The workers demands in seek of life-work balancing workplace with dignity are–

1.To provide purified drinking water

2.To no call mid-night, all-night and Sunday overtime

3.The supervisors to not force the workers to work overtime

4.To not complaint for taking medical leave

By Hsu Latt Phyu -Oct 20, 2024

Myanmar workers from Fu Cheng Garment factory at Yin Jiang industrial Zone, China said that they are being asked for excessive overtime which they have to work for free until 10:00 pm if they don’t finish the demands; causing them difficulties.

The factory which is owned by a Chinese national manufactures SPYDER ACTIVE warm jackets.

A production line with 25 people are asked for 700 fabrics per hour which leads them to work until 10:00 pm for free.

Workers are also forced to work on Sundays to be able to finish the demands without getting paid. The Myanmar national workers from Fu Cheng garment factory ask assistant from Industrial Workers’ Federation of Myanmar – IWFM regarding the violations.

“The workers are working without taking a break but the supervisors verbally abuse us and workers who can’t bare went back to home country. We are usually forced to work overtime for free without getting paid with the reasons of we don’t finish the demands. In September. we went to the office to told that we will go back to Myanmar and the employer said they would reconsider the fabric output demands and we have to pay compensation to go back to Myanmar,” a worker said.

Workers have to deposit their one month salary which is promised to be return if they resigned but the leave benefits are denied while they are working.

“We don’t get leave here and wages are cut if we miss a day. We don’t know how much is our daily wages. They said we are getting paid according to output quantity. 700,000 mmk is the farthest we can earn. We neither get overtime fee or leave,” a worker explained.

The workers demands are to

1-To ask only for possible fabric output

2-To not force overtime until 9:00 pm for free

3-The supervisors to not verbally abuse the workers

4-To have transparency on wages

By  Hsu Latt Phyu -Oct 19, 2024

Workers from KBL Garment bridesmaid dress manufacturing factory which locates at Industrial Zone 1, Kyansitthar Road, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region said that they are facing difficulties as the factory is forcing them overtime until 11:00 pm.

It is also said that there is no workplace coordination committee in the workplace. The factory is owned by a Chinese nationality and manufactures DAVIDS BRIDAL, Studio, Melissa Sweet, JULES CELO brands bridesmaid dresses.

The working hours are from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm but overtime is from 4:30 pm to 9:00–11:00 pm.

“Overtime were reduced after we complaint for calling overtime until 11:00 pm but they are doing it again. We have to sleep at the factory if we want or go back with our own plan at night. There is no place for us to sleep and we have to sleep near the machines unproperly,” a worker said.

Workers were not provided notice nor informed in advanced about the overtime but they were forced to sign agreement just before the overtime starts.

“The officials intimidate that we would not be allowed to work normal overtime for a week and fined if we tell them that we don’t want to work overtime. All workers don’t want to work overtime until 11:00 but we want to work for normal 2 hours overtime because the daily wage is not sufficient for our families’ expenses. Therefore, they intimidate us with that point,” a worker explained.

Workers were not provided transportation after the overtime and they don’t get enough sleep if they sleep in the factory due to mosquito problems and it leads them to health issues.

“We want them to have sympathy. We can’t afford anything but just social security if we got health issues for working excessive overtimes. Only some people got social security leave,” a female worker explained the difficulties.

Another difficulty of the workers are having to work until 6:30 pm on payday instead of 4:30 pm.

“Workers who told them to let go at 4:30 pm were said that they can go back but salary will be paid on Monday and normal overtime will be forbitten for a week. The pay day was on Saturday and we also have to work overtime on Sunday. We want Sunday as holiday as we have to pay debts and transfer money to house. For now, we don’t have holidays and the working hours are until 11:00 pm. We face mosquito problems whole night and we don’t get enough sleeps. There is workplace coordination committee but they don’t do anything about labour rights and the factory only force us to sign for overtime but don’t consider any of our difficulties,” a worker said.

Workers were complaining for the violations but they were not exposed as the factory owner knows the investigation in advanced and taught workers to lie.

“The worker will be dismissed if they told the truth to the inspectors and we don’t trust the labour officers too. They can’t protect us that leads to this kind of anonymous complaint,” a worker said.

The workers’ demands for a better workplace are–

1.To not force overtime until 9:00, 11:00 pm and to get permit from relevant departments, to allow workers to decide on consents and to provide transportation if they do

2.To pay before 4:30 pm on pay day, to give day off on public holidays

By  Hsu Latt Phyu -Oct 18, 2024

LITA MYANMAR Co, LTD garment factory workers said that each factory workers are cut at least 10,000 kyats for vernation of line managers and supervisors in addition of the labour right violations.

The factory locates at Compound No - , Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone 4, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon region and owned by a Chinese national.

The factory is manufacturing BURTLE, PUNT RPMA, HEARTGREEN, Golden Bear, A DAY IN THE LIFE SENSE OF PLACE brand apparals with more than 1,000 workforces but there is no trade union in the factory.

“They force workers who put Thanakha on their face are forced to remove with a wet tower in the entrance of the factory. Those who complaint are taken photo and issued a warning. They should make a rule if they don’t want workers to put Thanakha in the workplace but removing it with a wet tower is a complete humiliation,” said a worker from the workplace.

All supers are charged 50,000 kyats and workers are charged 10,000 kyats mandatorily for Thadingyut vernation of factory manager and workers are not satisfied with the decision.

The working hours are from 7:30 am to 11:30 am and from 12:00 pm to 4:00 pm and the line manager Daw–and the two assistances are pressurizing the workers to work nonstop without allowing to rest.

“We feel like inmates as soon as we enter the factory. We have to drink water at the shelf and have to pick up the water bottles ourselves. It is difficult of pregnant workers. Workers are inspected like a suspect at the end of the day making us to go back only after 7:00 pm although the working hours end at 6:30 pm,” a worker explained.

The underage workers are hired in the factory without medical certificate and they are hired as adults. Around 60 workers who are hired as day labours are forced to work free on weekends and they are not appointed as permanent stuffs after working for more than 3 months.

“Workers from production lines get paid 30,000 kyats attendance bonus and other workers get paid 20,000 kyats only. The cleaning workers and helpers aren’t paid a kyat. This is a discrimination among the workers who are working each assigned jobs,” a worker stated.

The factory doesn’t provide transportation for weekend overtimes although they forcibly recruit overtimes, making workers to come with their own plans and yet there are verbally abused for missing overtime.

Some workers are hired without employment contract and workers are not provided social security cards although they have contributed around 8 months for it.

Workers are demanding following terms for a secure and violation free workplace.

1.To provide social security card,

2.To not force day laborers for free on weekends

3.To provide employment contracts for workers who doesn’t have it yet

4.To appoint workers with more than 3 months of service as day laborers

5.To provide transportation for overtime

We are workers from Nga Pya Daw Kyaung Street, War Ta Yar Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon region. The factory owner and managers are Chinese nationals. There are other Chinese nationals in the factory. It has been only a few months our factory started to operate but they are violating labour laws.

The Chinese national factory manager and the QC lady dismiss the workers they don’t like without any credentials. There is no compensations and the dismissed workers are mostly Myanmar nationals.

Some women are dismissed as soon as they got pregnant and the QC lady forcibly asked a female worker if they are pregnant in public. It is embarrassed for Myanmar girls and they were dismissed without any valid reasons the next day without compensation.

They are recruiting mandatory overtimes since August and we are intimidated to be dismissed if we don’t work. We have to sign overtime agreements without our consents and we don’t have break time before overtimes. We can have dinner at 8:30 pm but we had to work nonstop since lunch until then.

We are verbally abused and humiliated in public if we can’t work overtime for health reasons and dismissed on the next day.

We also work overtime on holidays and day offs. We work overtime at least on 2 day offs. Currently, we are working everyday and they are calling overtime on October 19 and 20 as well. The factory office stuffs are forcibly charging us for Thadingyut vernation of superiors. All supers are cut 30,000 kyats, supers are cut 20,000 kyats and sub-ordinates are cut 5,000–10,000 kyats mandatorily.

They buy not only gifts for vernation but also jewelries for factory manager and QC lady with the money they charged from us. It is a huge loss for us while we are struggling for our livelihoods in this crisis. We want actions.

Workers from Prettex Myanmar factory said that the factory officials force them to sign to work overtime on Thadingyut holiday (October 16) which is a public holiday.

“The supervisor told us to delay to go back hometown and forcing overtime on holiday,” a worker explained.

Most of the workers came from remote areas and they have planned to go back home in holidays and being forced overtime without consents make them suffer.

Thereis a tradition of returning home on the day of the Thadingyut holidays for vernation of parents and elderlies in Myanmar Buddhist culture. In addition, Section (17) of the 1951 Leave and Working Holiday Act stipulates that employer must obtain the employee's will and request a prior permit from the Department before that day if the employee have to work on public holiday.

“They always complaint the workers but what they are doing is just wrong. Workers don’t have anyone to rely. Tit has been two years this factory is operating but there is no workplace coordination committee. Now they are manipulating the holidays only by their consents,” said a factory worker.

Chapter (2) Section (3) Sub-section (b) of the 2012 Labor Dispute Resolution Law stipulates that a workplace coordination committee must be established within a specified period in accordance with the requirements if there is no labor organization, in the workplace.

By Min Ni Kyaw -Oct 15, 2024

Workers from Jing Yang tile factory which locates at Mya Street, Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township said that they are assigned to task which are not related to the job as soon as the working hours are over.

“We are asked to cut the grass, clean the drainage, fix the roof, remove the rust and algae and female workers have to wash the underwear of the Chinese nationals stuffs of the employer,” they said,

The factory shift the job types without workers consents for not working overtime on Sunday. Jing Ying (Jing Ying Int’l Co.,Ltd ) tile factory is visible on Google Map navigation app as Jing Ying International Building Material Development Co.,Ltd.Workers said they are getting paid lesser than the minimal wage.

“Workers get paid only 150,000 kyats and new workers get paid 200,000 kyats. We don’t get pay raise although we work the same,” a worker said.

It is said that there is no employment contract between employer and employees.Section 5 of the Employment and Skill Development Law, enacted on August 30, 2013 stipulates that "an employer must sign an employment contract within 30 days after appointing an employee to work."

Jing Ying (Jing Ying Int’l Co.,Ltd )pays the salary with the slip that have Arr Mann Thit label and workers have to sign for terms not related to work in August.

Workers said that they have complaint the violations to the Department of Labour Relations.

By Hsu Latt Phyu -Oct 14, 2024

Workers from Chinese national owned BEST GARMENT (LAOS) CO.LTD which locates at Kan 3 region, Vientiane, Laos hires more than 400 Myanmar workers and violating their rights and workers are seeking for help,

It is learnt that workers are seeking help from Industrial Workers’ Federation of Myanmar–IWFM for labour right abuses and dismissing the worker who tells truth about the workplace conditions to the audit.

There is no trade union in the factory and the factory is manufacturing TCHIBO CERTIFIED MERCHANDISE brands apparels.

Myanmar workers were advertised to get paid 250 USD with free rent and meals but got paid only 150 USD in reality.

“They said that the reason we get paid less is because we don’t hit the output demands targets. Supervisors asks 1,400 garment pieces a day for a production with 18 people and we have to work overtime for free until 9:00 pm as well as on Sundays if we don’t finish the demands,” the worker explained.

Workers are only entitled to what the factory allowed and only Laos nationals are allowed to drink cool water but the Myanmar nationals are not.

“They allow us, Myanmar nationals to drink hot water only to prevent us to go restroom rapidly. Workers suffer kidney problems and a worker who had work for 11 months suffering Kidney problem but still working here as they can’t afford compensation to resign,” worker said.

Workers were told they can go back to Myanmar after working for 1 year without compensation and the social security fees will be return with percentage but in reality, workers have to pay compensation for going back to Myanmar for every reasons.

Workers are cut for 150,000 kyats for taking leave a day for any reasons with or without medical and social security certificates. Workers have to contribute more than 800,000 kyats per month.

“There are many difficulties. Employer said social security will be return with percentage if we go back to Myanmar for any reasons including health issues after working for a year although the contract is signed to 3 years. Workers who can’t handle anymore resigned by paying the compensations but the workers who can’t afford are tolerating and continue working,” said a worker who don’t wanted to be named.

The workers who told the truth about the free overtime recruitments and salary doesn’t match with the advertisement on job vacancy were fired.

Workers are requesting the following terms for the sake of a safe and secure workplace

1.To allow the worker with kidney problem to go back to Myanmar

2.To allow Myanmar workers to drink cool water

3.To not cut for social security leave

4.To not recruit free overtime

ByCitizen JournalistsOct 13, 2024

Workers from General Textile garment factory said that they are forced to work substitute on Saturday for Thadingyut Holidays. Furthermore, the factory recruits them overtime until 12:00 am on Sunday and weekdays.

“The pay day 5thday of month was Saturday. We had to work half day on that day for substitute. We have to work mid night overtime on Sundays and weekdays as well,” a worker explained.

It is learnt that workers are allowed to have dinner only for 30 minutes only after working until 6:30 pm. The overtime is non stop from 7:00 pm to 12:00 am and they return home at 4:00 am in the morning.

Workers had to sleep unproperly on the floors and desks at the factory after overtime and they also faced incest problems as the factory turned off lights and fans.

“We don’t get enough sleep after going back home at 4:00 am as we need to comeback on time for the next morning. We all are tired for consecutive mid-night overtimes. We want to rest on Sundays even if the orders are important. They said they will call overtime on October 14 and 15 as well,” a worker explained their difficulties.

Workers said that they are facing health issues due to not getting enough time to rest. The ministry directed to pay 1,000 kyats subsidy in August but the factory delayed for a month.

“We don’t get 30,000 kyats subsidy for August and get paid only in September. Still we don’t get paid for Sundays. We get paid only 26,000 kyats,” a worker said.

On August 1, 2024, the ministry of labour instructed the factories to pay a new 1,000 kyats subsidy starting in the first week of August.

General textile garment factory locates at Inn Lyat Village, Mawbe Township and hires around 700 workers. The factor is owned by a Chinese national and only a WCC is present but there is no trade union.

There are two buildings in the factory’s compound and shares the entrance with the other factory; Hengda garment.

By Hsu Latt Phyu -Oct 12, 2024

Workers from MENGYUE GARMENT Co.,ltd garment factory said that the factory is violating them by asking for excessive fabric outputs and forcing free overtime.

The factory locates at Mya Taung Wun Gyi U Moo Road, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region and manufacturing Japan ordered PALLTEX brands chef outfits, rain coat and long pants with more than 100 workers. It is owned by a Chinese national.

It is said that there is no trade union and a Chinese national man and woman factory managers are directly managing the workers and both of them and the interpreters are verbally abusing the workers making them to feel humiliated in the workplace.

Workers are asked for fabric outputs that lines beyond their productivity such as 30 outfits and 35 pants per hour for each line with 30 workers. They are asked for much more output even if they finish those excessive output by working nonstop.

“They increase the fabric output even if we finish after working nonstop. We can’t finish the new demands they ask so we have to work overtime on Sunday for free nearly every week,” a worker explained.

The factory doesn’t provide sufficient drinking water and forcing underage workers as adults without medical certificates.

Workers are cut for 4,800 kyats daily wages, 4,000 kyats subsidy and 30,000 kyats attendance bonus because of not being allowed to take medical and casual leave.

“There are workplace incidents in this factory. A worker’s hand was cut off as they were hired as packing job but assigned to do snapping. The employer doesn’t take responsibility and accountability,” a worker explained.

Daily wage 6,800 kyats, attendance bonus (2000+2000) kyats and overtime fees 1,400 kyats per hour is advertised as the salary but workers only get paid daily wages 4,800 kyats when they resigned; causing rapid disputes.

Workers are demanding the following terms to become a safe and digit workplace.

1.To allow legal leaves for workers

2.To take responsibility and accountability for workplace injuries

3.To ask only for possible fabric outputs

4.The Chinese national manager to not directly manage the workers

5.The Chinese nationals from employer’s side to not verbally abuse the workers

By Citizen Journalist -Oct 11, 2024

Workers from Textile Palace 2 factory said that their factory gives theirseniorityfees only after three years instead of annually without their consents.

“This system only gives for 2 years even if we reach 3 years. They said the 1 year fee is deposited. They should give annually according to the law. We want our money after a year,” the workers said.

The 1951 Leave and Holiday Act stated that “Factory should provide workers who work for 12 months continuously the average salary or 10 consecutive holidays within the next 12 months.”

The factory hires around 700 workers and located at Industrial Street, Myaung Takar Industrial Zone, Mawbe Township, Yangon region. The workers are having concerns regarding their rights as the factory doesn’t sign the employment contract after working for a year.

“The veteran workers get the employment contract only after 1 year and the new workers haven’t sign after working for nearly 1 year,” they said.

Chapter (3) Section 5 of the Employment and Skill Development Law; Subsection (a)(1) stipulates that an employer must sign an employment agreement (EC) within 30 days of hiring an employee.

Textile Palace 2garment factory is co-owned by Chinese and Myanmar national and workers said the factory is operating under the name of the Myanmar national. The factory manufactures Sinsay, GEMO, Suivez Nous and Trollkids brands apparals.

By Ma Ma -Oct 11, 2024

Workers from Chinese national owned Star Sandar Garment factory said that they are not accessible to leave benefits and day laborers are being discriminated against.

The factory locates at Shwe Kyar Street, Sin Ngue Ward, Inn Sein Township and operating with more than 800 workers. There are around 20 day laborers hired in the factory and the factory is manufacturing Jackets.

“We don’t get casual and medical leaves even for health issues and parents’ funerals. Thus, we lost 40,000 kyats for an absent.

By Min Ni Kyaw -Oct 10, 2024

Workers from at Tainjin Fashion Milestone garment factory said that they are visiting private clinics for health issues because the factory doesn’t provide them social security cards although they contributed monthly for it.

“We paid monthly for social security fees but we don’t get the benefits. The factory denies to provide the social security card by saying that they are being busy,” a worker who doesn’t get the card said.

Pregnant workers are having difficulties for healthcare provisions due to not having social security cards.

A female worker who faced miscarriage in the factory wasn’t provide social security card although they paid for it and allowed only 3 day offs. The social security law stated that 6 weeks leave must be provided for miscarriage but the mentioned worker had to work after a recent miscarriage.

Th pregnant workers are also having difficulties in transportation as they have to stand up in the bus.

“Outsiders are allowed to sit in the front seat and pregnant workers are standing at the back. The all super sit in the front seat in Thadarphyu cars while pregnant women stand at the back. It is not even appropriate to see as a third person,” they said.

Workers said that the factory doesn’t provide employment contract for workers with more than a year of service and workplace coordination committee can’t be asked for help on workplace violations.

“There are many cases where we submit letters to WCC for help but we never get help. WCC never implement assistance for us. We want them to be able to rely,” a female worker stated.

Workers said they want the WCC to be reformed and implement the terms and conditions they negotiated.

Tainjin Fashion Milestone factory locates at the intersection of Seikan Thar and Kannar Road, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township and manufacturing Sinsay, Vero Moda brand apparls with more than 1,400 workers.

Content:
We would like to ask for help.

Around 600-700 workers suffered from laid off at MRTV 4 (Forever Group) media company. The headquarter locates on Pyay Road, in front of Kamayut University TTC school.They also locates at North Dagon Township, Wandameya and Pindaya. Around 800 workers were working at more than 60 departments.

Around 200-300 workers were laid off in May 2024 and their legal compensations are paid separately 3 or 4 times according to their seniority.

The other workers were laid off on 2ndand 3rdJuly. About 300-400 in quantity. Some departments doesn’t have workers any more but only around 3 people including supervisors. The laid off workers had to sign. There are workers from remote townships in laid off list.

They told us to sign as that the compensation will be paid monthly and it is labeled as charity in the contract. I think the company breaks the law that states that compensation should be paid all at once. Media production stuffs are not easy to shift careers quickly and there are lack of employments during this political crisis. Therefore, we seek legal process regarding laid off.

The wages and the charity fees are delayed nearly every month. September wages will be get paid on October 15th. They said employees were not permanently dismissed. They can come and work if there are certain tasks like day workers. The daily wages will be calculated by dividing the last salary with 30. Its workers’ choice to work or not.

Its like we are laid off permanently. Employee cards are taken back. They are still disrespecting the stuffs by not having transparency on the remaining wages and delays.

MRTV 4 covers more than 80 percents of Myanmar’s advertisement. We heard in some events that the profit was in millions of dollars before covid pandemic and coup. Some workers who were laid off during covid are not officially laid off, explained and get paid. Other workers know that they were laid off.

They intimidate us by saying that they are close to the ministry of labour and director team is comfortable with the central government (Nay Pyi Daw).

Stuffs were not paid since Covid pandemic (2020) until 2022. The company summons those who are need and only them get paid. There are stuffs who were dismissed since then. The company rehired the stuffs in 2022 and transferred to new departments without asking workers’ consents or testing their proficiency. Most workers resign after depression due to workplace inconveniences.

We want them to take responsibility and accountability as they are working with world-wide famous companies. We sees as a disrespectful behavior against the workersfor not renewing the employment contract since 2019 and label the compensation as charity fees.

They don’t give us notice in accordance with the law. Workers can’t demand anything due to current situations but we want justice.

By Min Ni Kyaw -Oct 10, 2024

A worker who participated in the protest for transportation fee at Vince Myanmar footwear factory said that the protest started on October 7, 2024 and the negotiations are still being conducted.

“The factory asks workers to pay half of the transportation fee. The drivers asked for 60,000 kyats on October 3, 2024 and the factory asks 40,000 kyats from each worker after pay day. The workers doesn’t have to pay the transportation fee anymore after paying their expenses. The factory said they would front it and will cut for two month fees in the next month and workers are protesting against that,” they said.

The protest took place at the dinning room of the factory and around 200 workers participated except the supervisors and leaders. The negotiations are carried out by both parties and settlement was reached, a worker said.

“We don’t need to pay for September and we have to pay 15,000 kyats each for this month and the factory would pay for the remaining. I heard that the agreement will be signed in witness of the labour office officials tomorrow,” a worker said.

The Vince Myanmar factory locates at Myay Thaing Ward No-166, Compound No-2, South Dagon Township, Yangon region and it is operated by one hundred percent foreign investments according to the information of DICA.

Content:
By Min Ni Kyaw -Oct 10, 2024

We are workers from ETERNAL FASHION CO.LTD garment factory.

The factory calls overtime until 12:00 am starting today (October 7th) and until October 16thfor Thadingyut holidays. There will be no overtimes if we don’t work those overtimes.

It has been 5 months we were working overtime once in two days until 12:00 am. It has been a month we were called every day like that until October 4th.

We have our dinner at 8:30 pm and it’s the only break time we have. We work non-stop since Lunch.

Workers work from Monday to Friday from 8:00 am to 8:10 pm. We don’t get break time except the lunch time.

We only get Sunday day off once in a month for 5 months. It has been only two weeks we don’t work like that and it is because of an investigation.

We finished working at 5:10 pm on Saturdays and 6:10 pm on Sundays.

We suffered from health issues due to working all night overtime nearly every day. The supervisors intimidate with our employment stability if we don’t work overtime. You can check the factory if you doubt what I am saying. The township Labour office visited the factory on October 3.

The inspection took place on HR office. The workers had to answer the inspectors as they were taught by the HR. They can’t tell them the truth. The inspectors didn’t visit the production lines.

I don’t know if they missed or didn’t dare to warn the factory but we are being called late night overtime again.

The factory’s unpurified water cause the drinkers to suffer diarrhea. Workers are only allowed to drink from pipe lines. Only the office stuffs are allowed to drink water from drinking water bottle.

Those who don’t work overtime are treated with malice and held grudges. Those who don’t work on Sunday are not allowed to sew big point fabrics. Therefore, we have to work overtime without consents.

We are cut for vernation to supervisors and managers. Each worker is scut 15,000–20,000 kyats.

The manager ordered to cut and the all super implemented. They cut immediately as soon as after the pay day (October 5th). It is a big amount for the workers and most of us don’t want to pay.

The manager Daw–of line 1,2,3,4,5,6 verbally abuses and cut the workers rapidly.

We rapidly complaint to township labour office and there are no changes from the factory. There is a workplace coordination committee but they do nothing for us.

Information–ETERNAL FASHION CO.LTD factory locates at Anawrahta Industrial Zone (West of the Township labour office) , Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon. The factory is 3 floors and hires around 10,000 workers. The owner is a Chinese national and the factory manufactures balabala, SEMIR, CN: L, EUR:M,US:M, EST.1990, MADE INCHINA and mini brand garments.

The factory use TikTok platform to recruit workers and uploads videos of workers getting paid well but the working hours and overtime were not mentioned.

By Min Ni Kyaw -Oct 09, 2024

It is said that Kingrich Myanmar factory said that workers will not get paid for protesting days and it was written at the report of WCC team’s meeting on October 7.

“Workers asked to get paid for the protesting days and the factory ask the workers to go back to work tomorrow. It is at the negotiating state,” a worker said.

The work stoppage protests began on October 7 and the officials from Labour office, trade union, WCC and factory officials are negotiating on October 9.

“Workers asked for 12,000 kyats per day. They get paid only 7,500 kyats for now. They also asked for other benefits. The factory owner denied by saying that they were already raised in June,” said a female worker.

A worker said that the supervisors are forcing new workers to work by intimidating them.

“All super Daw Ei Ei Win who manage from line 1 to 6 intimidate the workers with less than 3 months of service to work by saying that they will be blacked list in other factories as well. They said we are get paid well and don’t spend wisely,” said a worker.

Kingrich Myanmar garment factory hires nearly 1,400 workers and only 88 workers missed to participated in the work stoppage protestings and most of them are supervisors and leaders.

The factory is owned by a Chinese national and located at Yay Pyar Bus-Stop, Than Chat Wun U Nyunt Road, Industrial Zone 2, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon region.

By Labour Citizen Journalist -Oct 06, 2024

Workers from Myanmar York factory said that their request for an increase in attendance bonus due to raising commodity prices was denied by the factory officials.

“We want a salary that is inline with the commodity prices. We submit suggestion letters via the letter box and we processed via WCC,” said a worker.

Workers were criticized that they frequently asked for pay raise although the WCC member doesn’t ask for them. The factory replied their requests by a notice saying that wages can be raised only if the authorities directed to.

“We get paid only 20,000 kyats attendance bonus per month. Other garment factories pay 30,000, 40,000 and 50,000 kyats. It has been so long that we get paid this amount and we are asking for a total of 50,000 kyats,” a factory worker explained.

It is said that there are many workers who resigned due to insufficient wages and benefits. And the supervisors are also discriminating the workers.

“The supervisors biased in raising the grade bonus. Only those who are confident with them are raised but the ones who are really proficient, hit the target and handle big points are not. We don’t get paid as expect as due to these discriminations although we work the same. Workers with higher grade level receives more fabric fees. Supervisors get 6 times more than workers. They take all the benefits while forcing workers to hit the target. We only get the marginal wages,” said a worker.

Almost every supervisors from all departments are practicing biasing and discriminations in the factory which cause a loss for the workers.

“We don’t get leave for education and other reasons if we are not close to supervisors. They told HR doesn’t approve but those who are close to them get unpaid leave preventing their loss of length of service. We don’t get length of service as we don’t get unpaid leave and become like a new worker,” workers stated.

Myanmar York factory locates at Kyan Sitthar Road, Industrial Zone 4, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region and operating with more than 1,600 workers.

By Yoon Sat -Oct 06, 2024

Garment factory workers said that they are being recruited substitute overtimes for Thadingyut Holidays

“Its substitute overtimes for Thadingyut Holidays. They cut us by hours for holidays. They cut half of Saturday with hourly rate. 8 hours for two Saturday. 8 hours is counted as one working day. They don’t negotiate and we lost overtime fees. We doesn’t get double. But workers don’t dare to complaint. Another factory are doing the same as well. Workers want casual leave during the end of the year but being afraid ask. We lost all our bonuses if we don’t work overtime on Saturday’s half-day,” said a worker.

Workers are required to work substitute overtime for a half day on every Saturday in order to prevent fabric orders delay as there were 5 consecutive holidays in Thadingyut including 3 government holiday and a weekend.

“Our factory doesn’t call us yet. I heard that some factories are calling. Some paid for overtime but some don’t. Our factory doesn’t have much orders so they don’t call it yet,” said a garment factory worker.

Workers said that they were sometime not paid for substitute overtimes and not paid double for Sunday overtime. They are also cut for fabric bonuses, grade bonuses and attendance bonus if they missed the overtime.

The Thadingyut holiday is from 16thto 18thOctober and workers are having difficulties to go back to hometowns due to theterritorial instability

By Ma Ma -Oct 04, 2024

Day laborers from Chinese national owned Sunrise Myanmar Fashion garment factory said that they are being violated and not appointed as permanent stuffs although working for more than 3 months or in 6 months.

The factory is located at Kyauk Sein Road, Thardukan Industrial Zone 4, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon region and manufacturing Recycle and CLOSSHI Biz brand apparals.

“The working hours are from 8:00 am to 7:00 pm and the wages are paid weekly. They said that we will get paid 8,200 kyats per day and other benefits but get paid only 5,600 kyats per day. We work from Monday to Saturday and we don’t get paid wages for the half of Saturday. We don’t get paid for Sunday day off as we are labeled as day laborers. We get paid 1,400 kyats overtime per hour on weekdays. Permanent workers get paid 8,200 kyats daily wages, attendance bonus, subsidy and 1,800 kyats overtime per hour. We are working for more than 3 months but not yet appointed as permanent,” said a worker.

There are around 60 day laborers hired in the factory and they are losing monthly wages rights, leave benefits and subsidies.

“We are working the same tasks with other workers but we don’t get paid in salary slip. Our names are just written on a paper and asked to sign. We should be get paid the same wages and allowed other benefits as others but not yet until now. There is a workplace coordination committee appointed by the employer but they don’t resolve the issues related to labour rights and they are biased towards the employer,” said a day laborer who suffered.

Sunrise Myanmar Fashiongarment factory day laborers are demanding 8,200 kyats daily wages for all workers, to appoint day laborers as permanent stuffs after working for 3 months, to pay the remaining half day wages of Saturdays of day laborers with back date calculation, to allow paid off day on Sunday and public holidays and to pay the day laborers by salary slip.

By Yoon Sat -Oct 04, 2024

It is learnt that workers from Golden Colour Fashion (Myanmar) garment factory which located at Industrial Zone 3, Mya Taung Wun Gyi U Mo Street, Insein Township, Yangon region didn’t get the pay raise the employer informed them in advanced.

“According to my knowledges, we were told that we will get pay raise in September and we will get paid 11,000 kyats per day including the subsidy. Workers are demanding for it after they didn’t get paid on this paid day. It was said since August,” said a person who is close to the workers.

The pay raised which covers 2,000 kyats subsidy and 11,000 kyats daily wages was promised in the meeting with all super and workers which was held on August 15. The all super even promised to raise the overtime fees.

It was said 30,000 kyats attendance bonus, 11,000 kyats daily wages, 3,300 kyats expert fees, daily fabric fee and annual fees would be cut for an absent. The workers had to finish the workloads which require 8 hours within 6 hours, searched strictly by the securities and allowed to use restrooms only by the card.

Workers tolerated the tightened rules due to the hope of pay raise but their expectations became false when the supervisor told them on October 3 which was 2 days before pay day that they would not get paid as promised.

“You will get paid 6,800 kyats. Complaint anywhere and we will resolve. We don’t afraid to be get arrested. If you satisfy, accept what u get paid and then continue to work and if not resign,” the super citied the words of the employer.

Workers submitted letter to workplace coordination committee regarding the employer’s failure to keep their words and workers are demanding the rights of negotiations as the employer didn’t allow them to discuss yet.

The STUM said that Golden Colour Fashion (Myanmar)actions which included exploitation, promising false incentive and labour right violations will be recorded and found justice.

The factory which is manufacturing KAPPA, MEDICINE and KoToN brand apparals is continuously violating overtime recruitments limits, rights to form associations and discriminating

It is said that the military enumerate male workers list at He MeT company Limited garment factory which located at Twinathin Tike Wun U Htun Nyo Street, Hlaing Thar Yar Township o October 2.

There are more than 200 male workers in the factory which manufactures sinsay and OUTDOOR brand apparels.

“Around 25 soldiers entered the factory and enumerate male workers list. According to my knowledges it is for conscription. The employer gave the list and they told that they will come back on September 13. We are worried. We are not sure weather we should continue to work or rest,” said a male worker.

Most workers fled the workplace after the military conscription rule was implementd but the enumeration began when the workplaces return to normal.

“We are really worried. According to the news even night our and going to some restaurants is dangerous. I heard that we will be dragged. We don’t know what to do in this situation. Our families would call us back if they heard the news. I am thinking that I should decide something according to the potential situation,” a garment worker stated.

The military council has been restricting young people between the ages of 18 and 35 in various ways since the implementation of the military service law in the country. In most of the factories, young people over the age of 20 are hired.

The Junta is setting up policies in townships and charging the tricycle taxi drivers frequently.

By Ma Ma -Oct 01, 2024

Workers from Myanmar Zhi Xin Garment Co.Ltd said that the factory is violating the labour laws and they are being threatened to be sued if they complaint.

The factory is owned by a South Korean national and located at Papae Gaung Maung Khet Street, Hlaing Thar Yar Township and manufacturing Jackfield Original, CUTTER&BUCK, ODV and Jack Field brand apprals with more than 1,200 workers.

“They dismissed without moral and legal reasons. The working hours are from 7:00 am to 6:00 pm but we have to work overtime until 9:00 pm. The expert fees are cut if we don’t work overtime. We don’t get day off on Sundays. We get paid 1,000 kyats subsidy more but the other expert fees are cut. A2+ expert level workers get paid 180,000 kyats before but only get paid 120,000 kyats for now as the subsidy is raised 1,000 kyats. They said we can leave if we are not satisfied with the decision. In addition, we don’t also get legal leaves here,” said a factory worker.

More than 100 day laborers are hired and they are not appointed as permanent stuffs even after working for 3 months. They are working 10 hours a day but get paid only 8,000 kyats per day and only 6,000 kyats on Saturday. They don’t get paid for Sunday day off.

There is a work place coordination committee in the workplace but failed to protect the workers from manager’s verbal abuses. The factory threatened that those who complaint regarding those issues will be sued.

“A production line was transferred to the upper floor today. The leader informed the manager Daw Thandar Aung about the workplace odors but they verbally abused us and dismissed that line leader. The employer illegally dismissed workers whom are not confident with them. The manager and Chinese interpreters are the ones who verbally abuse us. A whole production line demanded for resolvent by stop working after their leader was dismissed without committing any mistakes,” said a worker.

Workers from Myanmar Zhi Xin Garment co.ltdare hoping to get legal labour rights, to not cut the current wages to get paid 1,000 kyats subsidy more, to not dismissed illegally, to give day offs on Sundays, the manager to not verbally abuse, to appoint day laborers with more than 3 months of service as permanent stuffs and to give full wages to day laborers.

By Yoon Sat -Oct 01, 2024

U Thaung Han, who was illegally fired from the Pepsi soft drink factory, refuted the factory's allegations during the (33rd) hearing on September 30th.

U Thaung Han worked at theLOTTE MGS Beverage (Myanmar) Co., Ltd (LotteMGS)’s manufacturing factory which located at Yangon–Pyi Street, Mawbe Township worked as a S1 senior electrician for 8 years. The factory dismissed him with the reason of saying not being present during important guest’s visit.

U Thaung Han, a worker at the Pepsi soft drink factory, was dismissed illegally against the employment contract on October 31, 2022 (31) and negotiations were carried out. As no settlement was reached, the Ministry of Labor instructed to file a lawsuit only in mid-March 2023, so the lawsuit began.

The factory’s lawyers asked U Thaung Han about the fact that they are warned before dismissal and dismissed in the witness of the WCC team as U Thaung Han refused to repair a cooler machine.

U Thaung Han said that there is no warning and the factory hired the exterior mechanics as the machine is expensive and they don’t refuse to repair and one member of the WCC was not present so it is legally not valid to say that he was dismissed in the witness of the WCC.

Currently, the (34th) trial date has been rescheduled on October (14th) at 12:00 pm. STUM stated that Pepsi failed to protect workers’ right although being internationally famous brand and still using the strategy to extend the trail sessions until the employer can’t afford more.

The Pepsi factory is owned by LOTTE MGS Beverage (Myanmar) Co., Ltd. and Myanmar Golden Beverage Co., Ltd (MGS)company and Lotte Chilsung Beverage Co., Ltd of Lottee group of South Korea collaborated since 2013-14 to manufacture Pepsi, 7Up, Mirinda, Mountain Dew and Sting softdrinks with the name of Lotte MGS.

There is a campaign to international customers to boycott Pepsi as the factory dismissed a worker who worked for 20 years without compensation and dismissed the sales in the same way without compensation on the grounds that they don’t hit the target.

By Labour Citizen Journalist -Sep 30, 2024

Workers said that Hlaing Thar Yar Township labour office failed to address and take actions to labour right violating issues they complaints.

“I reported to the western office. But they don’t accept the letters and told us that they will call our factory,” said a worker who is dismissed.

Workers said that they are being exploited, physically assaulted, recruited overtime which exceeds than the legal limit, sexually harassed and violated labour rights.

“We once complaint to the western township labour office. But the officers only told us that we are wrong although they are knowing that the employers are violating,” said a worker.

Workers said that their complaints doesn’t matter although labour right violations are occurring day by day. This fact makes the workers lose their trust on labour authorities.

“We are working overtime more than 40 hours a week and we are verbally abused and dismissed if we refused to. When we report to the authorities, the information of reporters are informed to the factory even before we arrived back home. The factory is already planned to dismissed us. That’s how realiable and trustworthy the labour offices are,” said a worker who was dismissed from their job.

A labour activist said that the labour offices buy times and inform the factory about the details of the reporters.

“They told to address the problem via WCC but WCC never worked. The worker remained status quo and the factory official doesn’t resolve. The workers are transferred and when they complaint another case its delayed again. Workers can’t survive in the workplace during this crisis,” they said.

Workers are also suffering from mental anxieties due to labour offices failure and delays to address the violations.

Workers said that similar case also happened at the Hlaing Thar Yar Eastern labour offices and the employers they fear are actually the superiors of the labour authorities.

By Ma Ma -Sep 30, 2024

Workers from ETERNAL FASHION CO.LTDgarment factory said that the factory calls them until 12:00 am and all-night overtime on some days with heavy workloads which cause accidental deaths as a consequence.

The factory is owned by a Chinese national and located at Hlaing Thar Yar Township. Around 10,000 workers are hired and Japanese ordered brands such asbalabala, SEMIR, CN: L, EUR:M,US:M, EST.1990, MADE INCHINA and mini are manufactured here.

“The factory is three floors. There is a total of 10,000 workers working here although working hours varies. The main problem is calling overtime until 12:00 am and sometimes until dawn. We don’t get day offs on Sundays. We have to sleep with our own plans inside the factory. A ferry pick up us at 5:00 am to go back to house and come back on time for the next day. Those who don’t work overtime are treated poorly. We also have to work until 12:00 am from September 26 to October 15 as the Japanese order deadline is on October 15,” a worker explained.

“Workers are suffering hallucinations, workplace injuries and being weak due to excessive overtime. Some workers died from felling from the car,” said a factory worker.

There is no trade union in the factory but only a workplace coordination committee the employer appoint on their consents.

The activists from job applicants are pressurized to resign.

“The supervisors verbally abuse us to get the fabric outputs. There is dispensary and nurse but no medicine in our factory. There is water purifier but the drinking water is rusted and not purified. It also have mud odors. We are tired and suffering from excessive heat. Unpurified water is a concern for health. We need to inform a day in advanced for casual leave. We can’t take leave by phone. Medical leave is permitted but it is not easy,” a worker explained.

Workers are seeking for the factory to call overtime only after surveying them, to provide large drinking water bottle, to allow legal leaves, to eliminate pressurizing the labour activists, to take actions on verbal abuses and to hires a doctor and provide medicine in the factory.

By Ma Ma -Sep 30, 2024

MYANMAR SINYOUNG FASHION CLOTHES garment Factory workers said that the employer is violating than before after ministry’s cosmetic investigation of excessive overtime issues and failure to take actions.

The factory is owned by a Chinese national and located at Yangon-Pathein Road, Asugyi Ward, Htantapin Township, Yangon region and hires more than 500 workers including child laborers and day laborers.

“The working hours are from 8:00 am to 7:30 pm. But we are working until 9:00 pm due to excessive fabric orders. We are very tired and want to rest early on some days but we can’t. We are forced and pressurized. Those who don’t work overtime are discriminated against. We reported to the labour office for excessive overtime recruitment but it just got worse after their investigation,” said a worker.

The factory manufactures Sinsay brand pants and workers are cut for 4,800 kyats daily wages, 2,000 kyats subsidy, 1,000 kyats meal allowance and 30,000 kyats attendance bonus. Child laborers are forced the same as adults and more than 60 day laborers are hired. Day laborers with more than 3 months of service are not appointed as permanent stuffs.

“Workers are asked for excessive fabric outputs that exceeds than their productivity. A cavity with 45 people including clerk, seamstresses, helper and supervisors are asked for 50 good quality garments per hour. We are working nonstop but the supervisors verbally abuse us if we don’t finish the demanded outputs. There is no one who will stand for us and we can’t complaint,” said a seamstress.

Workers are having difficulties as the information of the worker who complaint to labour office is informed to the employer back. Workers are seeking for the employer to ask only for possible fabric output, to not assign child laborers the same tasks with adults, to provide maintenance for the restrooms and to allow legal leaves.

To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

By Yoon Sat -Sep 30, 2024

According to the workers and activists it is learnt that more than 400 workers are being violated at Bohua Fashion garment factory which located at Bamaw Atwin Wun Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region.

The Chinese national owned factory is manufacturing mimibala, SEM/R, TOREVD and TOREAD THE WORLD brand apparels with more than 400 workforces. There is no trade union in the factory.

More than 400 workers at the factory are having difficulties of not having enough spaces, emergency exist, sufficient dinning place and employment contracts. Only veteran workers have employment contract but the employer didn’t give them a copy. There are only four gender classified restrooms and they are not sanitary and there is no dispensary and medicines in the factory.

Around 100 day laborers are hired and some of them are not appointed as permanentstuffs even after working for nearly 2 years. Those workers are dismissed illegally when the employer don’t need them and rehired as new workers.

“Almost every worker at snap, iron and packing departments are day laborers. Underage workers usually sick after working unfair tasks with their ages,” said a worker.

A production line with 45 people are asked for 40 garments per hour which exceeds than their productivity. The demanded garments are also difficult to make but the Chinese national lady verbally abuse the workers if the demands are not finished.

Workers have to work from 8:00 am to 9:00 pm although the official working hours are from 8:00 am to 6:30 pm according to job vacancy. Workers are working from 4 to 5 hours of overtime per day while the HR is suppressing them in order of their job stability.

The manufacturing brands are ordered by other factories and workers said that they witnessed factory’s officials said that “We don’t care about being reported. We are doing business here because we don’t fear anyone.”

The workers’ demands are–

1.To ask only for possible fabric outputs

2.The Chinese national factory manager lady to not verbally abuse them for not finishing the employer’s output demands

3.To not force overtime until 9:00 p,.

4.To provide maintenance for the restrooms

5.To give a copy of employment contracts to them

6.To appoint workers with more than 1 year of service as permanent stuffs

7.To provide medicines in the factory

To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

By Hsu Latt Phyu -Sep 30, 2024

Myanmar migrant workers who are working at Chinese national owned EST GARMENT (LAOS) CO.LTDgarment factory at 3 Kan area, Vientiane, Laos said that the factory asks for excessive fabric outputs and supervisors are the threating them to be physically violated and cut if they can’t finish the outputs and the salaries are not paid as advertised. Some workers also resigned by paying the compensation due to labour right violations.

The factory hires more than 400 and manufactures TCHIBO CERTIFIED MERCHANDISE brand apparels.According to the workers there are no trade union in the factory.

The factory advertised Myanmar migrant workers that they will get paid from 220–250 USD per month but in reality, they don’t get paid that much while working from 7:30 am to 7:30 pm.

“They advertised that we will get paid 220–250 USD but we don’t actually get paid,” said worker.

A production line with 18 workers are asked for 1,400 garment unit outputs per day.

“The supervisors especially the all super of line 15 threaten us that we will be physically assaulted and would not get paid if we don’t work overtime. We have to work free overtime on Sunday to finish the output demands. The supervisors are Myanmar nationals and they pressurize us so much,” said a worker.

Workers said that there is no expert fees in the factory and they are given in fixed wages but the salary varies from one month to other.

“The working hours are excessive. We only get 11 lakhs maximum. We don’t get paid daily wages if we don’t finish the daily demands. And salary is cut at the end of the month by saying that we failed to reach the target. No matter how hard we try, it just can’t finish,” said a Myanmar garment worker.

Workers are allowed to drink only a little water and Myanmar nationals areonly allowed to drink hot water to not rapidly go to toilet.

“Only Laotians are allowed to drink cool water and Myanmar nationals have to drink hot water. The mobile phones are confiscated during working hours. A worker asked for break time to talk and heal due after their father passed away but they are no allowed to take until evening. There is no labour rights here,” a worker said.

Workers explained that there are some workers who resigned by paying the compensation due to discrimination and excessive fabric demands. Only those who can’t afford compensation are continuing to work and workers seek help from Industrial Workers’ Federation of Myanmar–IWFM.

“An audit will come to the factory this month and we are taught to tell them that we get paid 240 USD per month. This factory have a sub-factory in Myanmar called BEST WIN which located at Shwe Pyi Thar Township.

The migrant workers working are seeking for resolvent and their demands are–

1.To pay salary as advertised

2.To ask only for possible fabric outputs

3.To not recruit overtime without paying

4.The line 16 all super to not threatens the workers with physical assault and cutting the wages

5.To not discriminate the Myanmar workers for drinking water.

To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

By Hsu Latt Phyu -Sep 27, 2024

Workers from Ten Da Garment factory said that they are being dismissed illegally, asked for excessive fabric outputs, taken photo of female workers without permission.

The factory locates at Watmasut Wunhtauk Street, Industrial Zone 4, Eastern Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region and operating with more than 500 workers.

The factory which is owned by a Chinese national is manufacturing LCW VISION, SANIA CATALINA, MO WOMAN, Defacto, CLOSSHI, mwr and RESERVED brands apparals and there is no trade union in the labour rights violating factory.

“Items and machines are kept at the dinning room. There is also no enough chairs so we are having difficulties for dinning. There are 13 restrooms but only 2 are assessable and both of them can’t lock. The door only covers the face and the lower part is visible. It is very uncomfortable for female workers,” a woman worker said.

Workers are asking resolvent from the employer regarding to the fact that the Chinese national technicians taking photos of young and pretty female workers without permission as well as those who are not comfortable with them and intimidating them that they will be blacklisted from applying to other factories.

The working hours are from 8:00 am to 7:30 pm excluding dinning hours and from 8:30 pm as overtimes and workers have to work until 6:30 on Saturday which actually has to be half day only.

Workers get paid 4,800 kyats daily wages, 2,000 kyats daily subsidy, 30,000 kyats for B level, 20,000 kyats for C level and 10,000 kyats for D level as expert fees and 10,000 kyats attendance bonus.

“We are cut attendance bonus and expert fees for arriving to work 5 minutes late. The attendance bonus is also cut for taking 2 days of legal leaves. 1 month expert fee is cut for taking gate pass. We lost so much for a day of absent in the whole month,” said a worker from the workplace.

The workplace are being managed directly by Chinese national technicians and workers are assigned to departments and lines in need instead of their native department only. Those who don’t work at assigned place have to sign warning and commitment papers.

A production line with 25 to 30 workers are asked for 50 to 80 garment outputs per hour and the supervisors are verbally abusing the workers for not finishing the demands.

“Supervisors and leaders curse us rudely in the production lines,” a worker stated.

The employer calls for mid-night and all-night overtime on the grounds of important orders and those overtime are forced mandatorily.

“There are day laborers in the factory. Day laborers who have less than 6 months of length of service are dismissed with a notice if they don’t work the overtime. Those who complaint are also pressurized and dismissed,” said a male worker.

Workers with less than 3 months service are dismissed without valid reason if they don’t work overtime and go back home with gate pass. Those who have more than 3 months of service are not allowed to take overtime. Workers who reported to the labour offices regarding the overtime are discriminated by the employer by not giving overtime hours in the following months and pressurized to resign.

“There is a suggestion letter box in the factory but no one read our letters. The employer said that the box is kept as cosmetic to be in accordance with the law and there is no time to read our letters. The factory has been opened for more than 2 years and there is no workplace coordination committee in a factory with 500 workers,” said a worker.

Workers are asking for the following terms and conditions regarding to workplace violations and their demands are–

1.To survey the workers consents for mid-night and all-night overtimes

2.The supervisors to not verbally abuse the workers

3.To provide sufficient dinning place and chairs

4.To not allow the foreigner technicians to manage the workplace directly

5.To not asked for excessive fabric outputs

6.To provide maintenance for the toilets.

7.To resolve the fact that Chinese nationals taking photos of female workers without permission

8.To not dismiss the workers with less than 6 months of service for not working overtime

To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.
