Content: It is reported that the Thai government has approved the issuance of a pink card for document of residency for foreign workers, including illegal Myanmar workers, to live and work as legal workers in Thailand. "Yes. It has been approved. It was submitted to the Thai government by the Thai Ministry of Labor, and the Thai government approved it. The approval has been received. There is no exact date when the process will start. The starting date and the cost will be announced later," said a person based in Thailand assisting Myanmar workers in Thailand. The Thai Ministry of Labor submitted a request to the Thai government to issue a pink card for foreign workers including Myanmar, Vietnam, Lao and Cambodia nationals to become legal workers to live and work at Thailand. Thai Labor Minister and officials from various relevant departments met and discussed, and it was decided that foreign workers living and working illegally in Thailand would be issued legal residence permit, pink card as a document for residence. The Thai Labor Minister said that this decision was made to make it convenient for the Myanmar nationals who entered Thailand illegally due to the political situation in Myanmar and the expired MoU workers who have difficulty returning home due to various reasons. In addition, foreign workers including Myanmar, whose work permit will expire on February 13 2025, will be allowed to extend it for two (2) years, and if that period expires, they will be extended another two (2) years just like MoU workers, according to the statement. In addition, workers who work in the Thai-Myanmar border areas with blue Border Pass books will be allowed to stay and work for 6 months, while previously they were allowed to stay and work for 3 months. Content: The Myanmar Embassy in Singapore has announced that the renewal of passports for Myanmar nationals in Singapore will be accepted from 9:30 am to 2:00 pm on Monday, a public holiday on June 23.   They said that about 120 Myanmar citizens are regularly provided with passport renewal through 75 online appointments and 45 WhatsApp appointments every day. Due to the difficulty of getting an online appointment from the embassy website and working day off conditions, there are now many Myanmar nationals waiting to renew their passports in Singapore. Therefore, approximately 200 Myanmar nationals (passport expiration date until August 31, 2025) will receive a special program to renew their passports between 9:30 a.m. and 2:00 p.m., a government holiday on June 23 (Sunday). Content: Starting from June 1, after Thailand eased the visa policies and released a list of more than 90 countries that will be allowed to stay for 60 days without visas, but neighboring Myanmar is not included in the list, according to the Thai government. "Thailand and Myanmar are neighboring countries, but due to the political situation in their country, they are worried about asylum and they do not allow Myanmar nationals to get a 60-day visa waiver. If the head of a household is bad, the children are affected, just as rulers and citizens," said a Myanmar national in Thailand. Thailand's neighboring countries such as Laos, Cambodia, Malaysia, and other Southeast Asian countries such as the Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam, Brunei, Indonesia included in the 60-day visa exemption list but Myanmar nationals will continue to be allowed to stay in Thailand only for 14 days without the need for an entry visa as before. Content: The Royal Thai embassy in Yangon announced on June 5 that it is possible to apply for a migrant worker visa at the embassy. Migrant worker visas (Non-LA Visa) can be applied for at a rate of 400 people per day, and MOU companies that transport legal workers abroad can only apply after booking via the website. The visa application process will take about three business days, and the embassy has informed that those who will apply for a visa should follow the established rules. The things to be followed that are advised are to book through the embassy's website, to apply for a visa at the embassy according to the appointment received, to check the correctness of the personal information on the visa page and to purchase the air ticket only if it is correct after receiving the applied visa. Since the MOU is valid for 90 days from the date of receiving the visa, the MOU companies can make other preparations needed to leave during that time. In addition, the Thai Immigration Department has granted migrant worker visas a residence permit of two (2) years from the date of entry without additional fees, and informed that the embassy will not be responsible for solving any subsequent problems caused by their needs and carelessness. MOU workers were sent to Thailand from Myawaddy to Mae Sot or Kawthaung to Ranong by car, and from April 29, 2024, it was sent by flight from Yangon Airport to Don Maung Airport. Content: According to the agency community, foreign employment agencies are having difficulty finding workers due to the age limit for domestic men to go abroad to work. Men between the ages of 23 and 31 are prohibited from working abroad, so it is said that the search for workers for overseas employment is taking longer than before and is being scrutinized. “Previously, the labor force is full if the demand for jobs was correct and, and it doesn't take long to find a worker. It's convenient. Now, the age limit set by the government is the age that entrepreneurs from other countries want to hire. But now, we have to remove those ages. If they are around four or five months over 22, the ministry will not allow us to sign a contract, so the workers who want to go will not be able to go, and the agency will not be able to call them. It is difficult," said an official from a licensed agency that transports workers abroad. It is said that some job postings have increased the age of around 40 due to restrictions on the right of men to work abroad at the moment. Due to the restrictions on foreign workers, young people are leaving the country in various ways, and arrests are also on the rise. "In the past, most of the job invitations were only up to the age of 35, and the entrepreneurs didn't like the older ones very much. Now, we see a lot of vacancies accepting up to the age of 40. What's going on now is that young people between the ages of 23 and 31 don't know what to do. Some of them went illegally. This age restriction is like forcing them to go to foreign countries to work illegally," said a person close to the agency community. Currently, there are more and more people traveling illegally to work in foreign countries, and the amount of money paid to brokers to travel is also increasing. Content: The Chinese national owned Popular Garment factory which located at Phan Chat Wun U Shwe Oo Street, Industrial Zone 2, Hlaing Thar Yar Township has been operating for more than 20 years, and in 2021, the factory opened another factory called Beaume International Garment under the same roof.  Currently, there are only more than 70 workers left in Popular Garment factory as more than 400 workers were resigned last month. 32 workers who demanded to be separated the workers and to clarify their seniority were dismissed. Among those 32 with more than 20 female workers, most of them are around 20 years old. The worker said that now only 70 of the senior workers are left. The worker said that the factory only use Beaume International Garment label in recruiting for new employees. “They said there is a change in owner but said its not again when we resolved. On May 20, Popular workers’ length of service since 2021 are added in the Beaume so we want them to clarify where did the past 20 years of service went,” said a worker. They can’t answer our questions upon the lost services, so it is evident that the same factory has 2 owners, 2 factory names, and two WCC groups, and there has been no change in the employment agreement and the name of the applicant for the workshop operating. On May 20, 2024, more than 70 Popular workers are layoff-ed on the grounds of not having sufficient orders and they were only given 4,800 kyats daily wages and 1,000 kyats stipend. “On the day of the return to work, the workers were not allowed to enter the workplace and was resisted by security personnels, and they called the military by acting like workers were violating. It have been more than 4 times workers tried to resolve together with military, wardens and administration. It seems like they want to cancel the workers’ length of service at the Popular factory. We want this issue to be resolved. More workers are resigning, only 70 people left now,” said a worker who don’t want to be named.  It is also known that 885 workers protested to raise the daily wages to 5,600 kyats in June 2023. The factory is manufacturing NORTHLAND and Multiblu brand apparels. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: The skyrocketing price of goods in Myanmar has become obvious these days, and the price of rice, which is a staple food in the country, has been raising in multiples within the country. In this situation, despite the fact that some basic people are consuming coarse rice which is cheaper than rice as a substitute, the relevant Myanmar Rice and Rice Association is planning to export 135,920 tons of rice this month as a way to earn foreign currency. Currently, in the domestic rice market, the price of refined rice has risen to 8,500 kyats as the highest price, and the lowest price of coarse rice is up to 3,000 kyats. Therefore, the price of rice has increased by 1,000 kyats to 15,000 kyats compared to the beginning of last May. The rising price of rice is also difficult for people. Now, it's not only rice, but other consumer goods are raising as well. The only thing that doesn't follow is the salary, so the people who were comfortable before are also tight. From the beginning, life is worse for basic class. People rushed to buy the rice that was sold to feed the ducks and chickens in a rice mill. They are even thanking for selling them with 3,000 kyats per pyi (2.24kg)," said a rice trader. According to the press release of the Myanmar Rice Association and exporters, the status of foreign rice exports in the fiscal year 2024-2025 is 2.5 million tons of refined and coarse rice and there are eight ships docked at eight international ports to export rice abroad. 12,500 tons of rice from Ahlone International Port, 12,500 tons of rice from Yangon International Port, 10,000 tons of rice from Bo Aung Kyaw Port, 9800 tons of rice at Wilmar port, 91120 tons of rice from Sule Port; a total of 135920 tons of rice will be exported this month. In addition, it is known that 4 more ships will arrive to export 74,000 tons of rice to international ports in the near future. Content: Buyers say that the price of palm oil sold outside retail is as high as 12,000 kyats per peik thar (1.63kg). The current price has continued to rise from the price of 7,000 kyats per peik thar (1.63kg) in Thingyan (April). Currently, palm oil is difficult to purchase and there are reports that there is a shortage. The people said that the fuel cards that are taken out with the quota are not available regularly. “I had to pay 1,200 kyats for 10 kyat thar (0.163kg). I have to go to market as it is not available in the nearby family shop,” said a palm oil buyer on June 5. The palm oil which is the essential kitchen product is sold by quota and the official price is still below 6,000 kyats. “We can buy twice a week before but since the last week it become just one time per week. We haven’t bought for this week. I heard there is a palm oil shortage and it is not convenient for us to buy with 12,000 kyats per peik thar,” said a house wife. Palm oil is allowed to be purchased at the rate of 50 kyat thars per household. The warden issue oil cards and people receive the cards every week in some neighborhoods but most of them do not have enough. “They casually investigated with civilian dress. A shopkeeper was found selling palm oil and the whole market have to sign to not sell it again. They sent those who sell again will be prisoned and the shop will be sealed,” said a shopkeeper who is running a shop in the municipal market. The official palm oil price is 5,345 kyats per peik thar but the outside price is costing more than two times of it. Content: Workers from Tianjin Fashion Milestone Garment factory said that they are working 3 hours of overtime a day after 8 working hours and also forced to work overtime on Sundays as wells. The Chinese owned factory is located on Seik Kan Thar Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township and operating with more than 1,100 workers. Although there were more than 1,300 workers in the workplace in the past, they had to regularly work overtime for up to 3 and a half hours a day, and on Sundays as well. Those tired workers who were not allowed to rest resigned from job. “The working hours are from 7:30 am to 7:30 pm and the lunch time is from 11:30 am to 12:00 pm. WE work continuously from 12:00 am to 7:30 pm and the employer doesn’t allow us to take a break although we are requesting. A cavity with 55 people including supervisors and helpers are asked 35 jackets per hour and the super verbally abuse if we can’t finish. We have to work without having lunch to finish. We are cut from 500 kyats to 1,000 kyats for quality failed fabrics. Even if we finish after working every minute, they still exploit our bonus or discriminate,” said a worker who don’t want to be named.  The factory doesn’t have a trade union and they are manufacturing VERO MOODA, Sinsay and LCWAIKIKI brands apparels. There is a workplace coordination committee but can’t help any issues as they are only formed by the selected workers of the employer’s favor. “There is a nurse and a medic-clinic but there are no medicines and they don’t treat us well or give us medicines if we visit the clinic. The in charge of COC is a Myanmar national but yet they point things with feet to junior workers,” they said. The workers said that they want to request to give a day off a week as they are working overtime daily without day offs which cause them health issues, to survey their consents before calling overtime, the supervisors to not verbally abuse the workers, the Myanmar national COC in charge to not point with feet and to ask only the possible fabric outputs. Content: It is reported that 126 Myanmar workers were defrauded of hundreds of millions of kyats although the discussion to send Myanmar seasonal workers to South Korea has not been settled yet. “Myanmar can’t provide the documents South Korea asked for and vice versa. The project is managed by the mayor and it doesn’t need immigrations and labor ministries. But Myanmar would only allow to send workers only after those documents are approved. That’s where things are still. And we can’t gather people for the negotiations. It is obvious that they are lying when you listen logically to what scammers say. But people don't care as they want to go right now,” said a person who is sending migrant workers. Daw Chaw Su Hlaing said that she would quickly send seasonal workers to South Korea, and the 126 trainees from Myint Mo Academy were pre-purchased at the rate of 2,750,000 kyats and 3,200,000 kyats each. The contract was signed but workers are not going anywhere so they announce via the lawyers to resolve. “They scam a large amount and not black listed. Its just for a school. But we don’t know how many such schools are there. Korean language school owners are having a headage now. People want to go quick as soon as possible and don’t think logically,” they said.  Ever since the news broke that they were discussing sending seasonal workers to South Korea, financial scams involving recruiting people to go to South Korea as seasonal workers have occurred throughout the country. Agencies said that they warn not to make advance payments until there is a press release from the relevant government, and they also have repeatedly warned that the recruitment of temporary workers is still under discussion and has not been confirmed. Currently, there are a lot of scammers on the internet about hiring seasonal workers in Korea. The current fraud of thousands of dollars is also the first to come to light, but it is also known that there may be many frauds in other language schools as well as individually to the workers. The countries are still on the state of discussing the possibility of sending seasonal workers to South Korea. The recruitment of seasonal workers in Korea is not managed by the Korean Ministry of Labor and other departments, but by the mayor's plan, so the Myanmar side has not been able to provide the necessary documents. Currently, there are more and more financial frauds with documents claiming that seasonal workers are being recruited to South Korea. Also, the fraudulent recruitment of seasonal workers started at the beginning of last October and have been ongoing until now. Regarding the issue, the Republic of Korea Embassy, Yangon has confirmed that documents related to the sending of seasonal workers from Myanmar are being shared on the Internet. It is also announced that the documents and information are not relevant to the Korean government and the Republic of Korea Embassy, Yangon, and the Korean government has not issued any announcements regarding seasonal workers in Myanmar. Seasonal workers do not need to speak Korean and there is no need for educational qualifications, and they work for eight months a year, then take a break for three months, and after they have worked for five years, they can change to another type of visa. Content: According to the workers from LITA MYANMAR garment factory which locates at Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone 4, Yangon said that the factory call overtimes on Sundays, asked excessive fabric outputs, verbally abuse and not granting some benefits. The workers said that the Chinese national owned factory operates with around 1,000 workers but there is no trade union. The factory is manufacturing GLACIER, CONVERSE, heartgreen and BURTLE WW brands apparels. They are working overtimes on Sundays and also all evening and all night overtimes but not informed in advanced. They are neither able to refuse to work overtime and not provided transportation. Those who refuse to work overtime are discriminated against in the factory. “They usually force us to work at other departments that we haven’t done before and also ask for the same outputs. They ask around 35 garments per hour and we have to work without going to toilet and takes a water break. They verbally abuse us every time they asked for fabric outputs even if we can finish,” said a worker. They are cut daily wages 4,800 kyats and attendance bonus 10,000 kyats for a single day of absent. The working hours is officially from 7:30 to 6:30 but some departments are forced to work all night on the grounds of important fabrics without getting paid for attendance bonus and expert fees. ‘There are water storages sometimes as they provided water only with the bottles. The toilet water is cut during the break time and only given on working hours so there are difficulties. And we can’t go to toilets in working hours,” said a worker. The workers request that to ask their consents before calling the overtime, to provide the transportations for the overtime, to give all workers attendance bonus and expert fees equally, to ask only possible fabric outputs, the foreigners not to directly manage the factory, not to treat poorly to the workers who visit the factory’s clinic and to provide sufficient pharmacies. Content: According to shopkeepers, it is becoming difficult for retail shops to stay afloat as the price of domestic goods, including basic food to consumer goods, is rising every day.  At present, commodity prices are changing daily. Due to this situation, retail stores are facing the problem of increasing capital and declining sales. “We sold with 550 kyats but have to buy with 600 kyats later and that’s happening rapidly. It is stressful to sell goods. Even if we sell, we are worrying if we could buy with that price again and if there is shortage. My shop is a family business, so we don’t have much capital. We will close the shop if the situation get worse because there is no interests, some shops have already closed,” said a family business shop owner. Commodity prices have been rising faster after the coup d'état. During the Thingyan, there was a record rose, and there are currently shortages of goods. "A pack of coffee is sold for 350 kyats. The kids snacks which sold for 50 kyats before  it is sold for 100 kyats now. The price of some items has not gone up, but the quantity falls. Only two pack of snacks have equivalent amount for a pack of its before and there are many family shops right now. Many people open shops to earn extra income. But the demands are decline due to raising prices. A shop in a street may benefits before but 3 or 4 shops is not,” said a shopkeeper. The commodity price are continuously increasing due to the decline of currency values and difficulties in transportation. The raw rice price is 5,000 kyats and the palm oil cost 900 kyats. A branch of sweet potato leaves cost 700 kyats, a 10 kyats thar (166g) of tomato cost 400 kyats and a peiktha (1.6kg) of onion cost more than 2,000 kyats and a peiktha of garlic cost around 1,500 kyats. It increase 1 lakh just in an evening. World gold price may seems a bit decline but the dollar price are racing so I am not sure weather the gold price will decline again but it just my opinion,” said a market researcher. 1 oz of gold in global market cost 2,442 kyats but in Myanmar 1 kyat thar cost more than 51 lakhs. In May 25 evening, 1 oz of gold in global market cost 2,334 kyats but in Myanmar, 1 kyat thar cost 5,240,000 kyats, 5,230,000 kyats on May 26th and more than 53 lakhs in evening of May 27. Therefore, the gold manufacturers are currently suspend selling gold by pieces and the market is quiet for now. The closing price of the Yangon Region Gold Industry Association in the evening of May 27th 2024   for academy Mee Lin Gold is 3,999,300 kyats and the price in real market is 5,300,000 kyats for Akhauk gold. Content: Basic class people are having difficulties to buy palm oil as the family business shops that sell palm oils are closed. At present, palm oil is being sold on a rationed basis. In the wards, a family is allowed to buy ngase tha  (1.8 lb) with the oil purchasing cards. “We don’t get the cards. So, we have to buy in the market which cost 1,000 kyats more. But it is difficult when they don’t sell,” said a housewife from Shwe Pyi Thar. It is reported that even though some wards have a card to buy palm oil once every three days, there are also some wards that no longer get it. In addition, manual laborers have financial and time constraints to extract oil. “Its past 9’oclock when they give the oil card. We have reached to the factory at that time and when we come back its too late to buy. It is not comfortable for asking other people to buy palm oil for us if we don’t give a 500 – 1,000 kyats stipend. We just buy some equivalent amounts of 1,000 kyats nearby. Its like we don’t get the palm oil cards at all,” said a factory worker. Currently, it is set to be sold at only with an additional small higher price of transportation than the government's set price with only a small addition of transportation costs and general expenses. In practice, it is casually inspected whether the sale is in accordance with the instructions or not without authorities’ uniform. “They sold with higher price when inspectors wear like undercover. The whole market have to sign pledge after being caught. They said those who sell again will be sentenced in prison for 3 years and the shop had to be closed. We can’t sell with 1,000 kyats when we are not buying with the price they set. I feel set for my customers when I can’t sell anymore,” said a shopkeeper who is selling palm oil in the municipal market. At present, the price of palm oil per peittha (3.6 lb) is published daily, and it has been reported that they are working to stabilize the price. Content: According to reports from Thai media, more than 30 Myanmar workers, including a child, who crossed the border illegally, were arrested near the checkpoint in Thikhron village, Nunglu village tract, Sangkhlaburi town, Kanchanaburi district, Thailand. At around 6:15 in the morning on May 26, 18 men, 9 women, 3 underage children, who came in a truck, were jointly investigated and arrested by Thai local authorities. According to the investigation they are from Yangon Region, Bago Region, Mandalay Region, Mon State, Kayin State and they came to Thailand to work at Bangkok and other cities. They have to to the brokers from 15,000 to 20,000 baht to came here and certain amounts have been paid. It is reported that those who have been arrested will be taken to Sangkhlaburi Police Station to proceed according to the law. Content: It is said that there are many people who have sought help from the anti-trafficking police to help them because they were sold as Chinese men’s wives and trafficked after going to work in China. It is said that there are the victims themselves who contacted the anti-trafficking police also those asked for help via the family members of the people who were trafficked. It is said that the majority of those who are sold as Chinese men’s wives are those who are trafficked to the other country by looking for work online. “The most common thing is that people are sold from looking for work online. They are taken advantage of by brokers and traffickers by the fake advertise salaries online when there is lack of employment and low wages in the country. Those who fell in the traps were sold as Chinese men’s wife,” said an officer from anti-trafficking police force. The anti-trafficking police have connected with China's Shwe Li anti-trafficking office to bring back those who have asked for help. It is said that there were 30 women who asked for help last year and 26 of them were rescued. There were 7 people who asked for help in this year and two of them were found and rescued and trying to recuse the remaining people as well. Due to the low wages in the country, despite working, it is becoming difficult to make a living and adult women and men who are able to work are traveling to foreign workplaces and borders to work and some are targeted by scammers and some are trafficked. Content: It is reported that on May 21, the judge ordered to file an additional lawsuit against the Company label in addition of CEO and HR of Pepsi company in the lawsuit filed by the workers against the officials of the Pepsi soft drink factory in Mawbe Township and Pepsi nominated 3 complainants.  “It is true that the Pepsi company would be sued too. The company have to nominate a representative for that. It will follow the process. Workers submitted a request letter and they will submit a refutation. That’s how plaintiff cases work. The company will submit proofs and the judge will decree after that,” said a person who is helping the case. The Judge approved Daw Su Su Myat who was selected by the Pepsi Company’s meeting decision as a representative and the rescheduled the next court at 11:00 am on June 4. After the two-sided examination was conducted at the Mawbe District Court in the case (Pepsi) filed by U Thaung Han, a former worker, at the trial on April 3rd, the judge ordered that the company label be sued as an additional lawsuit, and the company have to confront. U Thaung Han was dismissed illegally on October 31, 2022 due to his age which is against the EC contract and the negotiations were not success in several levels and the worker sued only at mid-March 2023 when he get approval letter to sue.  There is a campaign to international customers to boycott Pepsi as the factory dismissed a worker who worked for 20 years without compensation and dismissed the sales in the same way without compensation on the grounds that they don’t hit the target. Content: It is said that officials from Township Labor Department would come to inspect our factory on May 25, 2024. The factory didn’t inform all the workers but selected 15 clerk and 3 veteran workers on May 24  to be inspected. I heard the inspection is due to the reports from Myanmar Labour News. The factory resolve only the narrow dinning space among the facts mentioned in the news. The other things such as not providing purified water, hot temperature due to not opening the doors, not allowing water bottle, increasing the output demands and verbal abuse are not solved. The production manager called the clerks on May 24 and tells them to say the inspectors that the issues mentioned in the news are not correct. We heard from the workers that they taught them to answer that we are only asked 25 fabric per hour, we are allowed to take water bottle, they provide purified water and they don’t shut the doors.  They assigned the clerks to pretend like helpers, seamstresses and workers from other departments. As a worker, I worried that the problems happening really will not be addressed. I request for the fair inspection. Content: Workers from South Korean national owned Panko Bago Company which located at Bago said that the factory is calling them excessive amount of overtime more than 4 months,” a worker said. “We have to work Sunday overtime every two week. We only have 2 days off per month. We had to bring a bed sheet to sleep on when we are called night overtime. We have to sleep in rows," the workers said. The factory call overtime for 2 hours a day normally but also called until 8:30 or 10:30 pm casually and workers have to eat dinner with their own plan. And having to work from 12:30 pm to 6:30 pm continuously as well,” according to the workers. “Those who are not called for overtime go back home at 4:30 but those who are called don’t even have 15 or 20 minutes to rest, so they are more tired,” workers said. And they face problems whenever they see the petrol teams on the way back home after the midnight overtime. “The supervisors don’t ask for our consents. It is like do or leave. They signed overtime papers for us. There are many people who fainted or stiffed for having to work that much,” workers said. They are not informed about the overtime in advanced so parents worried as they came back late. And leaves are not granted in the factory so they are labeled as absent when they take a leave and attendance bonus is cut. “We are tired but no benefits. We lost 30,000 kyats which we can afford for rice. Workers with around 5 family members most become difficult,” said a worker. The overtime payment is not transparent as they give by names and there are discriminations in the factory. There are supervisors who are selling illegal lotteries and some stuffs from the administration team are participating. “There is two groups. One who sell and buy illegal lotteries and one who don’t. The factory seems like a casino. The administration team pretended that they don’t know because they too are participating,” the worker said.  It have been 6 months the illegal lotteries are being sold. Another problem is the workers have to run to the dinning room as it is far from the factory.  According to DICA’s data, Panko Bago Company factory located at Nyaung Inn Village, Bago Township and operating with foreign investments. There are around 1,000 workers working in the factory and workplace coordination committee cannot do effective actions. Content: The security worker who worked at GTIG Guohua Glory Garment factory which located at Wun Saung Mhu Street, War Ta Yar Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township filed a report and the case is being addressed. “He contracted via the brand yesterday. The factory tends to give the worker’s 4 points of requests but not yet signed. The trade union, employer and the brand are negotiating but not reached to an exact solution. Because re-hire is ok but the overtime which have to be calculated by the backdate are still being negotiated,” said a person who is helping the worker.  The security worker started working at the factory since 9th May, 2022 and had more than 2 years of service working with 3 day shifts and 3 night shifts from 6:00 am to 6:00 pm as day shift and from 6:00 pm to 6:00 am as night shift and was dismissed without any mistake committed on the grounds that a new employer will be replaced. The worker said he didn’t receive 4 hours of overtime while he worked there and hired as a day employer until 2 years without an EC contract therefore contacted Solidarity of Trade Unions, Myanmar - STUM with four points: 1. Illegal dismiss, 2. Not getting paid for 4 hours of overtime per day, 3. Hired as a day employer until 2 years and 4. The factory failed to make EC contract. The employer, employee and brand are negotiating for those 4 requests.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: Workers from Eslite Garment factory which hires more than 3,000 workers and located at Maung Kyan Thee Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township said that the supervisors are verbally abusing them to get more fabric outputs beyond their productivity. The Chinese national owned factory is manufacturing Japanese brand GORE-TEX and a cavity with 30 people including the supervisor have to give 80 to 90 fabric per 10 hours. “They are asking more than we could make. We negotiated before but currently a worker is assigned for 3 to 4 points. We are being verbally abused every day for not meeting the targets,” a worker said. The factory workers are get paid 50,000 kyats for A+, 40,000 kyats for A and 25,000 kyats for B+, 20,000 kyats for B, 10,000 kyats for C as professional fees. The factory bias the workers who are confident with the supervisors and those who are not are discriminate in the workplace,” the worker said. There are more than 100 day laborers in the factory but they are not appointed as permanent stuffs after working for more than 3 months.   “The soldiers looked for the trade union leaders in the factory in August, 2023 but the workers was fortunate as the manager informed them a night in advanced. Sine then, the workers were oppressed,” a worker said. The trade unions were cracked down intentionally and workers are oppressed since then. The workers said that they want to request to ask only the possible fabric output, not to bias the expert fee, to appoint day laborers with more than 3 months of service as permanent workers, the supervisors not to verbally abuse the workers. Content: It is reported that the illegal Burmese workers are concerned about Thai authorities are collecting biometric information in the districts where many Myanmar nationals live. There are many Myanmar nationals who are legally staying as well as many who are living illegally, so this collection of biological information is said to be a concern for those who are living illegally.  “Those who have migrated for political reasons do not dare to give the information now, it may be dangerous if this information gets into pro Juntas’ hands,” said labor activist Daw Wai Wai Tin. Only the Burmese nationals are collected for the bio-data among other foreigners in 5 districts where most Myanmar citizens presence including Tak and Samut Sakhon. Around 10,000 Myanmar workers are collected eye and face scans and Burmese nationals from other districts will be collected as well according to the sources. Regarding such a survey, authorities said it is for health reasons, and the difficulties and social health conditions faced by Myanmar every day and that there is no need to worry about harassment after asking the information obtained. 600 people per day will be surveyed. “There might be plans to arrest when they are issuing documents for illegal workers but this survey will not raise the arrests. They can’t be arrested more than this. There are also arrests in the night time but not because of this project,” said a Burmese migrant activist in Thailand. Although the collection of biological data is titled as a health survey, only those with the UID card which the biological data were collected are allowed to travelled to foreign countries in Myanmar too. This kind of collection and restriction of biological records both domestically and abroad is a deliberate act to create a crisis for the security of the people according to a Myanmar national in Thailand. There are many Myanmar nationals in Thailand who oppose the military dictatorship including workers, Labor activists say that this collection of biological information is a concern for everyone's safety. Content: Workers from New Talent Garment (Myanmar) Co.,Ltd said that they are working with the boiler smoke odors in the factory B where they start boiler smoke more than 5 times a month. “We smell odors when they start the fire. The smokes even look like fog  in the factory,” a worker said. Factory B is a three-story building, and the sewing place is on the top floor. It is said that there are 10 machine lines on that floor and around 400 workers are working. The workers said that they are constantly suffering from suffocation and dizziness due to the smoke and fumes. "The smoke looks like a fog, so we had to go to the hospital due to suffocation and dizziness. The factory does not provide masks. There are no more clinics and nurses, so they have to pay their own way to the welfare clinic. We have to carry a bottle of respirator. I was also forced to work because I couldn't afford to visit clinic anymore," said a worker. The workers said that the drinking water is not clean and contained particles and having odors due to keeping near the toilet. "There are two places where we can drink water. We had to drink in a bottle from a pipe that passed through the toilet somewhere. The Chinese are also washing their hands there. The next place is the HR office.  The water is sedimented," they said of the drinking water situation. The workers also said that the number of workers who quit their jobs is up to a few hundred in a year as some New Talent Garment supers verbally abuse them. “A pregnant female worker felt unwell when she arrived at work. She get up and vomit. As this happens, she told the Super to change the fabric point. But they don’t. The female resigned the next day. Some male workers are resigned after verbally abused,” the worker said. It is known the line 4 super verbally abuse them in rudest ways.  A pregnant worker who submitted a resignation letter as super did not give her a gate pass also suffered a miscarriage while waiting for her resignation letter.  The workers also said that justice was not served because the labor officials selected only 3 workers from the factory to inquire about the incident. There are more than 1,000 workers working at the two building of the New Talent Garment factory owned by Chinese nationals and the factory locates at Own Nae Kone Village, Hleku  Township, Yangon region and the workers are manufacturing socks and jackets. Content: Recently, some factories in Yangon's industrial zones have increased the minimum wage and hiring. However, according to the current commodity price, the rate is still lower than what they should be getting, even though they work with an increased amount, the workers say that they have to work 16 hours a day to make a living.  According to the Minimum Wage Law, the legally set domestic minimum wage is 4,800 kyats, and in the past year, it has been set to increase by one thousand kyats per day as a subsidy. "This is not a rate that the workers should really get. Some factories are still paying 4,800 plus a thousand. The commodity price is much higher than before. The wages should be doubled than before. The current increase has not reached enough to pay," said a member of the trade union. Since May 1 this month, factories in Yangon have been hiring workers for 6,800 – 7,200 -7,500 kyats per day, etc., and they started recruiting workers with the raised rate as well as raising the salary of current workers. The 2018 wages of the workers have only been slightly increased only by 2024 but it is not enough according to the current rising commodity prices, so it is necessary to adjust the workers' daily wage to a rate that matches the commodity price. A USD worths more than 4,000 kyats, and the price of gold has reached over 5,100,000 kyats, so the price of basic commodities is also rising steadily. A pitha of Salt cost 9,000 kyats, a pyi of rice cost 5,000 kyats, a pitha of onion cost 3,000 kyats, a branch of bean cost 1,200 kyats and a egg cost 350 kyats therefore a worker should get paid from 10,000 to 12,000 kyats considering the years missed to revise the minimum wages law. Due to these very low wages, local workers easily leave for foreign countries such as Thailand and China.  It is said that the labor shortage in factories will increase further. At present, new factories and factories that will expand the production line have increased the demand for skilled workers, so there have been such types of daily wage increases. A dollar worth from 1,200 to 1,300 kyats at 2018 and employers are still paying 4,800 kyats when a dollar worth more than 4,000 kyats after a year. Content: Workers from Chinese national owned Li DA garment which located at Oothaphraaa Street, Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township told that they are working 6 hours without a break and having health and social issues due to daily overtime. “They don’t give us a break from 12:30 pm to 6:30 pm,” a worker said. And the factory only provide a breed for them when they work overtime until 8:30pm without a break. “They give us a breed and we have to work immediately after that, we can’t take a proper break outside. The workers are so tired,” they said. The working hours are from 8:00 am to 6:30 including the overtime and they have to work from 12:30 until the end of working hours continuously. The daily overtime without proper meal cause them health problems and some even have to visit the clinics with the gate pass. “Some workers come from Hlaing Thar Yar. They arrive home at 9:30-10:00 after the factory’s working hour finished at 8:30. They don’t have proper time to eat except the ready made foods. They come with plasters on their head in the next morning,” according to the worker. Although the factory workers are facing health problems, there are no clinics or nurses in the workplace. There are workers' refusals for the overtimes, but some employees forced them to work.  “The supervisors force us to sign only with their accord. Workers refuse to work overtime but the supers don’t let them go until they signed,” a worker said. The workers are working overtime until 6:30 a week and until 8:30 a week since after the Thingyan. The factory assigned them to work until 7:30 for this month. There are around 6 cavities and 250 workers working at the Li Da garment factory. Myanmar Labour News posted at news about 29 workers of the Li Da garment factory resigned after the super was demoted to line leader position. Workers said the working conditions aren’t improve since then.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: There is an increase in recruitment of skilled Myanmar garment workers through the installment system in China’s industrial zones and the Myanmar workers who are going are also raising as well. “They called expert seamstress with free travel expenses but they should do the Smart ID card before. The salary of the first month would be mortgaged and they will get paid starting the second month. The free travel expenses will be cut from their salaries. If they quit before 3 months, they have to compensate the travel expense. Many people are interesting to work and brokers are also raising,” said a Myanmar worker from Shwe Li.  Many Myanmar workers are going to work at Shwe Li, Man Si and Lyan Hal garment factories where recruitment are raising.  “My acquittances are now at Shwe Li. There is lack of employment in Muse. Some goes with agencies and some goes with the network of current workers. The important thing is they have to try to get the smart card. The car ticket price from Mandalay to Muse Cost 250,000 Lakhs. They have to book in advance,” said a driver who is driving on the Mandalay-Muse road. Some goes with the network of their friends who are current workers and some goes with brokers which cause from 5-7 lakhs.  Two industrial zones are recruiting 60 expert seamstresses including the former workers and new workers who already have smart card via the brokers. There are people who make smart cards with brokers which cost from 80,000 to 200,000 kyats. Currently, there is a shortage of skilled workers in the country, and even cause a situation where wages are raised a little, working in China can earn a minimum of 700,000 to 1000,000 Myanmar Kyat per month, so they are moving to work in garment factories in China, where they can easily enter and leave. Content: Myanmar workers in Malaysia who have incomplete credentials and who will return to Myanmar with a Certificate of Identity (CI) issued by the Myanmar Embassy, ​​were notified by the Embassy in Kuala Lumpur on May 21 to apply for an exit pass at the Malaysian immigration offices during the period when the Malaysian government is waiving fines.  The Malaysian government announced that foreigners who illegally entered Malaysia from March 1 to December 31, 2024, can leave Malaysia within 14 days after paying a fixed fine of 500 ringgit and 100 ringgit for an exit pass at the Malaysian immigration offices with a passport or CI to the country of origin and a return flight ticket. Currently, there is agendas to arrest illegal foreign workers in Malaysia, and it is reported that many Myanmar nationals are being arrested with incomplete documents. "There are too many arrests these days, those who would go back with incomplete documents should apply for an exit pass because if they are arrested, they are going to be sentenced to prison. Now is the time when the Malaysian government allows them to pay the fine and take the plane back safely," said a Myanmar worker in Malaysia. The Myanmar embassy has informed that Myanmar nationals who have obtained an exit pass at the Malaysian immigration office should obtain a passport or CI document, air ticket and the acceptance letter with the fine, acceptance paper with paid fines at the Malaysian immigration and the exit pass that allows to leave Malaysia in case they are caught before the check-in date to leave Malaysia to exempt from arrest.  In addition, the Myanmar Embassy further informed that the fine of 500 ringgit and exit pass 100 ringgit to be paid at the offices in Malaysia must be paid by credit card / debit card only. Content: According to the industrialists, all the factories in the industrial zones in Myanmar will only get 2 hours of electricity a day. Previously, they got 4 hours of electricity a day, but they were informed through the relevant township electricity office that they only pay two hours a day starting at May 19th. "They didn't send a letter and. The electricity office told me over the phone Since we are a glass factory, cutting is convenient only if there is electricity. The cost of using generator is will high So, we have to do most of the works when there is electricity. The rental costs are not avoidable, not only me but all employers are facing the difficulties,” said a employer from Hlaing Thar Yar Industrial Zone 3. An official from the township's electricity office told a local news outlet that due to the lack of electricity at present, only 2 hours of electricity are being supplied to industrial zones to pump up water. "If the employers spend more money and have less profits and losses, the wages for the workers will be lower. I read an entrepreneur's post saying that the time the electricity present is before the factory’s working hours," said the labor activist. The weather temperature has increased, but people are suffering from the effects of the heat because of the short time they have access to electricity. Content: The Minister of Defense, a member of the Military Council, said on May 20 that they are preparing to recruit militia service training batch 3.   He spoke at the coordination meeting of the Central Committee for Public Service Recruitment held at the Ministry of Defense in Nay Pyi Taw. The militia service law is currently being drafted and said at that it will be submitted to the Union Government for approval through the Security, Law and Order Committee. The military council has said that 5,000 citizens will be recruited every batch, and currently, they have recruited up to 2 batches. "The head of ward administration and members asked for 10 thousand kyats per household in the neighborhood for personal replacement. I don't know whom they will replace. I don't know which batch. We had to give the money as there is no one in the eligible age in our family," said a resident of Myeik. In addition to this, up to 60,000 people will be recruited for military service, and there are over 6 million men and 7 million women in the country, a total of nearly 14 million are eligible for military service, according to a spokesman for the Military Council. Due to the demand for labor force in the country after the conscription, some factories are raising wages to hire workers, and some foreign companies are saying that there is a shortage of labor force in the country. CJ, the Korean chicken hatchery industry, has announced that it will temporarily stop operations in Myanmar. "It is true that there is labor shortage because of the military service law. Another thing is the low wages. Many people are trying to go to abroad," said a labor activist.  All those who fail to attend the military service call-up will be dealt with according to the existing law, and the Minister of Defense of the Military Council has also instructed to start the 3rd batch before reaching the target. Content: Max Technology headphones factory workers asked to determine the bonus only with the expert fee as they are asked for excessive outputs and facing pay cuts. The factory locates at Than Din 19 intersection, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon. “The inspectors come after we reported but nothing changed. We have to sign for the overtime in advance and sometimes we don’t have to work. They said they would dismiss if we could’t meet their hourly rates within 3 days. They asked 300 earphones per hour. Even the senior workers could make 150 per hour. The bonus are cut if we can’t finish. The workplace coordination committee follows their orders. We want to request that not to ask the impossible fabric outputs, the supervisors not to do only on their accord and to determine the bonus only with the expert fee instead of the hourly rate,” the worker said. The workers at the factory have to come early for the meeting every day, and they are not allowed fully half an hour for a meal break, and the supervisors verbally abusing to the workers and charge if they use the restroom 3 times. The workers are requesting to determine the bonus only with the expert fee instead of the hourly rate as the factory asked for impossible outputs and those who don’t finished are cut. “We want the factory to call overtime only if they can give it and the working hours should be exactly from 8:00 to 4:30. The superiors not to verbally abuse and to give the full salaries. The hourly rates asked by them such as 200 strings per 6 minutes is even impossible for them and they told us that they will cut as if we can’t finish. They ask 1,000 pin points per hour and the maximum we could do is 800. They don’t give the daily wages of the workers those resigned,” a worker said. The factory have been operating for only 6 months and working with 5 lines and more than 250 workers. Content: Workers from Saung Oo Shwe Nay garment factory said that the Department of Labor issued them the letter to sue their employer but it is taken back. The factory locates at Alal 3 Street, Ngwe Pin Lae Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon. “The western district Department of Labor officials issued the letter to sue the employer for violating the EC contracts and let the workers read. After the workers agree they badged and signed and kept it in an envelope but after 15 minutes, the decision was changed,” said a worker who participated. The Employment Agreement (EC) contract is signed under Section 5(a) 1 of the Employment and Professional Development Act of 2013, and this contract must be complied by the employer and the employee. Those who do not comply must be dealt with in accordance with Section (39) of the Employment and Professional Development Law.  The violation of the employment contract was negotiated 3 times between the workers and the employer of Saung Oo Shwe Nay garment factory A at the Hlaing Thar Yar Department of Labor office. Workers said that the contract is signed according to the law and the violations are the workers being changed to other departments. There are more than 300 workers in the A factory and the workers asked to dismiss them with compensation if the factory will not re-open. In addition, on May 13, officials from the township's Ministry of Labor visited the Saung Oo Shwe Nay factory and called and inspected 4 workers from A factory who were making demands in the evening. Therefore, the labor office officials repeatedly intimidated that they would not receive the salary for the period under negotiation if they did not work, and they did not ask and discuss with the workers who were making the request.  The case was examined by the arbitration panel, and the employer's representative must pay the interim wages, but the arbitration decision did not decide upon that issue. Saung Oo Shwe Nay garment factory is owned by Chinese national and employs about 1,800 workers and manufactures SMOG, H&M and DIVIDED brand apparels. The workers also said that H&M orders were transferred to other branches due to the disputes with workers. Content: CJ Feed Myanmar, which manufactures and sells animal feed and chicken hatchery, has announced that it will suspend production based on the lack of manpower to produce products and the current decline in business operations.  Starting May 28, CJ Company's production and sale of animal feed and chicken hatchery will be temporarily suspended, and it is said that the current operational capabilities are decreasing more than before. The company's facing a shortage of labor in addition of sales becoming difficult, facing increasing costs and difficult of obtaining raw materials which is an unavoidable situation.  The company has requested the dealers and  customers of the CJ company to give the arrears of goods by June 28th 2024. "Other factories that produce animal feed are also facing such difficulties. They are also struggling to solve it. Now, it is not just the factories that have a shortage of workers. There is also a shortage of workers in the agricultural industry. Many of them go abroad. In our corn farming, we pay 12,000 - 15,000 kyats per day, but there are very few people who will work," said a corn farmer.  Since the implementation of the conscription law in the country, many young people have left abroad, and due to the decline in the domestic economy and low wages, the construction, industrial zone and agriculture, live stocks and other various industries are experiencing labor shortages. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: The workers of the Joc Myanmar Garment Factory say that their benefits and salaries are being cut. It is reported that the factory is owned by Chinese national and manufactures TR Style and TIGORA brand clothes. “They cut daily wages, attendance bonus and grade fees for absent,” a worker said. Even though they informed the leave they are labeled as absent and cut for daily wages and attendance bonus. The workers said that there is also a postponement of the bonus and benefits to which workers with a year of service are entitled. The workers are forced to sign for 2 weeks overtime schedules without being asked for their consents. “They force us to sign that we know there is overtime for 12 days (2 weeks). But they don’t ask our consent and it was worse before, they just inform about the overtime at 4:00 pm with a microphone,” said a worker. The working hours of the Joc Myanmar factory are from 8 am to 6 pm (with 2 overtime hours), but the workers said that starting next week, they will be asked to work overtime until 7 pm and give half an hour of rest.  A worker said that the factory workers could not refuse overtime and were verbally abused and intimidated with employment. "A worker can’t work overtime for 4 days if they refuse one. I was asked to go back at four o'clock in the evening. The Chinese experts told me. There are such intimidations. There are days when the workers can't work overtime due to their circumstances. Overtime can’t be void as salary is not enough. Sometimes, when we refuse to work overtime, the super just keeps verbally abuse," said one of the workers. At the Joc Myanmar Garment Factory, lunch time is divided into two periods, and at 11:30 am and 12:00 pm, they have half an hour to eat lunch. But the workers said that from the time they returned to work, they had to work continuously until 6 p.m. without stopping. “Those who eat at 11:00 am have to work at 12:00 and those eat at 12:00 have to work at 12:30. We have to work for more than 5 hours and around 6 hours as we finished the work at 6:00 pm,” they said. In addition, the workers also said that they were suffered because the factory reduced the payment of their grade bonus (expert fees) in April, saying that they did not take into account public holidays. "They reduced the amount of money we had to get by putting down the grades for April. Seems like they will even pay less on Sundays. For us, we suffered between 30,000 to 50,000 each. They should know that the cut money can be used for four or five days for the workers," a worker said. One of the aggrieved workers also said that they have complained that their bonuses have been cut. Around 10 workers out of around 700 factory workers were summoned and examined and the head of the Factory and General Labor Law Inspection Department, U Tun Aung Kyaw, decided in a moment that the workers should not receive their regular bonuses. Workers said that there is only workplace coordination committee that doesn’t address the workers’ presentations, instead of the trade union at the Joc Myanmar garment factory which locates at the U Myae Street, Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone 4. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: According to the licensed agency community, online recruitment is on the rise and advertised transparently by those who send the workers illegally after the restriction of men's permission to work abroad from the age of 23 to 31. They said that there are more and more advertisements on online pages of people who are smuggled to the other country by various methods including by applying visit visas to many foreign countries, including Thailand, Malaysia, Laos, and Korea. "Since before, there have been fake pages and fake accounts and advertisements calling for jobs online. But lately, we have seen many people filming videos of how they deliver, interviewing the people who they sent, and uploading those videos. We have seen more advertisements to make people believe that they are sending through illegal ways securely," said a person close to the agency community. It is said that some people who want to work abroad have been scammed by these advertisements. "I found that they advertised for people who want to work in Thailand, so I called them and checked. They said that there are men from 23 to 31 can also go even without their passports. They said that if there are different price just to arrive or helped get a job. They said that I have to pay a deposit first. I didn't like what they said, so I didn't continue,” said a person who inquired to go work abroad. Currently, there are many people being arrested for entering to foreign countries illegally, and illegal workers are being arrested almost every day in Thailand, Malaysia, and China. Content: I am a worker from Tha Shu (Myanmar) Glory Fashion garment factory. There is no sufficient dinning space in the factory. I attached a photo. There are 15 cavities in the factory with 70 workers per cavity; total 1,400 workers are working in the factory. The dinning room is not fit for the workers since then, but it becomes more tidier as they put machines and equipment in the room. Some workers have to eat on the floor and some have to eat in places which they shouldn’t be. The drinking water is also not purified. It came directly from the well via the pipe lines and it have odors. We are drinking those impurified water. We tried to take water ourselves but the factory doesn’t allow to take inside the factory, so we have go outside to drink. The line managers and supervisors scold us if we take time a little long to go drink outside. They also scolded for not getting the demanded outputs. They humiliated in public with the rudest words and sometimes the owner even participated. They asked 40 overbought fabrics per hour which we sew only 25 before the coup and we are assigned unfairly. They close every door except one since the start of working hour so seamstresses are suffering from the high temperature and there is lack of fans. The factory located at Shwe Than Lwin Street, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone and owned by a Chinese national. We want the officials to resolve the disputes. Content: The human trafficking business that recruits Chinese men’s wives is growing again at the China-Myanmar border, and it is seen that both those who recruiter and applicants are doing it openly. "In the past, they lied about having to work as a maid. But for now they told the truth and doing the business transparently, it increase after the coup. The recruiter told that they would get 150, 180 lakhs for being wife of a Chinese man for 3 months. Some worked even with 100 lakhs. I feel sad when the women themselves are willing to do. The fortune told by Bo Gyoke seems true. I want to warn the girls that not to believe them. They just marry them to void legal actions and they will treat them like a slave after that. And the wife is shared by around 3 friends. Burmese women shouldn’t trust them, Don’t sold yourself with around 100 lakhs. You would be in trouble after that,” a jewelry dealer from the Chinese border said.  Human trafficking brokers are recruiting from Facebook and WeChat social networking sites such as Muse-Shwe Li-Jie Gong employment groups to purchase Chinese men’s wives, and there are many female workers who say "Interested, please contact me". Such activities were done secretly in the past, but due to the scarcity of local jobs in Myanmar and the political situation in the country after the military coup, many Burmese women who want to work as housekeepers believe in the incentives of legal marriage with a lot of money, and many Burmese women are being trafficked. “We have difficulties to help inside the mainland. There are many requests from them to help. But we can only help with limits. The Chinese will confiscate all the documents of those women. Some women are physically assaulted. Not only them but they have to give birth as well. Good Chinese rich man is hard to find. Its very difficult to help them if they are in middle or northern China. We can’t track so don’t chose that path,” said a local resident. Due to the lack of jobs and the political situation in Myanmar, there are many cases of Burmese women being sold as Chinese men’s wives in northern and central China, after arriving at the China-Myanmar border to work with one week border pass from Muse.  There are also many women who chose with their consents and majority of them are from Mandalay, Sagaing and Magwe divisions. A resident said that it is difficult to deal with the current human – trafficking cases of being sold as Chinese men’s wives, and if they are sold to places like northern and central China, it will be very difficult if the human trafficking organizations from China and Myanmar have linked with each other. Therefore, they said that they want to warn not to accept the financial incentives To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: Despite the gold and dollar value rising in Myanmar, workers still receive only 4,800 kyats for 8 hours of work without being raised the daily minimum wage. Last year, the ministry increased the stipend by 1,000 kyat, but the salary was not increased.  "Some factories have increased the daily wages on this month. Some factories are paying 4,800 a day and 1,000 as an allowance. I have heard that workers from some factories are asking to raise the allowance. 1 kyat thar of gold (16.6 gram) is over 50 lakhs and a dollar is over 4,000 dollars. So far, the workers’ wages are not raised. 4,800 kyats a day can’t even feed their stomach well," said a worker. Some factory owners in Yangon have raised the daily wages due to the shortage of workers and some factory raise 1,000 kyats in the allowance. “Some factories are hiring with 6,500 or 7,000 or 7,5000 kyats and some factories are giving 2,000 kyats daily stipend and 10,000 monthly extra allowance and raise the attendance bonus from 20,000 kyats to 30,000 kyats. But there are many factories which still pay 4,800 kyats as the law don’t legally revised. The employers have to raise mandatorily only if the minimum wage law is revised. Currently, only few employers raise but that is still not the preferred amount,” said a trade union member. The workers said that although some factories increased the allowance up to 7,500 kyats, they did not add a thousand kyat allowance, so it was not a significant change. The workers said that only if the minimum wage specified in the law is changed, the overtime fee would be increased, so they are still losing the increase in the allowance until now. A dollar only cost 1,200 – 1,300 kyats when the daily minimum wage was set at 4,800 kyats in 2018. Six years later, in 2024, a dollar cost over 4,000 kyats, and workers are still working with 4,800 kyats. Labor activists point out that the current wage of workers; 4,800 kyats for an 8-hour day is only around one dollar. Therefore, the Solidarity of Trade Unions, Myanmar (STUM) has requested that the minimum wage be increased to 10,000 kyats in their announcement on May 1st, (134th) May Day announcement. Content: Workers from RICH PINE INTERNATIONAL GROUP LIMITED which locates at Cyber City Industrial Zone, Amman, Jordan asked the Industrial Workers’ Federation of Myanmar (IWFM) for help for not being paid in accordance with the contract but instead paid by the ticket system, being asked excessive fabric outputs, being cut and discriminated against. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing Calvin Klein , LIZ Claiborne brand shirts, pants and jackets with more than 1,000 workers. The workers are suffering health issues due to not getting enough sleep and don’t get fully paid as well. Therefore, they are informing them about returning to Myanmar but the factory asked 2,000 USD as a compensation which makes them difficult. The factory hires workers more than 400 workers from Myanmar with MoU and said that they will pay 177 Jordan Dinar per day and 1.25 Jordan Dinar per hour for overtime but in reality, they are giving with the ticket system and the workers are having to work from 8:00 am to 10:00 pm or 12:00 am. “We are affecting from health issues due to having to work 12 to 14 hours per day and the mandatory overtime which we can’t refuse. Despite calling excessive overtime, they forced us to sign a lied document saying that we only work 2 hours of overtime per hour. The citizens can go back early but forced us to work after closing the gates and we have to go back from the back door,” the workers explained.  The factory ask excessive fabric outputs that lies beyond the workers’ productivity such as 40 difficult fabric pieces per hours that leads the workers to work from 12:00 pm to 10:00 pm without allowing to have any meals in between.  Only Myanmar and Bangladesh nationals are working as seamstresses in the factory and Chinese, Urdu and Sri Lankan nationals work at other sessions and the benefits, salary and overtime fees are different. “We are cut and forced to sign a warning if we can’t finish all the demanded fabric outputs. We The supervisors are suppressing the workers and more than 50 Bangladeshi workers go back with their own flight tickets in these days. We can’t withstand and there is no one to rely,” said the worker. The ticket system payment create the tensions between the workers and supervisors according to the workers. “We are forced to work until 10:00 pm for free on the Friday which is the public holiday of Jordan on the grounds that we don’t hit the garment outputs targets. The workers who don’t work overtime are treated with malice and those who work until midnight are not paid for the morning overtime fees,” the workers said. Workers are suffering from mental and health issues after working nearly for a year and they are requesting the factory to send them back to Myanmar but the factory is asking 2,000 USD for that, saying that they took care of the workers expenses to work here with zero cost system. But workers said that the agencies already charged them around 630 USD to work there.  The HRs forced the workers to told the audits that they didn’t pay agent fees, didn’t tested urine, working only 8 hours per day and get full daily wages and overtime fees. The workers address their problem to Industrial Workers’ Federation of Myanmar – IWFM for their labor rights being violated which is against the contract and rules. 1.          To call overtime only with the workers’ consents 2.         To follow the mutual contract between employe, employer and agencies 3.         The supervisors not to verbally abuse and discriminate the workers 4.         To give full daily wages and overtime wages 5.         To let the workers enjoy the 1 hour of lunch time fully and not to assign any tasks during that time 6.         Not to force overtime for free and to pay for those free overtime with backdates.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: Dishang Fashion workers stopped the work to demanded a raise to 7,000 kyats in daily wages and to raise the overtime fees and attendance bonus as well due to the rising commodity prices which is difficult for them to cover their expenses.   The factory is located at Min Gyi Mahar Khaung Street, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township and operating with more than 1,000 workers. Currently 95 percent of the workers participated in the collective demand and the works are suspended in the cutting and finishing departments. The factory paid 4,800 kyats daily wages, 1,000 kyats daily allowance, 1,000 kyats stipend, 14,000 kyats attendance bonus and annual bonus 5,000 kyats for workers who are above 6 months of service and 25,000 kyats for those who are above a year and the expert fees are paid 400 kyats for A4, 700 kyats for A3, 900 kyats for A2 and 1,200 kyats for A1 level daily. The workers are demanding to raise to 7,000 kyats in daily wages, 1,700 kyats per hour overtime, 30,000 kyats attendance bonus and the annual bonus. “We want to cover the expenses. Currently we are in debts as we can’t cover the dorm and commodity costs. There is an interest rate in taking debt so the debt even increase more. There are many people who escape from the debt. Currently we got paid more than 300,000 kyats but we have more than 300,000 kyats debts as well. Even if we can pay the previous debt, we have to loan another and the cycle repeats,” the worker said. The workers are spending more than 70,000 kyats to more than 1 lakhs for dormitory and they can’t afford for the electricity, gas and basic foods. They are having to work around 11 hours per day, more than 80 hours of overtime per month and get paid only 350,000 only when they don’t miss a single day of work but that even cause them to fell in the debt. The worker started to demanded since May 13 and they stilled continued to work at first since the officials said that they will negotiate but two departments stopped working on May 17, as their demands are not granted. “Workers are ready to negotiate at the departments. Other factories are raising the daily wages to 7,500-8,000 kyats. The commodity price will raise even more and make the workers more difficult,” the worker said. There is no trade union in the factory but the workplace coordination committee is participating in the collective demand.  The factory is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing ONLY brand apparels. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: Workers from ETERNAL FASHION garment factory which locates at Anawrahta Baho Road, Anawrahta Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon Region said that they are having a hard time as the factory is calling excessive overtime without a day off and cutting their benefits if they refuse to. The working hours are from 8:00 am to 6:40 pm including 2 hours of overtime and they get paid 6,500 kyats daily wages, 20,000 kyats attendance bonus, 40,000 kyats for A+, 35,000 kyats for A, 35,000 kyats for B and 25,000 kyats for C grade as a  technical expert fee and they also received other bonuses, overtime fees and annual tips 2,000 kyats. “The main workplace problem is we have to work 10 hours including 2 hours of overtime. The workers are selected and forced to work overtime from 6:40 pm to 12:00 am without their consents. We have to sleep at the factory on those days and go back to house with the ferry at 5:00 am and came back on time for the next day. They don’t give the technical expert fees, if we don’t do the overtime. So, workers are working as they afraid to lose it,” the worker explained. The working hours becomes 16 hours per day if they have to work until 12 am and some workers only have 2 days off per month. Workers who don’t get paid the technical fees can’t cover the expenses so they are having to work without their consents. “We have to work 16 hours according to their orders. But we can only feed our stomach only if we work like that. So, we can’t refuse but I am wondering who would feed us if our health effected because of that excessive workload. It is said they are working overtime every day since the post Thingyan holiday and the cutting department doesn’t even have a day off and the other departments are also being selected to work overtime Any type of leave are cut by 10,000 kyats, and according to the system, the workers will almost never get any benefits except for the daily wages. “It is a huge loss after being cut according to their system weather we absent or don’t work overtime. Workers are suffering by only getting the daily wages after working tirelessly for the whole month,” said the worker. There is also drinking water impurity problems in the factory that workers wished to be solved. Workers requests are to call overtime only with their consents(not to cut technical expert fees to those who don’t work overtime), to provide purified drinking water, to grant legal leaves, not to cut the attendance bonus, to give 7,500 kyats daily wages equally to line QCs and fashion QCs.  The factory which have been operating for more than a year doesn’t have a trade union or a workplace coordination committee as a workplace dispute addressing mechanism. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing VENTMAX and MCKINLEY brand apparels. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: According to local residents of Muse, Chinese authorities arresting the migrants every day as there are few numbers of people who go back to Myanmar after crossing the China border with one week entry card such as TBP, BP via Muse It is said that those who enter with a temporary border pass must return to Musa after 7 days and must do the re-entry processes. Currently, there are many people who go to work in China from the Muse border gate but do not return after 7 days. “There are many one week entry card users who don’t come back to Myanmar after exceeding the period. So, the Chinese polices are warning that to go back to Myanmar and they would arrest if their entry permit exceeds,” said a Muse resident. It is said that some of those arrested were punished and some were sent back to Myanmar and banned from entering China for 3 to 5 years. Currently, there are hundreds of Myanmar nationals who are arrested for overstaying in China every day, and it is said that checks and arrests are being made in every neighborhood. “One week entry card user could stay for a year if their Chinese employer apply them a work permit card at the Chinese card but the employer have to guarantee for that. The other people with one week entry or passport have to comeback to Myanmar via the border gate and must apply for the entry badge again or otherwise they could be arrested,” said a Muse resident.  There were very few arrests when Myanmar nationals entered China through the border gate at the end of last year, due to the battles in Muse township but since the beginning of this year, the arrests of overstay people have increased.Chinese authorities arresting the migrants every day as there are few numbers of people who go back to Myanmar after entering China with one week entry card via Muse  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar.
