Content: The Chinese national owned Hanfex Garment Co.,Ltd which locates at 2 street, Ngwe Pinle Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon Region doesn’t appoint workers with more than 3 months of service as permanent workers and workers are losing their legal rights and leaves, according to the workers. The factory is manufacturing Page One Young brand jean pants and employs more than 700 workers which 70 of them are day laborers which most of them already have 3 months of service but not yet appointed as permanent stuff. Those workers are not entitled to legal leaves and rights and got dismissed for missing a single day of work. There is no trade union and workplace coordination committee which can address the labor disputes. “Some day laborers have 3 months of service but not appointed as permanent workers but only called when fabrics are important. And they are dismissed after that. Day laborers can’t take leave for a day even for emergency because they are fired as soon as that happens,” said the worker who don’t want to be named. It is witnessed that most garment factories in Myanmar recircuit day laborers instead of permanent ones after the coup in 2021. “All are workers whether it is day laborers or temporary laborers. The employer hire day laborers as they don’t want to give legal rights and to be able to dismiss if they want. Actually, day laborers have to be appointed as permanent after 3 months of service,” said a labor activist. There are 45 workers including the super in each cavity and they are assigned 35 jean pants per hour, The workers are verbally abused by the supers and pressurized although they worked extremely hard to finish the fabrics. The employer is also pressurizing them as no one dares to complain. “The factory denies even if the social security approves our medical leaves. We are cut although we contributed for the social security,” said the worker. The workers said that 5,000 kyats daily wages and 10,000 kyats attendance bonus are cut for missing a day of work as they are not entitled to legal leaves,” said a worker. The workers said address more difficulties such as the foreigners (Chinese nationals) directly managing them and the restrooms are not clean and they want the factory to resolve those problems. Content: Workers from TongYing garment factory which locates at Myaung Ta Kar (Phaye Khin) Industiral Zone, Mawbe Township, Yangn region said that the factory force them to work substitute for the Thingyan holidays on Sunday by pressurizing them to sign an agreement and which makes them to work 20 days continuously without an off day. The workers said that they have many things suffer as they have to work substitute on Sundays. They refuse to sign the agreement but the all supers force them in various ways. The all supers lied them that every one have signed except them and force them exactly three times. The all super said that they have to work on 11th and 12th of April and have to come with their own plan if they don’t want to sign. The workers can’t effort to come with their own plans and they want to take a leave a day as they already worked hard on the other days. “Although there is Thingyan Holiday, no one wants to work continuously for 20 days. They calls those who don’t sign and force them and we have no choice but to do that as everyone there is pressurizing us including the all supers and supers. The former factory manager always asked our consents for these issues but the current one never did,” said the worker. The workers said that they told the factory that they would work half day on Saturday without taking overtime wages instead of working on Sunday but the factory doesn’t accept. According to the knowledges of Myanmar Labour News, TONG YING HK (garment) factory is manufacturing H&M brand apparels with more than 5,000 workforce for several years. Content: A worker from Saung Oo Shwe Nay garment factory said that the factory is forcing 25 workers to manufacture 27 H&M pants and the cavity that is assigned for this task is line no.37. “Every workers from the cavity have to manufacture 4 to 5 points which is an impossible amount. Workers have to work continuously and it seems like they are exploiting us,” said line 34 super. The worker continued to say that the factory needs 50 workers normally to manufacture at this rate and for now they are not get paid the fabric fees as they can’t finish the fabrics on time due to insufficient workforce. They have already talked with the HR department about their difficulties but there is no resolvent upon this,” said a worker. “We said to reinforce with more 15 workers but they denied it and just replied to do it without any reasons. They are even planning to increase the demands,” they said. The workers said the reason they have to work is because the factory pressurized them and they have submit the current problems to the WCC team but the factory keep a blind eye. “We have reported to both the brand and the HR manager but nothing have changed. There are some cavities with around 60 workers in the factory. They can share some workers from there even if they don’t want to hire new workers. It seems that they want to abolish the cavity and want the super to resign,” said the super herself. “There is only 21 workers who work full time in line no.34 not counting the super and 3 helpers. A worker said that the factory ignore the insufficient workforce and pressurizing them. “They asked the targeted fabric on 18th of this month, I said it is not possible and the cavity manager Told me to resign. The HR too failed to reinforce us,” said the line no. 34 super. It is benefits for the factory to assign with insufficient workforce but it became a burden for the workers and it is not convenient for long term, so that the factory should reinforce the necessary workforce, said the line no.34 super. Saung Oo Shwe Nay garment factory locates at Alal Street 3,Ngwe Pin Le Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon and the factory employes more than 2,000 workers and manufacturing New Yorker’s SMOG brand, Swedish H%M and DIVIDED brand apparels.   To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: HUI YUAN garment workers said that they have to work continuously for 7 hours without a break as soon as they finished their lunch to 7:00 pm. The factory locates at Dagon Seikan Industrial Zone. “We have to work until 7:00 pm after the lunch time at 12:30 without a break. They would give 10 minutes break, if we have to work overtime until 8:30 or 9:30. But 10 minutes is not enough for us and we don’t even know how it finish. The all supers are always scolding us,” said a worker. The factory didn’t tell the workers in advance about the overtime and force them to sign to work overtime just before they were to go back home. Most workers said that they don’t want to work mid night overtime due to current situations. “They don’t tell us about the overtime in advanced and we can’t refuse it. The all supers are continuously pressurizing us and they were too rude. We are working only because it is difficult to find another job. We don’t want to work till mid night but we can’t refuse,” said the worker. 2 all supers manage the 8 cavities of the HUI YUAN garment factory and both of them verbally abuse the workers. “There were 2 all supers in the factory. One for line 1 to 4 and another for line 5 to 8. The all super who managed line 1 to 4 is too rude that it’s not even appropriate to mention how she treats us,” said a worker. The all super of line 1 to 4 collect money from the workers with the reason to donate an orphan kid. The workers thought it was going to help a worker from the factory but in fact she used those money for the depts of a worker from another department. It happened one week ago and the all super did it by calling meeting to all workers from line 1 to 4. “We gave those money as we believed it is a charity but it’s an extortion as the money is given to use for personal issue and the other question is did, she used her position for this,” questioned the workers. There are around 1000 workers in HUI YUAN garment factory and the factory is manufacturing Jackets, Leathers and Warm cloths and it is operating by foreign investments according to the information form Dica. Content: Families who have adult boys from Yangon region are having concerns as the military summons for service and reached them out through the wardens. The junta announced on 2024 February 1st that they will implement the people military service law. This raise the people insecurity followed by summons and forming military personal recircuiting committee. “The warden said that my son have to serve and I am very worry. We don’t believe them and we can’t let our son go but we have no choice. We don’t know where to fled. My mom haven’t eaten since she heard that her grandson have to serve,” said a mother from Shwe Pyi Thar while crying. The Junta announced that they will start to recircuit personal at May and men will be priorly recircuited. “How can we trust them while they said they will take someone for a while for inquires and send the dead body back. They are recircuiting young men to send frond men. They have run out of human resources so that they give young people trouble, where we can inquire or ask if we get lost connection with our son,” said a mother who have a son from Mingalar Taung Nyunt. Residents from Yangon said that men from age 18 to 35 would be summons according to the military service law and adult men and their families are having concerns. Most townships in Yangon are starting to recircuiting and men are summoned by the quarter administrative office and the guardian or parent have to give the personal data if the individual isn’t there. Many youths join the nearest revolutionaries and the migration rate is also increasing after the Junta announced the military service law. Content: The workers from Sun Good garment factory from Inn Takaw Township, Bago Region which manufactures jean pants said that the Chinese manager lady (aka Jie Jie in the place ) is introducing Chinese men to them and matchmaking them. “She is matchmaking with every pretty Burmese lady. She is doing these things secretly and calling the girl she targeted to her office and talk to her via interpreter,” said the worker. The workers said that the reason they reported the issue is because they are worried about human trafficking and by taking advantage of the current political situations. The Sun Good factory is operating for just around 5 months and it is operating with foreign investments according to the information from Dica and the workers said that the factory which manufactures its own brand have less than 100 workers which half of them are single and the others are married. Content: The stuffs from the Mo Nar Li Zar Advertisement Occupation) Door to Door Marrketing company said that their wages and labors are exploited and they get paid very few. The business is locates at Bago Bus Stop, Bago Road, 11 Ward, Haling Thar Yar Township. “The working hours starts at 10:00 am and we have to walk to townships that we promote and get back only at 8:00 pm. We got back only at 11:00 pm if we have to go to rural areas and have to rest only at 1:00 am after finshing the documents,” said a sales stuff. The sales stuffs only have 2 holidays per week and they also have to take care of the employers’ personal stuffs at the morning. Currently there are 20 stuffs including male, female and LGBTQs. “They woke up us at 6:00 and force us to do house works such as cooking, cleaning and car washing and go out for sales only at 10:00 am,” said the worker. The business distributing shampoos, beauty products and fat loss medicine with their own brands and selling at Yangon and Ayawaddy region with door to door system. “They force the stuffs to hit the target. If not stuffs have to buy those products with their own money which cost 10 of thousands. We have already signed that the employer would not force us to buy the products,” said the workers. The workers are staying in the workplace and it’s a situation where they can’t refuse to sign. The transportation fees are also cut from their salary as well. “They give us 2,000 transportation fees if we can sell and if not 3,500 is deducted. At least 10 days per month. Some were deducted for 3 or 4 months continuously which makes them to run away from the job,” a sales stuff explained. There are having difficulties for personal expenses in addition to support the families due to several deductions. And the business have more working hours and less holidays than other jobs which doesn’t help the personal development of the workers any at all,” said the stuff. “The products are expensive and most people can’t effort it. Most sales stuffs don’t hit the targets and have many days which are deducted which makes them even to not have a penny to spend. There are only 2 holidays per month and the working hours are too late which makes us unable to do any personal developments and lost our future,” said the workers. The company doesn’t explain them about the deduction before hiring and the employer confiscate the workers’ NRC and ID cards. There is no employment contract and labor cards are not also asked on recircuiting.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: ZHEJIANG NEWWAY(MYANMAR) GARMENT (previously SEN YU CLOTHINGS (MYANMAR) which locates at Bamaw Atwin Wun Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon is demanding 250 fabric pieces from the workers in 10 working hours, according to their workers. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and operating with more than 1,000 workers and doesn’t have a trade union and workplace coordination committee to address workplace disputes. The factory is manufacturing XSIDE brand Japanese jackets. The wages in the factory are 5,800 kyats for 8 working hours a day, 1,400 kyats overtime per day, 20,000 kyats attendance bonus per month, the expert fees are 40,000 kyats for grade A, 30,000 kyats for grade B and 20,000 kyats for C. “The main violation is asking the impossible fabric amount from the workers such as 25 fabric per hour for an cavity from 8:00 am to 7:00 pm which makes 250 fabric per day and the supers together with the foreigners verbally abuse us if we can’t finish the fabrics,” said a worker who don’t want to be named. The workers said that they don’t get medical and casual leaves in the factory and attendance bonus 20,000 kyats and expert fees are cut for missing a day of work. “They cut our attendance bonus even if we take a gate pass for a certain issue. The foreigner intimidated that they would cut our expert fees even if our causal leaves approved,” said the workers. “Workers from other departments have to work all evening or all night without their consents and those are around 10 days per month. The workers are unsatisfied as they don’t get paid overtime wages and other benefits fully,” said the worker. The workers said that their requests to the factory are to ask only the possible fabric outputs from them, the foreigners not to manage them directly and verbally abuse, not to cut attendance bonus and expert fees for taking legal leaves, the supervisors not to verbally abusee the workers, to provide safety measures and heat and cold balance coordination in the factory, to pay the overtime wages fully and to call overtime only with their consents. Content: Workers from KBL garment factory which manufacture DAVID'S BRIDAL and celebrate bride dress said that they are still facing right abuses even after the labor office had come to inspect due to the news reported. Myanmar Labour News have uploaded a news on 26th February that the KBL garment factory is calling overtime until midnight and supervisors are verbally abusing the workers. The workers said the coalition of officials came to inspect on March 1, but the abuse are still on going. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and locates at Industrial Zone (1), Kyan Sit Thar Street, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon Region and there is no trade union or workplace coordination committee to address the workplace disputes. The working hours are from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm and the overtime is until 9:00 or 11:00 pm and the workers are having concerns due to the current political situations. The workers negotiated not to call overtime until midnight but the supers refuse and intimidate them that they will be fined with no overtime at all for a month and workers have no choice but to continue doing the overtime due to the livelihood. The workers said that they reported to the news outlet to seek resolve for the abuse but its not currently what they except yet. “The factory taught some workers in advance how to answer the inspectors’ questions and only 3 workers from each cavities are asked and the workers answered as they are taught by the manager,” said a worker. The workers are called overtime on the peasants’ day (March 2) and on Sunday although the inspection have done. “We sometimes work to 8:00 or 11:00 pm and also on peasants’ day and Sundays. The managers and super visors said that the inspecting team said that overtime is legal if both employer and employee agree. I believe that the inspecting team and the employer together suppressing us,” said a worker. The fabric fees are also exploited such as only the workers who are comfortable with the supers are get paid instead of the workers’ who worked hard at the end of the month while issuing the fabric fees. The workers said that they are unsatisfied with this decisions. “We want to request to issue the salary at around 4:00 pm on the pay day and it is not convenient to get paid late. We want to get back home early on the pay days and there are many thieves are robbers on the street due to the current political situations,” said the worker. Content: The workers from WHN garment factory which locates at Sayar San Street, Industrial Zone 2, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region said that they don’t have employment contract with the factory and their rights are being violated. The factory which is owned by a Chinese national is operating with around 500 workers and there is no trade unions and workplace coordination committee in the factory. The factory is manufacturing ET VOUS, PROMOD. CALLOPE and PUNT brand jackets and pants. The working hours are set as from 8:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. with an addition of 2 hours of overtime but in reality, the workers have to work overtime from 9:00 p.m. to 12:00 p.m. which cause them difficulties. “The night overtimes are optional and workers consents are not asked. They don’t call the whole factory but they select those they want. We don’t want to work due to the political situations but we have no right to say no. They provide the overtime workers a bus but the workers only return to home at 10:00 p.m. We have to sleep in the factory on the days we work until 12 and go back home at 4:00 and came back in the morning after having a bath,” said the workers. The workers also that these overtimes are called illegally as they have to hide in the garage when the inspectors came in. “We have to work overtime for free until 9:00 if we have many fabrics to kept and fix. On Sundays, we don’t get paid for overtime wages even if we finished fixing the fabrics,” the workers said. The workers said that they are having concerns due to having to work until midnight and they also explained how they suffer and how their health are affected for having to work until midnight. The factory asks for fabric outputs which is beyond their productivity and the all supers and supers verbally abuse them if they can’t finish which makes them working in a place where they are morally downgraded. They are not entitled to medical leaves and legal benefits although they have been contribute for the social security and daily wages, attendance bonus and expert fees are cut for a single day of absent. “We don’t get any legal benefits and medical leaves. There are around 500 workers but there is neither nurse nor medic clinic. The toilets are also dirty and damaged. Content: Jiashihao Myanmar Limited workers said that the factory cut the social security fees from their wages every month but they can’t take social security leaves and other leaves as well and they are also asked to manufacture excessive fabric outputs. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and operating at Khaya Street, Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone 1 with more than 1,000 workers. Workers have to pay 2,200 kyats per month as a social security fees and they go to the social security clinic with their own plans for health issues. Although the clinic give them medical certificate to take leave the factory doesn’t recognize it and cut their wages. “We are not entitled to not only medical leaves but also other leaves such as casual leave. The officials don’t permit us to take leave for emergency reasons and cut daily wages 5,600 kyats and attendance bonus 10,000 kyats and other expert fees from out salary,” said the worker. They are also asked excessive fabric outputs and a cavity with 30 workers including the supervisors have to manufacture 60 jacket per hour. That rate equals to 480 jackets for a day with 8 working hours which can be noted as a worker have to manufacture 16 jackets per day but the wages they get paid are only 5,800 kyats per day including the 1,000 kyats stipend from the government. “We even have to work overtime 2 hours to cover our expenses. We have to work 10 hours a day,” said a female worker who don’ want to be named. The worker said the fabric outputs are unfairly asked from the factory officials and the supervisors such as all supers and supers verbally abuse them while asking for it and the workers who made quality failed fabric have to sign a warning despite how hard they worked. “Expert fees are set as 50,000 kyats for A, 40,000 kyats for B and 20,000 kyats for C but those who are convenient with the supers and all supers get paid instead of those who really proficient. These are discriminations and we also don’t have enough dinning tables which make us eat uncomfortably,” said the worker. The workers also explained that there is no trade union to address the workplace disputes. The workers said that they want to request to give then legal benefits and leaves, to only ask the fabric outputs which are inline with their productivity, to reinforce required man power in the cavities and the all supers and supers to not verbally abuse. Content: According to the workers, KB Microfinanace Myanmar Co,LTD which locates at No(9), Kamayut Township, Yangon district does not pay them overtime wages. The company is earning by loan business for those who went to go and work at South Korea and having around 30 suboffices through out the whole countries in townships and cities such as Than Lyin, Tharkayta, North Oakkalar, Hlaing Thar Yar, Shwe Pyi Thar, Tuntwe, Mandalay, Mone Ywar, Mudon, Nay Pyi daw, Hinthada, Taungoo, Kyaut Sae, Dawei, Taunggyi, Magwe, Singue, Pyinmanar, Salin and other townships and employes more than 600 workers. Although the company is earning with the loan businesses, the workers are exploited by forcing to work overtime for free. The company force the workers to work beyond the legal working hours and the working hours of the drivers are from 6:00 Am to 6:00 pm and they only get paid overtime fees only if their working hours exceeds a total of 12 hours. The drivers are told to sign the contract which states that the working hours are 12 hours a day and the salary is 250,000 kyats per hour and the workers who signed said that it was happened as they didn’t know the law very well. “It was not like this before. It changes after the coup d’tect,” said the worker. They don’t have to work for 12 hours a day before the coup and their overtime wages are also paid regularly but the company made changes since after the coup. Content: Garment workers from Dongxin Garment factory are working 10 or 12 hours a day and all night overtime although the labor law stated the legal working hours as 8 hours a day and they don’t even get paid the overtime wages yet. The factory locates at Nawaday Street, Industrial Zone 3, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region. It is owned by a Chinese national and operating with more than 700 workers but neither trade union nor workplace coordination committee are formed. “The working hours are from 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. and an addition of two hours of overtime. We have to work the whole day including all night but we get paid for only two hours of overtime and not get paid for the rest and neither for the Sundays,” said the workers. The factory asks fabric output together from the seamstresses and the workers together based on the daily wages and force to work them until they get fabric fee of 6,600 kyats a day. “The seamstresses and the helpers have to work until they get the fabric fees of 6,600 kyats and they have to work until the midnight, dawn or even on Sundays if they can’t finish as some outside fabrics also includes,” the worker explained. The workers are having difficulties to finish the fabric outputs and demanded rates and they can’t even tell the factory that they want the overtime wages due to certain circumstances. There is no one to consult their difficulties as there is no workplace disputes coordination teams that makes us them being pressurized. The workers are also not allowed to take the legal gate passes. The day laborers hired in the factory don’t get the same benefits as the permanent workers although they are assigned the same tasks and the same working hours. The overtimes the factory is calling are also not approved by the respective labor offices but just by the employer, all supers and the supers. There is no reception and medic clinic in the factory and the employer does not take responsibility for the workers’ workplace accidents. The factory is operating for just more than a year and manufacturing Windcore brand jackets. 1.      To give the wages for overtime and also to pay with backdates for the previous ones. 2.      To appoint the day laborers as permanent workers. 3.      To provide a medic clinic and to take responsibility for the workers’ risk on way back home To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. In addition, the factory recircuits from 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. and those who aren’t doing well are dismissed. The Chinese authorities are also arresting those who are working with one week ticket and only a few amount of one week card holders are permit to enter due to the news that a criminal had fled to China.  But a Muse local who is a Philanthropy team member said that those with passports are given priority to enter China. Those who get a one-time entry card to China since February 26,27 are not permitted to enter China until March 3. Those who entered with one-time use card before was allowed to stay a year with the recommendation letter of the employee. For now, Burmese workers and locals warn not to come China as there were no more QR submission processes. Content: Workers from Jiashihao (Myanmar) factory explained their damages as the factory does not allow the workers who returned home to issue salary with someone on behalf of the workers. And workers who resigned are also allowed to take the salary by their selves only 10 days after of a month and workers are having damages for these facts/ “We lost 2 lakhs as we have to get wages for 15 days and there are 40 people who resigned in February and the total wages may be around 80 lakhs. It is not a small amount for the factory and also a valuable amount for us. It would cover our travel expenses and we can gift our family if we get more,” said a worker who resigned from Jiashihao garment factory.  Resigned workers are now at their home town and not being easy to come back to Yangon due to the investigations around the way and an labor activist said that workers can report to Department of Factory and General Labor Law Inspection regarding issuing the salary with representative. “Department of Factory and General Labor Law Inspection is responsible for the wages, so that workers could report to them. There were help in previous months regarding the matters with the copies of IDs. If it doesn’t help, they could seek for help from the lawyers who are helping. The amount is quite large so that they should,” said the activist. The workers resigned from the factory in the mid of February after the military service law came out, confirmed by a worker from Jiashihao (Myanmar) factory. Most workers who went back to home town are female workers. “I just arrived back fortunately as I was not arrested and not died yet, our houses told us to came back because of the conscription news in Yangon, so that us, who want to go back home went back together,” said the worker. Jiashihao (Myanmar) factory is recircuiting 500 workers as many workers had resigned and a worker said there are discriminations in the factory and they don’t get access to casual and seniority leaves. “Only those who are confident with the superiors get leave and the others don’t. Seniority leaves are also refused as they told that they have already given the equivalent money for it,” said the worker. The Jisashihao (Myanmar) Limited garment factory locates at Khyay Street, Industrial Zone (1), Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon division and operating with around 1,200 workers and manufacturing ZARA, LIDL, NEW WAY, GINA, JABP and OTTO brand fabrics. Content: The factory manufacturing Japanese CINEMA CLUB fabric brands is operating with ticket system and the allowance stipulated by government is not given if the workers can’t finish fabrics equivalent to 100,000 kyats by the ticket and the workers said that they are asked excessive outputs. The factory is the Chinese national owned factory called \(Myanmar)Co.,L.td factory which locates at Wun Htauk Street, Shwe Lin Ban industrial zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon division. There are more than 3,000 workers in the factory and there is no trade union nor workplace coordination committee to address the workplace disputes. The working hours are from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and the workers said they have to work until 6:40 p.m. if the factory called overtime. The benefits are 4,800 kyats for daily wage, 30,000 kyats allowance per month, 10,000 kyats attendance bonus and they don’t get the attendance bonus if they can’t manufacture fabrics with ticket system equivalent to 100,000 kyats. “The employer asked impossible fabric outputs from the workers in the name of fabric fee. The fabric standards are raised day by day and the supers verbally abuse during those times and those who manufacture small points never reached the 100,000 target,” said the worker. The workers said that most workers don’t get the 30,000 kyats allowance bonus as but finished with the daily wages. The foreigners are directly managing the workers in the workplace and attendance bonus is also cut for taking leave. “The supers pressurized us to work on Sundays with the reason of having quality failed fabrics and force us without giving overtime fee and we neither have the chance to refuse as they always find mistakes from us to make us sign warnings and dismiss us. We are working with wariness although it is a factory job,” said the worker. The workers said that they want to request the supervisors and supers not to verbally abuse the workers, the foreigners not to directly manage the workers, to give 30,000 kyats allowance to every workers, to ask only the possible fabric amount from the workers, not to cut attendance bonus for taking legal leaves and gate pass, to call overtime with the workers’ consents and to pay the overtime wages in accordance with the law. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: The foreign embassies restrict visa applications as they were more people who want to leave Myanmar after the Junta announce the mandatory military service law. The Embassy of Japan also announced the stoppage of hotline visa application due to excessive visa application and will accept only by the emails. In Addition, there are many people who go to China with one week entry ticket and there are restrictions too. The amount of people who went to go abroad increase after the military conscription news are stipulated and those who have financial difficulties also go to neighboring country Thailand, illegally. Content: The workers from Myanmar Sunview Garment (Solamoda Group) factory which locates at Min Aeyar Street, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township said that the factory is abusing labor rights by asking excessive fabric output, forcing to work for free in Sundays and not giving access to leaves. There are more than 800 workers in the factory and there are neither trade union nor workplace coordination committee. The brands manufacturing currently are SERVO brands fabrics. The workers said that the factory called overtime until 8:30 for the whole January 2024 and until 6:30 p.m in February and the all supers are verbally abusing the workers if they don’t finish the outputs they asked excessively. “The cavity feels like a hell and some workers even accidently hit their hand with needle only if they hear their voice, look how rude are they,” The workers have to submit application to supers and all supers whether leave or gate pass they would take and they are not get easily as they worried about the standards. “They give leave when we asked from the managers directly and later all supers made us difficult to take leave and they give us only when those who understands the labor law among us said we would report,” said the worker. The workers also said they want back date calculation for the Sunday overtime fees as they were not paid before. “The manager promotes the workers those who are comfortable with them and demote after 3 months if he doesn’t like. Actually, he should consider first before promotion because workers who demoted will find difficult to work. There is no one to resolve these situations,” said the worker. The workers said that they want to request to give Sunday overtimes with a back date, to check all requirements before promotion and not to demote after promoted, to give gate pass easily if they have proper reason and the officials to restrict the all supers and supers from verbal abuse,” said the workers. Content: The ministry of labour announced that the migrant workers from Myanmar who are living without document in Thailand could apply for Certificate of Identification from February 23 to the end of October. Currently there are five CI issuing camps in Thailand each locates at Pathum Thani, Samut Prakan, Samut Sakhon, Chon Buri and Surat Thani districts and there will also be mobile units in Chiang Mai, Nakhon Sawan and Songkhla districts. “Workers should process himself to not have to give more than it would cost. Don’t submit via the agents. We have to look the ground situations and there are too many Burmese who came illegally and many scummers agents too who are cooperating with the stuffs,” said a Burmese from Thailand. The ministry of Labour would ask for the income tax in addition of the CI fees. Those who applied at February 2024 have to give 600 THB income tax for 2023 October to 2024 January and the CI fee 710 THB, a total of 1310 THB. Those who would apply in March and later than March have to pay the CI fee 700 THB and income tax 750 THB and it would take 150 THB for a month later. The labor activist from Thailand said that many Myanmar nationals entered illegally to Thailand after the coup and the number of arrests are also increasing. Content: The Union Minister U Myint Naung of the Minister of Labour said that they had formed a monitoring team to resolve the labor right abuses expressed in domestic and foreign labour news outlets. He said this on February 22, when the officials of the UMFCCI and the charges of the industrial zone committees. The media are writing labor right abuse news as the workers are abused after the coup and it becomes a gate of bribery for the officials instead of inspecting the workplaces that are reported, said by a labor journalist. “We posted news about the workers’ damages and some factories got resolvent and some factories weren’t inspected at all. Some were inspected but nothing changed. They inspected in seek of bribery,’ said a labor news reporter. The ministry refused continuously for 3 years in the SAC’s media but the labor right abuses are raising year by year according to the Myanmar Labour News’ annual summary data. The workers have to work overtime without their consents, not entitled to legal leaves, cut their benefits, and force labor are also being witnessed. “There were trade unions before and we were dare to report any illegal things but we expect nothing for now. The factory would even know who reported them to the ministry. They discriminated those who reported and moved them to other departments and the worst is those workers had to resign finally,” said a garment worker. It is like a situation that the news of labor right abuses are exposed to the public only if the news outlets expressed them due to the arrested and oppression of the Junta upon the Unions, Federations and their leaders and members. “We told them how to write report if the workers don’t know back in those days. We educate them about their rights but we can’t live in Myanmar anymore for now. The workers have more fear than before too. The local and international community would only know the labor right abuses only if the news outlets are keep updating,” said a labor activist. It is also known that the ministry of labor uploaded their actions upon the factories and workshop which violate the labor laws after field inspection. Content: Myanmar Yong Jia Garment Color Correction color painting business from Nawaday villa, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon reappointed 7 workers who are dismissed for not working overtime. The employer dismissed those 7 workers on February 20th and 21st due to not working overtime. “The employer had to reappoint all 7 of them as they said they would return to workplace. The employer also provide the interim damages for the times when they are away from work,” said the supporters. 5 workers who explained that it is difficult to work overtime on February 20th when the workers are called overtime until 20:00 p.m. are dismissed and 2 more workers who are associated with them are dismissed again on February 21st. According to the sources, the employer said they do not want the workers who don’t follow his orders and said the workers should apologize and give 50,000 kyats for fine if they want to be reappointed. And this month will be also given for only 20 days,” said the workers. The dismissed workers and the employer negotiated again and got the resolvents to get back to the workplace and to give interim damages. Content: Workers from Full Way garment factory which locates at No 83, Min Ayar Street, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region said that they are not get paid notice fee for 1 month and the seniority wages and 197 workers are get paid only damages and February’s wages. They told that the factory would close only for a month starting January 1st and only the allowance and basic salary for January is given in February 5th and the workers were called in February 28th with the reason to pay the wages but instead pay the closure damages. “They told that those who don’t come between 10:00 to 12:00 will not be given and they give the damages instead when we arrive. They give only the basic wages for 6 months for workers with more than 9 years of service. They don’t give any other benefits. We lost our seniority and notice wages and the government officials also told us to satisfy with what we got in the hard times,” said the workers. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing sub orders from other factories although it was a factory that operates with its own orders. “They don’t give annual leave in previous years with the reasons of much orders. We got only 170,000 kyats in the last issued salary. The total numbers of workers are 197. We had worked during the annual leave for free in previous years. It is a great lost for us. Although we are not satisfied with the calculation of basic salary in the damages we have just to accept it as we can’t do anything,” said the workers. More than 150 workers in the factory are women and some of them are married women and pregnant women. There are many senior workers in the factory and a worker with 9 years of service is given only 1,100,000 kyats including February and damages for 6 months. The workers said the amount of damage is only enough for a worker who worked 10 years to spend only for 3 months and they would find difficulty to find a new job due to their age. The workers also sent mails to official departments via WCC to get the seniority and notice fees. “I spent 9 years here and get paid only 11 lakhs of damages. I think the factory is unfair upon the workers. The workers spent years and they should be given according to their seniority. The owner didn’t come himself but sent a representative. The labor office cannot resolve these problems. There are laws if we do any mistakes but where are for employers,” said the worker. Content: A garment worker from Mountain Tree factory which locates near A Lal village, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone said that the Chinese woman who is the factory charge is treating rudely upon them. The factory have around 300 workers and 6 transportation bus which is not sufficient for the workers. The factory have been operating for 3 or 4 months and does not have EC contract with the workers. “The charge woman physically assaulted us by throwing with nearby things in addition of verbally abused them since the working hour starts,” the worker explained. “Workers are called overtime from 8:00 pm and 11:00 pm and called overtime after 11:00 too. The workers have to go back with their plans as the factory does not provide transportation. All workers here are being abused. Overtimes are called without our consents and they even recircuited on Sundays sometimes. Although we are working due to our livelihoods, there is no worker who is not frustrate and afraid in every morning to go to work due to the excessive verbally abuse. The interpreter is also taking our photos to report to the officials,” said the worker. The workers also said that the interpreter is taking their photos to report them to the officials. The Mountain Tree factory is manufacturing Japanese fabrics and it is operated on foreign investments according to the data from DICA. Content: Workers from Myanmar solamoda Sunrun  said they can’t go back home as they are recircuited for excessive overtime nearly every day. The workers have to sleep on the working desk in the factory with odor blankets. The factory is locates near Kyawl Da Nyin Kone village, City Bypass road, Bago Industrial Zone. “The factory recircuits overtime until 11:00 p.m since December and workers don’t want to work due to security concerns these days. Furthermore, they are also forced to work until 3:00 am of Sunday after working the whole day in Saturday. The transportations arrived only at 5 and the workers who live far get back home at 7:00 am after taking the ride for more than an hour. They provide only lunch on overtime days and there is no breakfast nor meal break from 12:30 to 18:30. They have to work from 7:00 am to 11 pm after working a half hour break. Some workers were in tears as some Chinese in the cavity verbally abused. The QC workers are also demoted to shaving department and some workers are also forced to leave without damages. The workers said they want the violations to get expose to public. Myanmar solamoda Sunrun factory have 3 sub factories and the violations are occurring in No 3 sub factory which is from Bago. Content: There are news that the New Way shoe factory which operates at Kyan Sit Thar Street, Industrial Zone 4, Hlaing Thar Yar Township is going to move to another place and the workers seek the damages for those who can’t follow. The factory have been operating for 11 years and said they are going to move to War Ta Yar Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar and workers who can follow can follow and those who can’t will not be given any damages, the manager said. “There was a change of employer in 2023 but the workers didn’t know and they just found out that due to this issue. The factory said they would not move when we reported in 2023 and they are going to do it again now. They are pressurizing the workers to not have to pay those who can’t follow. Some workers have left and those with 10 years of service are also still working in the factory. The ones who can lead the workers are always fired and so there is no one here anymore.” said the worker. “The factory force us to take 10 days of annual leave when we are nearly reaching the target month of seniority. The workers can’t explain that they just want to take only if they need. We still don’t know clearly whether they will move or not and making the workers who can’t follow to leave by causing them stresses. The factory hired day laborers until this February and does not appoint us permanent although they have services from 3 months to 8 months and they are not accessed to any benefits 30 day laborers are fired without any damages. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing adidas shoes before 2024 and currently manufacturing Reebok brand with more than 400 workers. Although there is a workplace coordination committee, workplace disputes are not addressed. The workers said that their requests are to give damages to the workers who can’t follow when the factory move, to appoint the workers who can follow the same position as before, to give seniority leaves when need for those workers with more than 3 months of service and to permit the workers to take leave. The factory’s overtime is only until 7:00 p.m but the workers have to work until 7:30 due to counting the snack time. There fore the workers only arrive back home at 9 as the cars started to leave the factory only at 8:00. “I don’t know there the factory owners know or not but the Manager Daw Mya Mya Htwe scolded the workers today (February 28) for not working overtime yesterday (February 27),” said a worker. Tianjin Fashion Milestone factory which locates at Seik Kan Thar Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon  and it is manufacturing Sinsay and VERO MODA brand fabric with more than 1,000 workers and owned by a Chinese national. Content: BOFEI GARMENT Co.,ltd workers said that they want resolvent in accordance with the law upon the issue regarding the factory dismiss the day laborers illegally just before the brand representees came to inspect due to labor right abuses and hire new day laborers after that. The workers from BOFEI GARMENT Co.,ltd which locates at the intersection of Seik Kan Thar Street and Mya Taung Wun Gyi U Mo Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region said that the inspectors from the brand came to inspect after the factory is reported in the media for labor right abuse. The factory dismissed more than 40 day laborers without prior notice just before the inspection team came and those workers have damages as they already have more than 3 months of service and the workers are seeking resolvent upon that. The factory is a Chinese national owned factory which is manufacturing page one brand apparel with more than 400 workers and no trade union nor work place coordination team is formed in the factory. “The factory is reported in January for labor right abuse and they fire more than 40 day laborers in advance just before the brand’s representatives come regarding the matter. And they also pretrained the workers to tell the inspectors only the well-being about the factory. Actually, there are too many violations and nothing changed although the inspectors came in. They even hire more day laborers than before,” said the worker. The workers also said the drinking water is not purified and it have rust odors. The working hours are from 7:30 a.m. to 18:30 a.m. and they can’t refuse the all evening and all night overtimes that are called without prior notice. The workers said “Those who refuse to work overtime are discriminated against. They hold much grudges even to fire from the work and we don’t get access to the social security although we contribute in the social security and neither leave permit for health issue even if the social security clinic is permitting. It cost daily wage 5,600 kyats and attendance bonus 10,000 kyats for us to take a day off,” said the worker. The workers said that they want to appeal to resolve social security leave and medical leave matters, to resolve the case of dismissing the day laborers without prior notice and to provide purified drinking water.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: According to the workers from Handa garment factory which locates at the intersection of U Shwe Bin Street and U Myue Street, there are labor right abuses in the factory The factory is manufacturing BURTLE brand shirt and bras with around 3,000 work force and the WCC never stood with the workers. “Although the HR department said workers from HR department can took leave, the supers and all supers never give a leave but instead call 4 hours of overtime every day. The workers also have to work until 20:30 and only given for 2 hours when the salary is issued but the other two hours are given immediately and not displayed which is violating the labor rights,” said the worker. “They were calling all night overtimes and just changed to 8:30 pm just after the inspection team came. And they are asking impossible fabric outputs for the workers and those who finished are forced free overtime and if they refuse they will be discriminated. The supers from line (2), Daw Phyu Phyu and Daw Win Thander Hlaing are the worst. The pregnant workers are also forced for overtime and hided when the inspectors came in. The water provided by the factory is not purified and not sufficient which make the workers have to drink basin water and the toilets are also having ad odors and it becomes worse in the evening as they don’t provide the toilet water anymore and the factory turns a blind eye on such issues,” said the workers. Although the government have instructed to give the allowance of 1,000 kyats the employer is still not giving it to those who doesn’t finish the fabrics. And the Chinese experts are also pressurizing the supers and leaders to force more on the workers which leads to the verbal abuses of the supers and all supers. “It looks like they are making the workers life more difficult as the all supers intimidate to fire if we report, force us to work overtime on public holidays if we can’t finish the outputs which forbids the workers who are studying for personal developments,” the workers said about their feelings. Currently, they are having to work overtime on holidays as a substitute for Thingyan holidays. They have to work until 18:00 on Saturdays without being asked for their consents. “We have to work on February 11, 2024 Sunday for substitute of Thingyan holiday and its until 18:00. We want the officials to resolve the issues regarding the abuses,” the workers seek for help. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: Workers from RAINBOWTEC MYANMAR Manufacture Co.Ltd which locates at U Htun Nyo street, Industrial zone (2), Yangon said that the factory officials denied their leaves and cut nealy 30,000 kyats of their wages. “We are not entitled to any types of leaves. Daily wages 5,800 kyats, attendance bonus 20,000 kyats, fabric fee 4,000 kyats; a total of 29,800 kyats are cut,” said the workers. The RAINBOWTEC MYANMAR Manufacture Co.Ltd is owned by a Chinese national with and employes more than 1,000 workers and manufacturing TORRINGTON brands. There are workers with slightly over 15 years old and the current problems are  not having purified water and clean toilets. “They don’t give a reason or inquire something if they want to dismiss. They just fire us illegally,” said a worker. The workers are not told how much ticket fee they would got per fabric point and can’t ask about it too. “Those who sew big points are paid lesser than those sew smaller ones. The supers give more to the workers who are comfortable with them. The supers give them the fabrics their sewing and they divide the salaries,” said a worker. The ticket system should be transparent to the workers but the RAINBOWTEC MYANMAR garment factory officials do not follow it and exploiting the workers. The workers have to sign a warning when they sew a qualitied failed fabric although they are carefully trying their best to manufacture qualified fabrics. “The line 3, 7 and 11 supers are really rude and verbally abuse the workers while asking for fabric outputs. They publicly humiliated the workers that can only produce a little output and force them to do more,” said a worker. They are not able to enjoy the full 30 minutes of dining time as the supers force them to finish quickly. In addition of seamstress works, the workers are being exploited by being assigned to do janitorial work only after the working hours (18:30) The RAINBOWTEC MYANMAR Manufacture Co.Ltd workers said that they want to get assess to legal casual and medical leaves and their further requests are not to dismiss the workers illegally, the supers to not verbally abuse by name and not to assign janitorial works after the working hours. So that, we have no choice but to do,” said the workers. Salary is issued twice a month with half amount per once and the overtime wages beyond 18:30 are given at the end of the month. The wages other two hours of overtime is given after the next 5 days. Workers are asked for fabric outputs which exceeds than their productivity and the all supers and supers are verbally abusing them to meet that. Legal leaves are access only after being scolded. The workers seeks for reducing the overtime to 18:30 and only let those who have consents to work until mid-night, to give legal leaves, to assign only the possible amounts to them, not to force them and verbally abuse them. KBL Garment factory is a factory owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing DAVIDS BRIDAL and Studio brands bride dresses. LAT WAR GARMENT (2) factory locates in Min Dahti Street, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region and operating with 800 workers for manufacturing CR brand pants. The factory hires a lot of youths and day laborers with 3,600 kyats for 8 working hours. The day laborers who have service of more than 3 months are also not appointed as permanent stuffs and some are layoff. The supers and all supers are verbally abusing the workers if they cannot finish the fabrics they are unfairly assigned to. “There are 22 workers in a cavity including the supers. The GOOD brand is asked 30 fabric per hour and they don’t reduce the workloads considering the absents. We have to work overtime until 8:30 pm to finish the fabrics. We are worrying for having to go back late due to the military conscription news,” said the workers. The toilets and drinking waters in the factory that the workers are using are also not clean and purified. Content: A worker from U BEAUTY CO,LTD which locates at Ayar Street, Hlaing Thar Yar Industrial Zone (5), Yangon Region said that they are working without protective equipment in the factory due to their livelihoods. “The workplace is very dangerous. Some wigs have to be cleaned with acid to make them washable. We have to use academy rust remover for that. The factory does not provide us with the safety equipment. They only give a thin glove and mask but not the glasses. We have to smell the noxious odors while washing which makes our eyes burn, vomit and skin avulsed. It is very dangerous,” said the worker. The U BEAUTY CO,LTD is owned by a Chinese national and operating with more than 30 workers for more than a year but the trade union and the WCC haven’t formed yet. Most workers are day laborers and they are not guaranteed to be appointed as permanent stuffs even after working for 2 months but layoff with no reason. The day laborers only get paid 150,000 kyats per month and the permanent workers from 200,000 to 220,000 kyats. There is no slip for the salary and no contribution to the social security as well. The workers are not entitled to leaves in addition of being scolded by the factory owner who is managing the business their selves. Content: Workers from Dishang Kenny Garment factory which locates on Min Mahar Min Kaung Street, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zoen, Hlaing Thar Yar Township told that they are having to work 16 hours a day. Dishang Kenny Garment factory is a factory of a Dishang Group and the working hours are from 7:00 to 23:00. The owner is a Chinese national and manufacturing SEASON REASON by Lin&Red, RESERVED and CLOSSHI brand fabrics. “They force overtimes without the workers’ consents. They force us daily from 16:00 to 23:00. And force the workers to sleep in the factory to work again the next day at the same schedule,” explained the workers. The workers have to work overtime until 17:00 and also on the Sunday off day. The workers who refuse to work overtime are discriminated and treated with malice and the factory officials fire them as well. Most workers are also having health issues because of excessive overtime without casual and medical leaves. Their daily wages (5,800) kyats, attendance bonus (20,000) kyats and grade bonus depends on the levels are cut for taking a leave. Although grade levels are set, only the workers who are comfortable with the supers and all supers are getting it and day laborers who have been working for 3 months to 2 years are not employed as permanent workers which make them suffer from legal rights. The workers also said they are being asked for the impossible fabrics which the supers and all supers are verbally abusing them if not finish making them work overtime for free to finish those. In addition to the free overtime, the workers are also having concerns and feeling unsafe in everywhere due to the military conscription news of the military. Dishang Kenny workers said that they want to request the factory not to verbally abuse, call overtime without their desires, not to discriminate and hold grudges and to pay for their labor for overtime. Content: A labor activist told Myanmar Labor News that the chief of the office of labor guidance ask that what the workers suffer for the fake signature, regarding the factory use worker’s fake signature in the EC contracts. WEI HUA (Myanmar) Garment Co.,Ltd and a female worker seek for resolvent in the office of Department of Labour in Shwe Pyi Thar Township, as the later was fired and cheated on her signature. A supporting team member said that the chief told that fake signature doesn’t cause the worker anything when they have the last negotiation on February 20th. “He shouldn’t ask what the worker suffer regarding the employer cheat their signature. Its not in accordance with the law. They can’t decide whether the worker suffer or not, their duty is just to resolve the dispute,” said the supporting member. The chief of the office of labor guidance is responsible for checking the EC contract whether it is in accordance with the Employment and Professional Development Act or if both the parties had already agreed. WEI HUA (Myanmar) Garment Co.,Ltd force the workers who are worrying about the conscription law to work until 20:00. A worker said “They recircuit beyond the law as there are new orders in the factory and we are afraid to work due to the conscription. But the all supers and supers told us not to come in the next day if we can’t work overtime.” An inspecting came to WEI HUA (Myanmar) Garment Co.,Ltd on February 8th but the factory had already selected the workers to answer and continue to violate the laws after the inspection. They reported to the labor office as the factory continue to call for overtime and the factory finish the overtime while the inspecting team came to check at 19:30 on February 20th.  “We came back at 19:30. The inspecting team is around 10 people. They found out how are we being forced of overtime. I don’t know which action would they take,” said the worker. The Wai Hua Myanmar garment factory located at Kanaung Min Thar Gyi Street, Industrial Zone (1), Shwe Pyi Thar Township and owned by a Chinese national. The factory is operating with around 600 workers and manufacturing MOHITO. Hgtncalif, Hang Ten, Cortefiel and Hanure brand fabrics. Content: According to the workers, some workers from Asdet garment factory which locates in Yaw Atwin Wun U Phoe Hlaing Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region who reported about forced overtime, legal leaves and benefits abuses and physical abuses are dismissed. “The manager said she don’t care whether we report to anywhere. Recently, the officials from the office of labor guidance came to inspect the factory but came back after they got under table paid. Most of the day laborers are fired and some of them have years of service,” said the activist who is supporting the workers. The dismissed workers do not have EC contract and they worked with a 2 month contract. They are dismissed after reporting for labor right abuses but they did not get paid damages and other benefits as they are day laborers although they have served for years. Most of the male workers are only hired as day laborers and those who don’t work overtime are cut for attendance bonus and other bonuses. The day laborers are fired without any strong reason. And the 2 month contract of them is not a legal employment contract one but just on the paper. The workers have to elect 5 WCC representatives but the WCC is only assigned to sign the factory’s decision. They are being called for illegal all night and all light overtime recently. The working hours are from 7:30 to 18:00 and the overtime are until midnight, until dawn on Saturdays and also forced to work on Sundays and public holidays.  The workers inform the supers, all supers and leaders that they are exhausted of overtime but the supers and all supers said that they don’t need to work there anymore if they refuse to work overtime. Those who complaint are moved to other departments and also treated badly. As they reported the labor office, the all supers went furious on the next day and told that they would fire the worker who reported. The manager Daw Ei Ei Phyu called 5 workers in a session on January 25, and pressured them to confirm that they work overtime with their consents and the workers confirmed as they afraid. The overtime are only calculated until 20:15 and all night, all light and Sunday and public holiday overtimes are paid with 1,400 kyats per hour on the next days. The overtime are not included in the salary voucher. The workers want both the officials of Asdet and the government departments to resolve effectively regarding the abuses. The factory is a Chinese national owned factory which is operating with around 6oo workers and manufacturing CHANGE, esmaea (LIDL) and Footmael brands shirts and bras. Content: The  workers from the Chinese national owned factory JOC MYANMAR GARMENT which locates in Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon Region said that their factory is operating with more than 1,000 workers which 10% of them (more than 100 workers) are day laborers and their rights are being abused. Neither trade union nor work place coordination committee is formed to address the labor disputes. The factory is known for manufacturing BURTLE WW, brand men jackets. The working hours are from 7:30 to 18:00 with an extra overtime of 2 hours and day laborers are only given 5,800 kyats for 10 hours of work. They get paid only 5,800 kyats after working until 18:30 in Saturdays. They are paid once a week but it doesn’t cover their labor for the off day. “There are underage child laborers in the day laborers. The stream stresses are given only 5,800 kyats and the helper 4,800 kyats. The overtime rate is 1.200 kyats per hour. All workers should be given the same daily wages. Although they said they would give the fabric bonus once a week, we only get paid once in two weeks in reality. We don’t have access to legal benefits, rights and social security. We neither have trade union nor the WCC. No emergency sirens are installed and the fire extinguisher are also not provided in accordance with the legal instructions. The workers have concerns regarding safety measures,” said the worker. The workers said that  they want to be given the legal overtime rate, to appoint the day laboers as the permanent workers, to give the daily wages for day laborers’ labors in previous Saturdays and Sundays with a backdate, to give legal benefits and rights, and to give access to legal leaves. We can’t relief until we arrive our home and neither do the family members,” said a local from Shwe Pyi Thar Township. The young people’s worries are increase after the enacting of the civilian military service law and there are also several news of adolescents arrested with no reason. “The transportation is not convenient on way back home. We want the employers to consider and lessen for this. We do not know what responsibilities would the factory takes if something bad happens,” said a factory worker.  Public insecure is getting worse during the Junta’s era and people’s concerns increase after they had enacted the civilian mandatory military service law. Content: 197 workers from Full Way garment factory which locates in No. 83, Min Ayar Street, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon region are having difficulties as the employer close down the factory without any notices. Since January 1st the factory has been closed for a month and the workers said that although they received basic wages and allowances on February 5th, they still do not know when the factory will be open again and it is still closed until now. “We get daily wages of 4,800 kyats and attendance bonus 1,000 kyats rate, which is a total of 180,000 kyats. It is not comfortable for us to pay the expenses. We are not yet informed the date of the factory to reopen and how they will pay us. The employer is not here anymore. The landlord had sealed the factory so that we are worrying if the employer would not come back. They should give us damages if they would close. We submit a letter to inform us the day if they were to reopen. He said that he is going to lend to his friend’s factory when he was moving the machines. We can’t inquire no one as the manager also had been suspended. We want the employer to resolve. How can we trust the lawyers while we can’t trust our employers. If the factory is sure not to reopen we want the fair damages for our labor,” said the worker. The workers are only get paid with daily wages 4,800 kyats and attendance bonus 1,000 kyats. A 31-year-old worker with 9 years of experience said that despite sending a mail complaint to the relevant township labor office through WCC as there is no response from the entrepreneur, there was no difference.  The factory has been in operation for more than 10 years, and since all 197 workers are senior workers, they are demanding compensation if the factory is sure to be closed. The factory, which is owned by a Chinese national, previously had its own orders, but it has been around 1 year it has been manufacturing sub-orders from other factories due to lack of orders. Although the employer did not come in person, they came the labor offices through a lawyer. There are 4 court dates and the workers have not yet received the respond they want. “Only the lawyer came to the court for four times. The daily wages is only equivalent to a bag of rice. It doesn’t cover with the raising living expenses. As an employer, he should consider for the senior workers. He said he didn’t break Myanmar’s law. He contributed in the social security for many years and signed EC contract with us. The officials should help us. We seek for resolvent for our labor,” said the worker. More than 150 workers are female workers among the 197 workers. Most of them are pregnant workers and married women who have to look after their children and they seek for resolvent for their services of more than 10 years. “We can apply for other jobs, if they pay compensation in accordance with the law. But for now neither the damages nor the date to reopen are informed.  We have been waiting for so long and more than 150 women are having difficulties. Some are married, some are pregnant and some are single women. No factory wants to hire the age of over 30. We have served here 9 or 10 years. It is not easy for us to find another job,” they said. The trade union was no longer existed as the Junta came to search for them after the coup. And the responsive labor offices cannot help for resolvent in this ongoing dispute. “Workers don’t know where to go to process. The labor offices said they don’t break the laws but I don’t think so. But there is no transparency if we inquire via them. We had never violated the Myanmar’s law. So, we want to ask what will they do if the employer breaks,” the worker said. Content: The workers from HOPE ONE garment factory which locates near Maung Kyan Thee Street, near A lal ywar fire department circle, Hlaing Thar Yar Township have said that they are physically abused, asked for excessive fabric outputs and they requested to stop doing those things. The factory is a Japanese national owned factory which is importing Japanese brand sweaters such as Ladies Fashion, noa-ge brands and there is no trade union in the factory. The workers said that despite having to pay 2,500 kyats in social security contributions every month as occupational violations, they were not entitled to medical leave and their daily allowances were cut. Grade bonus are set as A(50,000) kyats, B(30,000) kyats and D(10,000) kyats but only those who tolerate everything with the supers and all supers get A and B grades but the workers who are really proficient don’t get it. It is a discrimination between the workers. The workers are not entitled to legal casual and medical leaves. Daily wages 5,800 kyats, attendance bonus 10,000 kyats and grade bonuses are also cut for taking legal leaves. There are more than 30 day laborers in the work place who are hired with 5,000 kyats for 10 working hours. There are also not employed permanently but rather hired and recall according to the number of tasks although they have more than 3 months of service. “The workers from a factory with more than 1,000 workers have to line up for going back home and the manager physically assaulting the workers who don’t line up (slapping the girls and knocking the head to boys). We can’t accept physically abuse in no way. We want them to stop,” said the workers. Excessive fabric output amount such as from 150 to 200 fabric pieces per hour are asked by the employer by intimidating with cutting the salary. The fabric output demands are not considered for the absent workers. “The supers call us meeting and verbally abuses badly and told that we have to work free overtime for not getting the fabric outputs. They also threated us with the military service law,” said the workers. “The line 6 and line 7 supers are the rudest. They verbally abuse the workers with the worst possible way in public,” said the workers. The workers who swed quality failed fabrics are morally downgraded and those who complaint are dismissed. “The workers are not allowed to use phones in the workplace but the all supers and supers can. The workers are cut 500 kyats if they don’t satisfy with the worker’s rotational janitorial works. The manager noted the uncleaned cavity and cut 1,000 kyats on issuing the salary. The workers are not only having to work for their cavity but for the whole factory and cutting the wages for not satisfying with the janitorial work is an explosion and we want them to stop it,” said the workers. The factory was reported for the first time on January 29 for violations of labor rights at the factory, and the factory denied the violations and responded via e-mail to take down the news and apologize, but the workers said again that violations continue to be committed in the workplace. The workers’ requests are the employer to allow the workers legal causal and medical leaves, the manager not to physically assault the workers, not to cut without the workers’ agreement, the supers and all supers not to morally downgrade the workers and the male all supers not to verbally abuse and harass the female workers and the employer not to force free overtime after asking for excessive fabric outputs. Content: Most of the local youths had gone to the foreign countries to work after the coup d'état. Some people think that there will be financial extortion and airport blockage for those who would go to abroad due to the current military conscription law. People who were preparing to go to work in foreign countries especially the youths are causing anxiety due to the announcement of the military conscription law by the state run media. The Military Council announced on state television that the National Military Service Law enacted in 2010 will come into effect on February 10, 2024. In this situation, young people who are old enough to serve in the military are worrying if they are prohibited from going abroad to work. "I'm waiting to go to Japan for now. I should be leaving in about next two months. Right now, I've to worry for the military service news. I saw the news. It's all the worse as they're going to prohibit people from going abroad. It's not possible to survive with the income in this country for the long term. It would be really uncomfortable if I'd be prohibited from going abroad,” said one person waiting to go to work in Japan. Both men and women are required to serve according to the military service law. Men between age 18 to 35 and women between 18 to 27 are set as the military age but for male experts its up to 45 and 35 for female experts. Religious workers, married women, single mom, physically disabled, those deemed unfit for military service by the Army Medical Examination Board, and those who have been exempted by an order issued by the Central Militia Recruitment Board are said to be the exemption from military service. "I'm worried. I was preparing to go to abroad because I don’t even like the normal situations. Now, it's worse as we have to serve in the military. There was a free way to go abroad before. Now I'm worrying if they block that way," said a person attending a training course to work in South Korea. Content: KSENG (Myanmar) Apparel garment factory which locates at No (-), Survey No (51), Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township is abusing labor rights including the unfair overtime recruitment. The factory is a Chinese national owned which is manufacturing Mataland , Clique , springfield , FB sister , GEM brands with around 900 workers. The factory workers are asked to sew more than they could and supers are verbally abusing them if they can’t finish. Therefore, workers have to work without going to toilet and without taking a water break. And the overtime are called without the workers’ consents and EC contracts are not given. And the workers are having difficult to go to social security clinic for workplace injury as they are not provided a social security card. The workers address these as labor right violations. The factory sign EC contract with the workers but do not handed the social security payment document to the workers that makes even the workers with more than 3 years of service become cardless. And workers are not entitled to legal leaves and the HR treating badly to the elderly janitorial workers for taking leaves. The workers said that they seek for workplace disputes resolvents as the WCC is formed by the employer’s consent and do not address the workers’ problem. The workers said that they are called overtime until 20:00 for the whole January and some workers called all night until 23:00 without a break time, snack and transportation. All night overtime working workers have to sleep in the factory and went back to home at 5:00 am just to come back to work at 7:30 a.m. which is causing bad effects to their health. The factory locates near Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone and the workers who live around War Ta Yar are having difficulties on way back home due to lack of transportation provident after late overtime recruitment. The factory does not provide snack for the workers and does not allow to take their own snacks which makes them difficult in the factory. The workers are also forced to work on Sundays if the important fabric orders arrived but the Sunday overtime and normal overtimes are not showed in the salary paper but paid separately. The workers are not allowed to use phones in the workplace and the clerks are confiscating the workers’ phones with a case and hand to the HR. The workers can take it back only after working and no responsibilities are taken for property loss.   ‘It is ok to not allow using phones in the workplace but confiscating our phones make us un-notify even if our family contact us for emergency issues. A girl from a cavity left her child with her mother as her husband leaves her. Her mother is taking care of her baby with a baby bottle. Her mother called her to came back as her baby is feeling sick seriously. Her phone is just a key pad phone and she was forced to sign a warning for using her phone. We would not know even if our families call us for emergency cases. We are working as it is difficult to find a job these days and the HR doesn’t show sympathy on us. They can punish for using phones in working hours but they should not confiscate our phones,” said a worker from the factory. The workers said that they have requested to give them the copy of EC contract, to form a WCC which can address the workers’ workplace disputes, to provide social security cards, to survey their consents for calling overtime, to consider their break time, to provide snacks for them if they are recircuited for important orders and to provide a meal if they recircuited until 20:00, to provide transportation, to allow access to use phone for emergency issues, to give legal leaves and the factory’s officials and the labor office officials to address the workplace disputes.
