Content: According to the factory workers, they have to start filling out the Biometric Enrollment Application Form of the Junta’s Ministry of Immigration and Population. "We are being asked to fill out such forms without any explanation at the factory. I want to know how it will affect the workers. Are we really having to join the military?" said a worker at the BOHUA factory, which locates on Secretary Road, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township. He also said that factory workers in various industries are facing many difficulties with each own anxieties according to the regime’s civilian mandatory military service law. “The male workers at our factory are too scared because of this law. They told their leaders that they don’t want to work overtime as they were afraid of being conscripted if they went back home late. They want to go back at 4:00 pm as the conscription is stipulated legally not the same as forced drugging before. The factory said they must work. So, the workers asked permission to sleep at the factory and to provide them a shutter. Workers said that they would not work overtime weather they are fired or not, settlement have not reached,” said a worker from garment factory from East Dagon New City Township. Most of the factory workers have to work overtime at night but they want to go back early for now as the conscription law has come out and there have been reports of missing young people in recent times but the employers are verbally abusing and illegally dismissing for refusing to work overtime which is making the hardest times for the worker. In addition, a kitchen worker from a restaurant from Mandalay said that “Workers are going back at 18:30 here. The employers close the shops too. No one is on the road on 19:00pm. Everyone is having concern due to the news weather it is true or not. Its better to be conscripted in our house than our home. Workers who work night shift will be very difficult during these times but everyone have concerns” On February 12, 2024 the Junta announced the reverse personal law that is promulgated by the State Peace and Development Council on 2010 with law No. 28/2010 and said the law must come into force on February 13th, 2024. The workers said that day laborers and child laborers have causalities as they are hired without being appointed as a permanent and hired only if there are tasks to do and fired if there are no more. “We are not entitled to legal leaves such as casual and seniority leaves. Although the social security pay, the factory does not and we lost our daily wages and attendance bonus,” said the worker. The workers said that they want to request to give legal benefits in the workplace, to ask only the possible amount of fabric output and to appoint the workers with more than 3 months of service as permanent stuffs. Content: The workers from Tianjin Fashion Milestone Garment factory which locates at No. (392), Seil Kan Thar Street, Shwe Linn Ban Industrial zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township said that the factory is confiscating their phones without their permission and pressuring for excessive fabric outputs which is not inline with the EC contact. The factory is a Chinese national owned factory which is manufacturing Sinsay brand warm coats, pants and dress with more than 1,400 workers.  “The factory is composed of 2 sub factories called A and B in the same yard. The total workforce for both A and B is more than 1,400 workers and the difficulties are the same. The factory workers have to work starting at 7:30 to the end of overtime at 20:00 mandatorily.  The workers are not allowed to take a break after the normal working hours but continuously forced to work overtime. The factory officials do not change anything although we informed them about our difficulties in the transportation as the ferry buses provided by the factory is not enough. The employer is excessively asking fabric output from the workers. The workers now have to give 50 fabric piece per hour where they used to give 23 fabric piece hour before. Although the workers are working continuously without taking a water break or toilet break, the all supers and supers verbally abuses the workers for not meeting the employer’s demands,” said the workers The workers are not even allow to enjoy 30 minutes for the lunch break but only 10 minutes and being pressured to get the excessive fabric outputs. The foreigner Chinese are directly managing the workers and the factory hires many underage workers and assign them the same workloads as the adult workers. The two Burmese manager who are in charge when the order investigating teams are come stipulated further rules by saying that they can add rules according to the Department of labor guidance which is not included in the employment contract. They didn’t negotiate with the workers for adding the new rules but the employer one sidedly announced those by calling meetings. According to the workers are abusing the labor rights by forcing the workers to sign the warning without known reasons and firing immediately. “The factory does not have the necessary medicines for the workers and not speaking appropriately to the workers when the workers ask for medicine. The workers do not have sufficient chairs for dinning too. The factory sometimes castigate the workers’ phones by force without the owners’ permission. The factory never took responsible for the workers workplace injury but verbally abuse the workers instead. The workers’ requests are the employer to follow the EC contract and not to force the workers to sign warning and dismiss by stating unnecessary rules, not to ask fabric output more than a worker can sew, to give full access to the dinning time, the foreigner Chinese not to rule directly and scold the workers and to resolve the problems with insufficient ferries, dining chairs and medicines. Content: According to the basic class people and general workers, their financial struggles for livelihoods escalates as not only the commodity prices but also the transportation prices increased and its not enough with their basic salary. “Some factories provide transportation but some don’t. If the factory doesn’t provide transportation, we have to take a bus and transportation fees are increasing as the same as the commodity prices. We are not able to survive with our lowest wages. Our life become more difficult,” said a worker. It costs from 1,600 kyats to 2,000 kyats for a worker whose factory does not provide transportation. And also, the expenses are also increasing and its not enough with the workers’ basic salary of 4,800 kyats daily wages and 1,000 kyats allowance. This make the worker difficult to fill up their stomach. “I feel very pity for the factory workers who are working with 4 or 5 thousand kyats a day. The transportation fee cost 2,000 kyats. And the remaining 3,000 kyats just get a meal. They have to work more; commodity prices increase but the wages does not. The general workers’ earnings are only enough for them to eat only a meal per day,” said the worker. The basic class people who are working in Yangon had to take at least 2 buses to reach the workplace. The bus fees costs from 400 to 500 kyats and workers have to deal with other general expenses too. That is which makes them more stressful. The Junta raised 1,000 kyats allowance per in addition of 4,800 kyats allowance starting at October 1, 2023. But as the overtime is only counted upon 4,800 kyats rate, the workers are not entitled to overtime fee raise. From the workers’ perspective, the 1,000 allowance definitely would not enough for surviving a day.  The workers had stated that it doesn’t make them sufficient in anyway. The current minimum wages for 8 hours working hours per day is 4,800 kyats and it was stipulated since 2018. The law said it should be revised every 2 years to be inline with the commodity prices but the 1,000 kyats allowance was added only on October 2023. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: The workers from Beaume International Garment factory which locates in Phan Chat Wun U Shwe Oo Street, Industrial Zone (2), Hlaing Thar Yar Township said that the employer called the military and police during workplace dispute. The factory operates in the same yard with POPULAR International Garment and opened new with the name of Beaume and it has been more than 3 years to assign the workers in both factories. The workers are not exactly knowing which factory hire them and wants their service seniority to be recorded clearly. The employer and the employee settle a negotiation on January 31st.The employer calls the military and the police during the meeting and no agreements were reached until 21:00. The workers said that they are assigned in both factories and being asked 50 to 60 fabric per hour and the all supers and supers are scolding them are verbally abusing them in the workplace.There is no trade union in the factory to address the workplace disputes. The workers said that there are day laborers who aren’t promoted to permanent stuffs until 8 or 9 months of service and the have causalities as they are dismissed whenever there are low number of orders and get paid only 4,800 kyats daily wage and 600 kyats per hour for overtime. The underage workers are also assigned in tasks that are completely out of line with the health standards and the workplace lack safety measures due to the odors. They are cut for 5,800 kyats daily wages, 27,000 kyats attendance bonus due to not getting access to legal leaves. The workers are also forced to work all light and all night overtime without informing in advance and those who refuse to work are discriminated against. The workers said that they want to request the employer to recognize the seniorities at the Popular factory and to legalize working at Beaume factory, the employer to give the workers casual leave, not to force to workers all evening and all night overtime without informing in advance, to eliminate the workplace odors, to appoint the day laborers with more than 3 months of service as permanent workers and to give full assess of daily wages and overtime fees, to ask only the possible fabric outputs from the workers, the employer to not call the soldiers and polices who are irreverent while employer and employees are negotiating. The factory is a Chinese owned factory which is manufacturing I’Z FRONTIER, THE TOUGH, Beaume, Royal Mail brands jackets, warm cloths and jean pants with more than 1,100 workers. Content: The workers from Myanmar Jiale Fashion Co.,Ltd 2 garment factory which locates at Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Shwe Pyi Thar had said that they haven’t received the January wages yet. Every 5th day of the month is the last day to issue the workers’ salary according to the law. But the workers from the factory with more than 400 workers said that they are having difficulties as they have not been paid yet. “They didn’t told us anything about the salary and didn’t paid although we waited until 20:00. The manager arrived at the next day and said they will pay only at 8th and also said those who are not satisfied don’t need to take. He throws the phones and got rampaged. They signed to give at 8th. Those who are less than 2 years of service are fired with compensation and the others are given only 50,000 kyats for the salary. They didn’t inform officially that they will give on 8th. They should inform the leaders even if they don’t want to inform the workers,” said the workers. “Everyone has expenses. We have to give our dormitory fees on 5th no own would wait for us to pay. They have paid 50,000 kyats and more than 250,000 kyats are left,” they said. The factory owner is a Chinese national and the Indonesian national GM didn’t inform about the delay of the salary until 8th February until the workers went to complaint. “They should talked in the meeting clearly if they can’t give. They are on rampage and we don’t know what will happen more. He signed in front of us. He is an Indonesian national. We are confident with the previous manager but this manager always take adventage upon her partner being the from the Junta’s side by saying “You could bet who would win between the factory and you.” It’s too bad for us,” said the workers. The workers said that Myanmar Jiale Fashion has two sub factories called 1 and 2 and the delay of salary is only happening on No. (2) as there are low number of orders which they are mainly depending on. “There are no orders anymore. I think they are making us to resign ourselves as they don’t have the money for compensation. There are starting to fire the workers with less than 2 years of service. They are rampaging weather than closing the factory down if they couldn’t operate anymore. Everyone are working to earn. All of us are more than 3 years of service and they fired those with less than 2 years of service in December. There are 400 people left,” said the worker. There is a workplace coalition committee in the workplace but does not address the workplace disputes.The factory fired workers with less than 2 years of service recently and only more 400 workers with more than 3 years of service are left. They also went to the labor office to seek resolvent as the manager not treating fairly to the workers.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: The workers from San Yuan Oversea(2) Myanmar garment factory said that they are having difficulties as their professionality fees for January are cut. The Chinese owned factory which opened at the Western Road, Htan Ta Pin Industrial Zone, Htan Ta Pin Township Yangon region is operating with more than 500 workers and manufacturing PADDED COLLECTION and COTTON BELT brand jackets. The wages are 4,800 kyats daily wages, attendance bonus 25,000 kyats, 1,000 kyats stipend and the professionality fees A+(51,000), A (41,000), B(28,000) kyats.  Currently the employer only give 11,000 kyats to most people and 7,500 for others for those who get A+ 51,000 kyats professionality fees before and the workers are difficulties with the living expenses. “They reduced the professionality fees. They reduced in this month and some gets paid 10,000 and others 7,000 kyats. They initially said they would give professionality fees to some lines with high productivity and would not give for some line. Actually, those workers who don’t have to sew also have to pave the fabric hairs and label them. But they are not get paid as it is not called productive by them, but everyone is working anyway.”  All worker salaries are reduced by 10,000 to 30,000 kyats and they want to get the same as before due to effects on their livlihoods. “We have difficulties. Even B graders suffer for 20,000 kyats and A graders 30,000 kyats. The employer wouldn’t know but that amount is also a meaning full amount for us during these times. No one gets fully paid and when we asked about the reason the factory said every factory have to work. As the manager said, we may don’t have productivity but we complained that we have to pave the hairs and label the fabrics and they don’t respond.” Although they reported to the labor office for these violations, they didn’t get a chance to say the truth while they came to inspect. “We reported and the officials asked if the factory give us social security and if we are cut on January 7th but no one dares to tell the truth. I want to say that I want everything to be truth. I want to say not to cut because it makes the workers struggle and they are also cutting for the social security’s permitted leave too. The social security gave 60 percent for health issue and 70 percent for maternity leave. But they take very long time and said that it’s because there are only few stuffs in the social security departments,” said the worker. There is no trade union in the factory and the workplace coalition team cannot take any action upon being cut for the professionality fee. “If they are having a good situation and continues to operate as before, we want to be given the same as before. We don’t want to be cut. They should give us at least some amount that they should. And they should inform us if they are in a situation where they can’t give, so that we can process legally. For now it  is unacceptable because they want to hire us but don’t want to pay,” said the workers. Content: A worker from Nadia Pacific Apparel Co.,Ltd which locates at U Htun Nyo Street, Industrial Zone 2, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon was stabbed with scissors by the all super and severely harmed. The victim is a 22 years old male and had to treat 3 days for the injury. “He said most of my fabrics are failing in quality and how am I finishing the demands. Then he stabbed me. I didn’t know immediately as I was focusing on sewing. Later, I found out the blood and it feels pain. I was so scared but I continue to work until 18:00 and the demands are also finished,” said the injured worker. The worker was injured around 10:30 am on January 31st and went to the social security clinic the next day. The one who stab is the app super of cavity 6 and 7. “I am working there over 2 years and this is the second time I am harmed. The first time was hitting my head with barehand, pinch my arm and shouted with the microphone. I was so scared and I didn’t work for a week. They are the one who called me to come back. I am more scared as it is happening for the second time. I am not going to work,” said the worker. Around 50 workers left as they are physically assaulted by that all super and line 6 super. The workers left as they are assaulted physically and verbally in a male – female co – working environment. “We reported to the officials but they didn’t take any actions upon the all super. Therefore I am scared. That’s why I don’t do anything. My younger brother had been done the same and he left as he was embarrassed,” said the victim. The worker have been working as a garment worker for 4 years and working at Nadia Pacific Apparel Co.,Ltd for more than 2 years. The victim’s family said that they want the factory to restrict the rule and take proper actions upon the preparator. Content: The Ministry of Labor of National Unity Government, NUG announced the declaration of Myanmar Overseas Employment Agencies Federation, MOEAF as an illegal association and abolishment. NUG said that MOEAF is abolished for cooperation with the Junta, active collaborating and financially supporting for the power perpetuation of the regime, collecting taxes to meet the demand for foreign currency and pressuring the workers to send 25 percent of their wages according to the way implemented by the Junta, buying jet fuel to carry out air strikes with foreign currency and actively collaborating to handed the bloodshed money to the Junta knowing about the purchase of weapons and ammunition. "I saw the announcement. People related to the military came to the agency field since after the coup. In addition, the agencies that are related to the military are gaining more benefits," said an agency entrepreneur. After the military takeover, there has been an increase in the number of people who want to work abroad, and the number of people who have obtained a license to operate an agency business has also increased significantly. However, more service charges and financial scams are increasing. There are reviews that the Ministry of Labor is easily issuing licenses to get tax money, and the action against illegal activities is weak. There has been an increase in the number of people who want to work abroad, and the number of people who have obtained a license to operate an agency business has also increased significantly after the military takeover However, service charges are increased and financial scams are too. There are reviews that the Ministry of Labor (the Junta’s) is easily issuing licenses to just to get the taxes, and the action against illegal activities are weak. "No one dare to complain the increasement of service charges for now. The service charges depends on their words. The important thing is to be able to go to abroad. We have also heard of being scammed. But we don't know where to complain. If there is a related federation do exist, I want them to help the people effectively. I have seen in the news that the federation resolved these cases before. Now I think they don't do it anymore,” said a person who is pursing to work abroad.  The National Unity Government stated in the announcement that although they had asked MOEAF to participate in the Myanmar democracy movement several times, MOEAF didn’t follow and failed to take actions upon overcharging of service, failure to expatriate workers to the determine place and labor right violations. The NUG government also warned that MOEAF would be blacklisted and prosecute under the anti-terrorism law if it continued to exploit the workers, lack of responsibility, and accountability, force to follow the instructions of the Junta  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: It is reported that 15 Burmese migrant workers working in Phuket were fired from their jobs without being provide supporting documents by their Thai employer although the employer promised to do. "In Phuket, 15 workers who did not get their wages contacted us for help. Their boss had revoked their Namelists saying that he would grant them Non-Thai Identification card. In fact, he did not and neither pay the workers. He is even driving them out of the workplace," said the WAG group, who are helping the workers. The process of making Non-Thai Identification Card includes submitting the name list for CI (Certificate of Identity), blood testing, finger printing and issuing permit paper. The workers said that the Thai boss called the police to arrest them in addition of castigating more than 230,000 Baht including the remaining wages and the money he charged to make the Non-Thai Identification card  Therefore, the workers together with the WAG group had reported to the Phuket labor protection and social security office to get back the refund of the remaining wages of more than 2 lakhs Baht. Content: The manager of Wai Hua Myanmar garment factory which locates at Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone (1) had fired two workers who had a workplace disputes due to misunderstandings. A worker explained that two workers had a dispute regarding the installation of needle cover for the sewing machine while the inspectors from the brand were to come. “We had disputed regarding the work but we don’t do anything which would harm to each other. The factory dismissed us instead of resolving. They should just make a warning,” said Ma Nwe New Aung. Wai Hua Myanmar employment contract stated that “Intimidating, bullying and physically assaulting in the workplace” as a normal offence in appendix (a) and “Physically brawling, rioting and physically assaulting someone to cause severe pain and arguing and scuffling” are described as a serious offense in appendix (b) and said the action is dismissing. “They don’t take any actions while the all supers did the same. They recircuited overtime until mid-night 00:00 without providing transportation. The two workers would have mistakes  as they have to do every works urgently just before the inspecting team come,” They are forcing the stuffs to sign warning and dismissed them for minor mistakes while they don’t see their own mistakes.  The employers didn’t sign the EC contract themselves. It’s the factory who did it,” said a worker who don’t want to be named. Wai Hua Myanmar garment factory located at Industrial Zone (1) Ka Naung Min Thar Gyi Street and owned by a Chinese national. The factory is manufacturing MOHITO, Hgtncalif, Hang Ten, Cortefiel and Hamure brands with more than 600 workers. Content: The workers from Asdet garment factory which locates at Yaw Atwin Wun U Phoe Hlaing Street, Shwe Libn Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar yar Township said that the supervisors (all supers and supers) are intimidating them to work overtime and day laborers don’t get paid for the overtime. Around 600 workers are working at Asdet garment factory and manufacturing CHANG, esmaes (LIDL), Footmeak brands shirts and female under wears. The factory is owned by a Chinese national and there is no trade union. “The officials are turning a blind eye for what is happening in this factory. Day laborers are not get paid for overtime,” said the workers. The workers said that the working hours of the factory are from 7:00 to 18:00 and they are forced to work all evening and all night overtimes on Saturdays and also on Sundays. Furthermore, the supervisors said not to come to the work if they don’t want to work overtime and verbally abuse them for moving somewhere in the workplace. The workers are forced to work all night overtimes on 24,25,26 January and didn’t get a proper space to sleep. They reported to the office of labor office as they recircuit to work on the next morning. The factory let them go back when the officials came to the factory. But they are verbally abused the next day for the case and intimidated that the one who reported would be fired. The manager Daw Ei Ei Phyu investigated the workers individually and the workers said they were just working overtime as they afraid. Although they had to work until midnight 12 o’clock in 15th and 16th January, they also had to work on 27th and 28th which is an off day as the labor office officials didn’t come to inspect. The workers refused the overtime as they can’t work anymore but the supervisors intimidate them and the labor office officials didn’t come to inspect anymore no matter how much they reported. The workers address their difficulties that they are very tired, not have time to cook and rest and the factory’s meal are not comfortable for them and inconvenience upon being intimidated of firing. The salary voucher only shows the overtime until 20:15 but the all night, all light, public holidays and Sundays’s overtime wages are hided after paying at next day. The factory does not accept to negotiate the workplace disputes regarding the illegal overtime such as all evening and all night overtimes except telling the WCC team to sign agreement letter for what the factory side did. The workers said that they want the labor office officials to resolve the Asdet garment factory’s labor right abuses with sympathy. Content: Chinese national own factory Hige Fashion Accessories Myanmar Co.,ltd which is manufacturing H&M and POKEMON brand fabrics dismissed 50 day laborers without any reason after being reported for labor right abuses, More than 200 of more than 400 workers are day laborers with services of 3 months to 8 months. The workers requested to appoint them as permanent stuffs and not to ask fabric outputs which exceeds the workers’ productivity. “The day laborers neither can’t contribute to the social security or access benefits related to it. They do not get Thingyan long term holidays and the worst is they are fired if there is fewer tasks and rehired if there are some tasks to do,” said the worker from the factory. The labor activist said that Myanmar Labour laws stipulated that day laborers and tap system laborers can access the same benefits as the permanent laborers but in reality, the factory are hiring the day laborers without giving access to legal benefits, social security, legal leaves and firing them with ease. A worker said that the factory fired more than 50 laborers with 3 months to 8 months of service without any reason after Myanmar Labour News have reported the workplace violations of January and they are seeking help to resolve the issue. ‘The employer fired the day laborers without any reasons. We want resolvent upon that as it is an illegal action,” said the worker. The workers said they want to request to employe back the dismissed day laborers and no to fire illegally. The workers said that they want to the factory to ask only the possible fabric output from them as they are currently asking 700 fabric pieces within 10 working hours. “The factory is asking 700 garments pieces within 10 working hours from the cavities with around 40 workers, all supers and supers verbally abusing for not meeting the fabric targets, workers who sometimes sworn fabrics that failed qc tests while working continuously to meet the targets are forced to sign warnings,” said the workers. The day laborers with more than 6 months of service are not appointed as permanent workers and they are suffering as they are get paid only 3,600 kyats per day while being assigned the same tasks with other workers. The worker ask resolvents upon the issues that they are not entitled to legal casual, medical and social security leaves although they contributed in the social security fees.  It is also known that the workers are cut by 5,800 kyats daily wages and 35,000 kyats attendance for missing a day because of not getting a leave. No janitor is hired and the workers can only go back home after doing the janitorial jobs of the cavities by rotating. There is no trade union formed in the factory to address the labor disputes. The workers said that they want to request to give them legal leaves, to appoint day laborers who have more than 3 months of service as permanent stuffs and the all supers and supers to not verbally abuse them while asking for the fabric targets. Content: Su Zhong Garment factory workers said that more than 200 of more than 400 workers who are manufacturing bpc and RESERVED international brands apparels are working the same tasks with the permanent workers despite of not getting assess to legal benefits and leaves.  The factory which locates at No.(36), Min Kyaw Swar Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar  Township is owned by a Chinese national. And the workers address the labor right abuses such as not appointing the day laborers who have more than 3 months of service as permanent workers, asking excessive fabric outputs, not giving legal benefits and leaves and verbally abusing in the workplace.  have more than 3 months of service and not entitled to legal leaves. The day laborers are hired and dismissed rapidly and also fired illegally for just taking a day of leave.  Daily wages 4,800 kyats, allowance stipend 1,000 kyats and attendance bonus 10,000 kyats are cut as when they don’t come to job as they are not entitled to leaves.  The workers also said that there is neither trade union nor workplace disputes resolvents. “There are more than 200 day laborers in the factory which is more than half of the whole population of the factory. They day laboreres who have more than 3 months of service are not appointed as permanent laborers. They have many suffers as they don’t get assess to the legal leaves and fire immediately after missing a day of work,” said the workers. All the workers in the workplace don’t get assess to legal leaves and cut 4,800 kyats daily wages, 10,000 kyats attendance bonus and allowance 1,000 kyats for taking leave a day. And the workers said that the employer is asking impossible fabric outputs from the workers such as 60 fabric piece per cavity with 50 workers. “We can’t finish the fabrics no matter how much we work continuously without a break to drink water and go to toilet. The all supers and supers together with the HR and Chinese interpreters who interferes into the cavities verbally abuse us for not meeting the employer’s demanded targets. The workers who reacted are fired so that no one dare to complaint more and keep silent,’ said the worker. The workers want resolvents upon the factory not forming work place collation committee and not providing clean toilets. The workers’ appeals are the employer to appoint the day laboers with more than 3 months of service as a permanent worker, the HR and interpreters not to verbally abuse the workers, the employer to allow legal casual and medical leaves and not to demand more than the workers can sew. Content: The workers from the Sunrise Myanmar Fashion Garment factory which locates at Kyauk Sein Street, Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone 4, Shwe Pyi Thar Township Yangon said that no actions are taken although they reported about being forced to work overtime and not having safety measures in the factory. The factory is a Chinese national owned factory which is manufacturing and exporting GLOBAL WORK, WOLLYTEC, CINEMA CLUB, HARE, LEPSIL,URBAL FUNCTION , SINCE 1930 UNITED ATHLA, FINO-OUT, LOWRYS FARM, AIRTHERMAL. WMB and HK WORKS LOND- N, GLACIER brands with more than 1,000 workers. The workers said that there is no trade union and although the workplace coilation committee is formed, they are not unable to address the workers’ disputes. The normal working hours are from 8:00 Am to 19:30 including 2 and a half hours of overtime but they had to work from 21:00 to 00:00 in January on the grounds of important orders and had to work 3 Sundays which are the only off days of the week. “The manager said that he had submit to the corresponding departments about recircuiting overtime and also said it was approved. We had to work like this in the previous months too. Sometimes they call overtime to all the workers and sometimes with rotation. The overtimes are not called with the workers consents but those who are selected have to work mandatorily. The WCC bias to the employers’ decision more than the workers’ consents. Right now, the HR manager is firing the workers who complain in the workplace with various reasons. The workers took the damages and just leave as they aren’t dare to complain due to the current political situations. There are also rumors about forming a single factory from current two factory. I am not sure weather they worry about the damages or to prevent workers’ disputes in the factory, they immediately fire the workers who complain. The remaining are also pressurized and monitored by the security. At most they even made the workers’ to be want to resign themselves. Some actually did. There are too many pressures in the workplace. Some workers are fired in the machine-repairing department currently. There are also some who resign due to the pressures,” said a worker. They also said they want the factory to improve the security measures which are too weak currently. “The factory doesn’t have emergency exist. The whole route is sticked with the fabric buckets. No emergency siren too. The toilets are also not clean and the ones on the upstairs are not distinguished with genders, female and male have to use together. The officials do not come to inspect us although the news are oftenly uploaded. The manager said that he owns the departments so he wouldn’t care no matter how much we reported as he came from the background of those departments,” said the workers. The workers said that they want to request to survey their consents upon calling the overtimes, to not pressurize and illegally fire and to provide safety measures. Content: "They showed us the news in the class. They showed Myanmar’s Alin news featuring the ministry signing for MOU. They also showed us movies (video files) of people who work there and are comfortable." Scamming with fake South Korean seasonal worker jobs are occurring not only at the townships but also in the Yangon region. The ministry of labor didn’t settle the situation but announced the process of trying to sign MOU via Myanmar Alin’s newspapers made the scammers find more preys. Therefore, Myanmar labour news conducted an Interview to a victim who got scammed for the people who are planning to go to South Korea as a seasonal worker to be able to aware of. Question: Why did you choose to work as a seasonal worker in South Korea. Did you receive the information about South Korea is recircuiting for this? Answer: I heard that South Korea is recircuiting via CK KR Sharing vlog page and widely used social medias such as Tik Tok, YouTube and Facebook. They are recircuit by making us thought that was real and attracted our attention. So, we thought it was sure.  Actually, we are learning Japanese to work in Japan but we consider working as a seasonal worker as learning Japanese would consume more time and have to take exam. We also thought we would get paid more.  Question: How did you get connected to the agency that would send you to South Korea as a seasonal worker? Answer: Its via the language class. Because we believed the language class. The agency have a relation with the class and the one who help us connected also a trust worthy person. They even didn’t know it would be a scam. We heard that the agency is sending workers to other countries too. We thought it would not be a fake as they showed us the videos from online which we have seen. Question: Can you share us the terms you had with the agency? Please explain the contracts, payment and their guarantee.  Answer: We agreed what they talked to us. We had to paid 25 lakh kyats to start the process. I was not there when the teacher from the language class gave the deposit, she alone take responsibility to do that. If we were there we won’t give according to the situations. But we let it be done as we trust the teacher. We gave our passports to them together with the deposit. We can’t go any foreign countries as our passports are in their hands. Its exactly 65 lakhs. We gave the deposit on November 2023. We started to learn Korean language at the basic class since after giving the deposit. Question: You said you went to a basic class. What did they teach you? How much students were there and how did they demonstrate you how much reliable the employment is? Answer: We had to choose the class whether a Korean teaching school or Korean language freelancer instructors. We had to learn for a month. They asked the remaining fees after the class. Their charges are not the same. They charged 85 lakhs for those who want to go quicky. The minimum is 65 lakhs. Four of us didn’t pay all. We told them to show the vacancy and we started to suspect as they can’t show. But 10 from our group paid all. When we inquired the people who paid all, they said they were camped after maximum a week. According to them, there are two camps. Myin Thar and Nyaung Na Pin. They have to camp 15 days in Nyaung Na pin where they had to do practical works related to agriculture. They were tested for color blindness, urine and blood. Myin Thar camp is only for a week and there have to eat and sleep there like a camp. Those who joined said that they had to write the 19 basic alphabets, 1 alphabet per ppage and 19 pages. And they made a talk show where they made the students to believe the officials came in. The Koreans also came. But the students had to eat and sleep terribly. They had to sleep for 15 days on a single person small carpet on the concrete floor. They showed news on the class term. Myanmar Alin announced that the ministry is trying to sign MOU. And they showed the videos of the workers who are comfortable working there. We didn’t experience those as we only gave the deposit. Those who finished the classes are given a QR code as a document. Question: When did you started to recognize there is no seasonal worker recruitment from South Korea and how?  Answer: Because they ask rapidly to pay. But can’t show any evidences of employment reliable, not even the vacancy. They asked to pay by saying that we had to go on 27th December. We were asked to give the remaining 40 lakhs with fast rate (1o lakhs rate) as we had given 25 lakhs before. They said the Korean employer would give an allowance of 89 lakhs before our departure so that we had to give 10 lakhs more. But again, said it is not an allowance but a loan which we will be cut 10 lakhs a month for 8 months. Their words became mass up. So, we inspected at the offices and found out that they haven’t connect with any offices. And the ESP Korean labor activist told us not to do that. Content: It is reported that S-M Myanmar Garment factory from Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone (4), Hlaing Thar Yar Township is forcing the workers to work overtime for free. The factory is a Chinese national owned factory which is manufacturing House brand jackets with more than 400 workers. The factory set the professional levels of the workers by wages; 70,000 kyats for A+, 50,000 kyats for A, 30,000 kyats for B, 20,000 for C but the workers said that they have damages as the real proficient workers aren’t get paid higher but those who are confident and tolerate to the supers get paid and biasing upon paying the professional fees. Furthurmore, they are not entitiled to legal casual, social security and medical leaves and total 25,800 kyats (daily wages 5,800 kyats and attendance bonus 20,000 kyats) are cut if they miss a day of work as they are not allowed to take leaves. Some workers even cut for the professional fees. The all supers and supers are consistently asking the impossible fabric outputs from the workers which a cavity with more than 40 workers have to give 35 fabric per hour and a single worker to handle two to three points as the currently manufacturing fabrics have many points. The employer asks fabric output without considering the absent population and the all supers and supers are verbally abusing too. The all supers and supers force freetime on public holidays and Sundays with the reasons to finish the fabric and the workers have to work as they aren’t dare to complaint the supers and all supers although they don’t want to work. Around 50 day laborers are not appointed as permanent although they have more than 3 months of service and they been forced as soon as the orders become low. A workers said “The factory gave 1 lakh kyats and fired the worker who had to take orthopedic treatment as they injured their hand while working in the factory. They are a day laborer who just have a service for a month,” The worker said that they want to request to employ the day laborers with more than 3 months of service permanently, not to force overtime for free, not to pressurize to work overtime, not to bias in giving professional fees, to ask only the possible fabric amount and to provide purified water as the current water have petrichor. The factory is a Chinese owned factory operated with more than 400 workers and manufacturing Sinsay, RE brand trousers. The factory is abusing the workers by asking the excessive fabric output from the workers, demanding 30 fabric piece per hour where the cavity with 40 workers even struggling to get 15 per hour and the supers verbally abusing the female workers if they don’t finish the fabrics. There is no one who can address the damages of the workers as there are no WCC team in the workplace and trade union. Although the workers contribute in the social security every month, they are not entitled to social security and medical leaves and the employer called a meeting to said no one would be allowed gate pass or leave unless it is a fatal case and if do no earlier than 16:10. And even if the workers could go to social security clinic for health issues their 5,600 kyats daily wages and 10,000 kyats attendance bonus are cut as they are not entitled to leaves and the same goes for taking casual leaves in emergency cases. It is also known that the employer does not address the issues of the stinky toilets which is in front of the dining room which affects their health.   There are more than 30 day laboreres in the work place and permanent workers are get paid 4,800 kyats daily wages + 1000 kyats allowance and 1,400 kyats overtime fee per hour and those who have more than 3 months of service are only given the daily wages and overtime fees of 1,200 and only 4,800 kyats for the whole day in Saturdays. They are working the same tasks with the workers although they are not get paid the same. The workers appeals are to appoint the day laborers with more than 3 months of service as a permanent workers, the Chinese foreigners to not be allowed to manage the workers directly, to provide a distance between dinning room and toilet, to ask only the fabric output they could give and to give legal leave benefits. Content: Mai Yi Bei (Yangon) garment factory which locates at Padauk Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township Yangon said that they are being asked for lavish fabric outputs and forced to work overtime for free if they don’t finish. The factory is a Chinese national owned factory which manufacture Sinsay brand women wafer skirts with more than 500 work force. “Although the factory said that we are working with ticket fee, the employer never set the ticket fee of the newly came in fabric points but only how much output the workers should give. A Chinese national woman and a technology expert manage the cavity and a Shan-Chinese mix Arr Shan manages other departments. They ask the impossible amounts from the workers. Asking such as 50 fabric pieces per hour for the cavities with 50 workers are one sided demand from the employer. We can’t go back home but have to work overtime from 18:00 to 20:00 if the employers’ demands are not finish. According to the worker, the fabric target is set monthly for each cavities and wages are cut if not met. "They asked to sew by saying that they would give fabric fees in other departments it is less than 1,000 even if the workers work continuously without a break," said the worker. More than 50 day laborers are hired and they are usually fired for missing a day of work and those with more than 3 months of service also have many losses as they not appointed as permanent laborers but repeatedly hired and dismissed.  The workers aren’t dare to take causal and medical leaves as the supers hold grudges upon those who did so 5,600 daily wages and 20,000 attendance bonuses are cut to them for their mandatory absents. “Recently, the factory made the one day work and one day off system due to the low orders and said that we have to work substitute days if orders become normal. The employer never negotiate with the workers but acting like leave if we could not agree on his actions with his own accord. The workers’ toilets are also not clean,” they said. The workers want resolvents upon issues such as workers’ legal leaves, supervisors holding grudges for leave takers, permanent employment for those with more than 3 months of service, fabric outputs that align with the workers productivity and overtime wages. Content: Helping organizations’ members said that the officials of the Sheng Da Ming Apparel Co., Ltd (Saint Thar Min) garment factory from Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone (1) fired a male worker for borrowing a lighter. It is reported that the helper worker Myo Zaw Htun was fired after being accused of smoking in the workplace while what he actually did was borrowing the lighter as the husband of the HR manager was asking. ‘The HR manager’s husband came to my place to borrow a lighter. I said that my friend has one as I did not have. I said that I will give him when I am free but he told me to come give at the toilet. I went to give and the janitor lady saw that too. She even told that I was borrowing a lighter when the HR asked her whether I was smoking or borrowing a lighter. But she answered reversely when we were in the labor office,” said Ko Myo Zaw Htun. Ko Myo Zaw Tun, who has been working at the Saint Thar Min factory for two years, was fired after being accused of smoking on December 30. Ko Myo Zaw Tun filed a complaint to the Office of labor guidance to resolve the grievances due to unfair dismissal. Ko Myo Zaw Tun, who is working at the factory, said that the HR manager made fun of him and told him not to come to work. Ko Myo Zaw Tun started working as a machine line assistant at Saint Thar Min Factory and later moved to the Cutting Department. He said that he was transferred back to the sewing machine line as he had a problem with the HR manager at work. "The HR manager transfer the worker to other departments with malice even before this incident. Now her husband is involved in the case. As it's her husband who borrowed a lighter, he also smoked. Is it to make the worker fired?  Anyway, the HR manager is involving," said a support member. Currently, Ko Zaw Myo Tun is preparing to file a lawsuit in the civil court as his grievanceshave not been resolved in mediation at the Township Labor Department. Saint Thar Min Garment Factory locates at Industrial Zone (1), Shwe Pyi Thar  Township, Yangon and manufacturing CALLIOPE brand with more than 300 work force. Content: The workers from the Dishang Group(Myanmar)Dihuali Grament garment factory which locates at Anawrahtar and Ayeyarwaddy Road Intersection, Anawrahtar Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township said that there are labor right abuses in the factory and they wants to ask for help for resolvent. The owner of the factory is the Chinese and the factory is manufacturing and importing FINEASSIST and BEST COOL brands jackets and pants. The wages are 4,800 kyats for the daily wages, 1,200 kyats per hour for the overtimes, 30,000 for attendance bonus and the grade bonuses are 36,000 kyats for A, 24,000 kyats for B and 12,000 kyats for C and attendance bonuses are cut no matter what kind of leave is taken just for a day, so that the workers said that they want the legal leave benefits. Fabric amounts beyond the productivity are asked and the supers are keep pressurizing for not getting their demands/ “The employer already asked the amounts beyond which we could give. The factory manager would pressurize the supers for not meeting the fabric targets and vice versa the supers would do the same to the workers. They ask 30 pieces per hour for some difficult fabrics and some are asked 50 to 80 per hours. They usually forced us to work overtime without our consents with the grounds of important orders,” said the worker. “We have to work until 21:00, 00:00 and 4:00 in some days and continue to work in the next morning. Sunday’s overtime wages are not added to the salaries but issued on the next Fridays. There are even some workers who fainted and got headaches due to excessive overtime and attendance bonuses and grade bonus are also cut for taking a leave too. We are barely surviving although working as this much,” said the worker. The workers have to buy drinking water from outside as the water provided by the factory is not purified and they want the factory to repair the scanted and damaged toilets. Day laborers are fired at 2 weeks after hired and the factory intimidates to fine if something wrong doing is found when the inspectors from Japan come. According to the workers, their requests are to recircuit the overtime only if they  agree on their own consents, to ask only the fabric amounts that they could sew, not to cut attendance bonus and grade bonuses for taking legal leaves, to provide purified water, safety measures and not to intimidate them. Content: The residents from some wards of Shwe Pyi Thar Township said that there are civilian watchmen recruitments and extorting 5,000 kyats from those who don’t want to be. The junta is pressuring to do guest notification and to petrol on rotation since after the coup. “They collect money unlabeled amount of money depending on us to build sentry post. There was an incident the Junta forces shot the civilian watchman to death after the 2021 coup in Shwe Pyi Thar, Yangon. Therefore, the residents are worrying upon the wardens recircuiting watchmen. “We patrolled by each ward in the past. But the junta forces shot to death. So, we are scare. We worry if our family would meet them while patrolling. And they said we have to pay if we can’t go. So, it is not comfortable during these days while we are struggling even to fill our stomachs,” said a civilian.   The junta usually arrested motorcycles and requisite three-wheelers under the pretext of security. People from Yangon are worrying about forming mandatory watchmen teams while there are recruitment by force to join military training in the villages in Bago Division. Content: According to Solidarity of Trade Unions, Myanmar (STUM), an underage worker is taking an osteosynthesis treatment as they injured their hand while working at a plastic pellets company at Thanmani 8 Ward, Sar Tike (In front of the climate office) bus stop, Kabbar Aye Road. It is reported that Aung Pyae Sone, who works as a general worker before reaching 18 years old was injured at work on January 23 at around 10:00 PM and is being treated at the North Okkalapa (Maydarwe) hospital. “The incident happened at night due to having to work until the night. We assumed this incident occur as he is forcing to work continuously. It’s on his right hand. The factory said on yesterday that they can complaint to wherever they like. The child’s parents are motorbike taxi drivers, they are under privileged. For the medical costs, 80,000 kyats for the doctor and 40,000 kyats for the caretaker have paid. It is known that child did not have anything to eat yesterday as the expenses are not covered,” said the STUM official. The operation was done at the night the incident happened and osteosynthesis treatment is done for thumb, index finger and middle finger of the right hand. STUM said that the factory owner is still unknown and it is being managed by the factory manager. “There are only around 10 workers. He is recircuited via some people from the neighborhood. It is said that even his parents were not known yet when he started to work. They also don’t know his salary. It has just around 1 month Aung Pyae Sone started to work. There are many SME businesses in the neighborhood. They do not contribute the social security and workers eat and stay in the workplaces in these kinds of businesses,” they said. The STUM team said that they will continue to provide necessary medical treatment to Aung Pyae Sone and will help to take the effective action against the employer. Content: The workers from Myanmar LUXURY GROUP garment factory which locates near Phone Gyi Kyaung bus stop, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon Division said that they are having a hard time as there are violations in the workplace and no resolvents upon those. The Chinese-owned factory has been operating for more than 5 years, and is currently manufacturing women clothing brands such as PROMOD and CALLIOPE with more than 600 workers and exporting to China. The workers said that there was no trade union at that workplace, and the WCC was formed, but there was no effective negotiation and settlement of workplace disputes. The worker explained about the violations is that they are forced to work overtime on Sundays, which are public holidays, until 12:00 p.m., and every worker chosen by the supervisors without being asked for consents are forced to work without the right to refuse. The normal working hours are from 7:30 a.m. to 8:30 p.m. for the whole factory and the workers also have to work on Sundays and they also talked about their worries regarding difficulties going back home. “The supers scold the workers who said they don’t want to work on Sundays. Only 1 Sunday of 4 is an off day per month and no off day at all for some months. No transportation is provided for late overtime hours. We have to go back with our own plan and we have security concerns on the way back home due to the current political circumstances,” said the workers. More than 100 of more than 600 workers in the factory are day laborers who get paid weekly. The day labors are being violated such as getting only 5,800 kyats but not not overtime fees for 8 working hours in Saturdays, not appointed as permanent workers although they have 3 months to 1 year of service and being illegally dismissed. As another violation, the workers were demand the fabric targets far more than they could sew and they had to work with little time to even drink water and go to a toilet during the working hours due to the pressure. "Employment contracts (EC) are signed only after one year of employment. The contracts are signed by the employer and all are taken. No one dares to ask about labor rights," said the worker. It is noted that the workers appeals are to call overtime only after asking their consents,  not to recircuit the overtime until the midnight 12 o’clock, to pay the overtime wages with back date calculation, to ask only the fabric amounts the workers can sew, to take actions upon the verbal abasements of the in chargers and officers, to sign employment contracts on due dates and to provide EC hand the EC contract books to them. Those who have ever complaint the supers never get a leave. They are labeled as absent even if they actually work after informing leave. 5,800 kyats daily wages and 10,000 kyats attendance bonus are cut when the salary is issue for taking leave a day,” said a factory worker. A worker said that the LUCKY FORTUNE GARMENT factory locates at Sayar U Htun Street, Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone (4), Insein Township and assigning the child labors the same tasks with other labors instead of the legal working hours for the underage workers. Those children are asked the same fabric targets and oppressed. Fabric targets are asked for each cavity and 60 fabric targets are demanded to finish per hour. The supervisors and supers verbally abuse them for not finishing the targets and they feel like they are being discriminated against, the workers said. LUCKY FORTUNE GARMENT factory has been repeatedly reported in Myanmar Labor News in 2023 due to the many violations against workers. The factory is a Chinese-owned factory with more than 1,000 workers and manufacturing brands such as TULTEX and EUCENTRO brands. Content: The workers from the Chinese national owned Wounderful Apparel Co, Ltd garment factory which located at Han City Power Road, Myaung Ta Kar Industrial Zone, Mawbe Township, Yangon region said that there are labor right abuses in their factory and they want help for it. The factory is operating with more than 450 workers and operating with more than 450 workers and manufacturing Coolteem ERC and ENSRORED brand soft sport shirts, underwear and lace dresses and exporting to Japan. It is known that there is neither trade union nor workplace collation committee to settle workplace disputes. The workers said that they have to sew for the workload of 2 people as they are being asked excessive fabric outputs such as 150 fabric pieces per worker. The supervisors such as all supers and supers are verbally abuse them rudely for not getting the fabric outputs. “They physically assault in addition of the verbal abuses. Recently, a clerk girl was asked to sew and fired by the manager as she can’t. The all super Hnin EI Khaing who went to inform about being fired physically assaulted her when they have a dispute, even the manager have to meditate them. The clerk reported at Mawbe labor office but the manager lied to them. Furthurmore, as the Chinese lady could speak Burmese well, she usually came to the workplace and physically assault the workers such as throwing nearby things. A worker who put a quality dropped fabric into the bin was accused as a thief and intimidated that their picture will be displayed if they doesn’t resign on their own will. They are dismissing illegally no matter how much service the worker have,” said a worker who doesn’t want to be named. Although the factory does not allow any leaves and fire for taking more than 2 days of social medical leave, they can’t seek resolvent with reporting to the labor office but only them were fired. The workers also said “The legal benefits are far from us. They don’t even allow a causal leave if we have an emergency case just before coming to the work. For such cases, they cut 4,800 kyats daily wages and 20,000 kyats daily wages.” The workers address their difficulties of having to work excessive works such as working from 8:00 to 6:30 and until 16:30 at Saturdays. They also have to work until 4:00 a.m without prior notice. “We have to work all night in Saturdays without prior notice. We can came back only at 4:00 am. They gave 1,000 kyats for transportation fee but we have to spend our own money as it is not sufficient for us. Its not safe for the workers to go back so that they should provide transportation service. They don’t give the overtime wages of our whole night overtimes by saying they would give substitute day off. They intimidate to cut the daily wages if the workers refuse to work overtime,” said the worker. The workers said that they are working all night overtimes with no choice and intimidate them by not paying their labor wages are definitely exploiting from them. The workers said that many of under age workers are hired in the workplace and assigned the same tasks as the adults. They are also forced for not getting the fabric output and get paid only 3,600 kyats instead of 4,800 if they resigned. The workers requests are to inform them in advance and to recircuit overtime only with their consents, to pay the overtime wages, to provide transportation service for the workers who work the whole night or to raise the transportation fees, to pay the child laborers salary with 4,800 kyats if they resign, the Chinese woman to not physically assault and the all supers to not assault the workers physically and verbally. Content: BOHUA FASHION Co,LTD which is manufacturing CROPP, XC brands jean pants is abusing the labor rights and no actions are taken even if they reported. The workers said that they got cut for taking legal leaves and they are being demanded one sided fabric outputs of the employer which the Chinese national female manager and supers verbally abuse them if not get it. They are being recircuited to work on Saturdays and Sundays and don’t get paid overtime fees. “They always said on meetings that, we are the one who would suffer if the factory lost order if we report on social media rather than fixing their needs. And U Thant Zin said that he knows with every department and he can resolve too,” said the workers. The workers said that they are not entitled to legal causal leaves and cut daily wages 5,600 kyats, attendance bonus 15,000 kyats (30,000) for taking leave in the second half of the month if they take leave for health and emergency issues. The worker said that the factory asked what is not the agreement output of the employer and the employee. The factory is asking 40 pant piece per hour for the cavities with 35 to 40 employees and never consider about the absent workers. “Some stuffs from the HR department came to the cavity to ask for the fabric outputs. They said they would pay 5,600 when they posted the vacancy but now paying only 4,800 or 5,000 is exploiting,” said the worker. It is also said that the employer force to work overtime in Saturday and Sunday for free by saying he would give substitute day off but cutting daily wages and attendance bonus for the so called day off too. The orders are interim orders from other factories and they are doing whatever they want. The employer does not give one copy of the EC contract to the worker,” said the worker. Although the inspecting teams come to inspect as the workers reported in various ways, the factory already thought some workers how to lie them. There is no trade union formed in the factory and although workplace coiltion committee is supposed to be formed by 3 electives of the employer and the 3 electives of the workers, the workers actually can’t choose their representatives as the employer force them to sign agreement on his chosen ones. The workers said that they want to appeal to provide clinic and nurse in the factory, the foreigners not to manage the workers directly, to give Saturday and Sunday overtime wages, the irrelevant people not to involve in pressurizing to get the fabric output, to allow the workers to chose their representative for the workplace coalition committee and to allow legal leaves and holidays. The factory is a Chinese national owned factory which is located at A Twin Wun Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon and operating with more than 300 workers. Content: It is known that the Japanese national own Hope One garment factory which locates near Mee That Circle, Alal village, Hlaing Thar Yar is violating the labor rights such as not giving the legal leaves, cutting 5,800 kyats daily wage and 10,000 kyats attendance bonus; total 15,800 kyats for taking a leave, not giving the medical leaves under the social security although the workers pay for it 2,000 kyats monthly. The Hope One garment factory is operating with more than 1,000 workers and manufacturing Ladies Fashion brands drawstring shirts. According to the workers, the supers always told them “Don’t inform leave to us. The superiors won’t permit. We are also not entitled to it. The targets won’t be meet if you take leave,” when ever they ask for a leave. The all supers and supers care only about the employer’s favor and the targets instead the health of the workers thus demanding impossible targets, forcing a worker to handle two machine, 250-300 fabric per hour for each cavity with 25 workers, the male supers and all supers verbally abuse for not reaching the targets which makes the female workers feel more humiliated and embarrassed due to the fact of male and female workers working together in the cavity. Furthermore, the workers are fined 1,000 kyats if some fabric have quality drops as they have to work excessively while being demanded much targets. And the salary issuing system is not transparent weather it is daily wages or ticket wages. The workers are given professional fee according to their grade levels, 50,000 kyats for A, 30,000 for B, 20,000 for C and 10,000 for D. The workers thought that they would get at least some professional fee according to their professional level but the employer use ticket wages which included in the issued salary instead of the professional fee and the workers are having difficulties due to that manipulation. The workers are also forced to work the overtimes as mandatorily, assigned the whole night overtime without getting informed in advance, and some workers who complaint in the meetings that they can’t work the whole night overtime are also told to give all the targets in the early morning as soon as they arrive the work if they can’t work overtime. Although the employer provides the workers 2,000 kyats transportation stipend according to their distance to the factory, the supers only give that stipend to only the workers who are comfortable with them but cut and take from those who aren’t.  Additionally, the workers have to do janitorial works in not only in their cavities but also all across the whole factory as the factory fine them 500 kyats after inspecting the sanitation of the factory and noted it is not clean. Private properties of the workers such as phones are also not allowed to keep with themselves but instead in the lockers of the dinning room, which are very old and loose as many people use those and the all supers and supers scold them and the HR forfeiture their phone if they keep nearby. There are workers who don’t never get back their phones from the HR and the workers who are suffering as they don’t dare to ask the HR to give it back. The workers want to request not to forfeiture their phones as it is not easy for them to buy another. And there are more violations such as assigned the unskilled instructors in a factory with more than 1,000 workers and not providing sufficient medical supplies that is essential to be in the factory. It is acknowledged that the workers advocating for 7 points- 1. To allow them causal and social security leaves.  3. To sign employer-employee agreement letter and not to impose unnecessary rules in the workplace. 4. Not to cut 500 kyats from the workers citing the factory's cleanliness as a reason, as the workers are not janitors. 5. The male all supers and supers not to verbally abuse, yell at and swear at the female workers. 6. Not to deduct 1,000 kyats for qc dropped fabrics. Content: According to STUM’s press, the officials of the Sunrise (Myanmar) Fashion Factory said that a worker called Ma Khin Ma Ma Myat was dismissed from her job on January 26th after complaining about the welfare card without following their process. It is known that the cavity clerk was given a copy of the card to pay the social security fee and the card for Ma Khin Ma Ma Myat, since she started to work at the factory at November 17. Ma Khin Ma Ma Myat received three days of medical leaves from the social security clinic due to poor health conditions but the manager permits only a day and label the two other days as absent without informing as she did not apply the leave in advance. As Ma Khin Ma Ma Myo suffered from her health conditions again in the middle of January, she submitted the social security clinic’s prescription of medical leave to the factory in the afternoon of the day the incident took place, but the manager denied to give the medical leave but instead an unpaidleaves as the new welfare cards are under process. Therefore, Ma Khin Ma Ma Myat headed to the HR office to said that she can’t access the new card as she already got the old one and to pay the social security with it. But she was dismissed on January 26 accusing that she complained them. "Ma Khin Ma Ma Myat has a limited amount of services in the factory, so that she would be less entitled to benefits if with the new card. Taking medical leave with 3 months of service means unpaid. But she would be entitled to full benefits if she renewals the old card that have years of service. But the factory does not process these,” Solidarity of Trade Unions, Myanmar (STUM) said.   It is said that the social security clinic employee did not give her signature on the new card number, so when she asked her to pay the welfare fee with the old card, the HR clerk said that she could not do it. The STUM team also learned that Ko Win Hlaing Oo, a worker in the Finishing Department of the Sunrise (Myanmar) Fashion Factory, was told that he would be fired from his job for taking a gate pass. Both workers refuse to sign on the notice paper that the factory pressurize them to do. The WCC group formed by the factory did not negotiate for the workers. Sunrise (Myanmar) Fashion Co.,Ltd which is manufacturing GLACIER, Iusso and HK EORKS LONDON is locates at Kyauk Sein Street, Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone, Yangon with around 1500 workers and have been operating for about 5 years, the workers said. Content: Best Choice Myanmar garment factory which locates at Kan Thar Yar Street, Anawrahtar Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon is manufacturing 157. FUNK and Vaile Bieue brands with more than 500 workers and the workers said that there are labor rights’ violations and forcing in the factory. The workers said that the factory is owned by a Chinese national. There is a trade union in the workplace, and the WCC is only made up of people selected by the employer, and there is no way to solve the difficulties in the workplace. Regarding violations, the workers are being forcibly asked for cloth standards, and one worker is asked to set up to 500 cloths per day, and the workers are forced to work overtime if the targets are not met. “The workers have to work overtime with no choice. We have to work even on Sundays and the overtime wage are not paid fully. 10 people from our cavity is given 5,000 mmk but others were given only 1,000 mmk. They don’t provide transportation for overtime in Sunday. We have to go with our plans. Despite of not getting overtime wages, we even need to spend our money for around 2,000 mmk. Most got diarrhea as they don’t provide a purified water but instead the token water in the factory,” said the worker. He said that they are having difficulties as they are called overtime on public holidays and not get paid in accordance with the law. The workers appeals are to recircuit the overtime only with their consents, to provide transportation if they are called overtime, to give full overtime wages, to elect a labor representative to the workplace coalition committee as per the consent of the workers and to provide drinking water in the factory.  This is the third time we reported the words of the workers regarding the Best Choice Myanmar factory and we have reported twice before at December 27, 2023 and January 5, 2024. The workers said that even after being reported, rights violations continue to be committed in the workplace without taking responsibility, rules and regulations have been issued not to speak in the workplace, and the brands that are currently being manufactured are no longer being sewn with clothing brands. Content: Workers from NEW FUBON Company Limited which locates at Pyin Si Min Thar Gyi Road, Shwe Lin Ban Industrail Zone, West Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon Region said that they are having some issues as the factory is recircuiting excessive amount of overtime without giving a day off. The factory which is owned by a Chinese national is manufacturing MOHITO brand with more than 150 labors and only been open for about 4 months. Currently, they are being forced to work without the EC contract and to work overtime without their consents, and they are having a hard time as their health are badly affected as they doesn’t get enough sleep after continue to work normal working hours after working overtimes, all light and all night overtimes on official holidays, public holidays and Saturdays. "The main problem is not getting enough sleep. We are pressured and discriminated against by the supers, all supers and the manager if we can’t work overtime the next day due to the lack of sleep. Because of this, we have no choice. We have to do double duty," said a worker. The worker said that they have had to go on such overnight stays for at least 15 days a month. The labor law stipulates that any worker must only work 20 hours of overtime per week. In addition, the worker said that the fabric targets for the workers in the workplace is not set consistently, but the demand is increasing every day, and they are asking for more than the amount that can be sewn. “They ask 40,50 and 100 fabrics for today. When the workers met the target by working all the time without a break to go to toilet or drink water, the target is raised the next day. As it is a pressurization, the supers and all supers swears and yells everyday if the targets are not met. New workers who asked for a gate pass to issue their salary at the old factory are also scolded such as ‘If you wanna go, take the resignation letter together,” said the worker. The workers said that they want to appeal that the employer to only demand the target that they can sew, not to force all light, all night and overtimes without the workers’ consents, the supervisors such as managers, all supers and supers not to pressure and discriminate against the workers. Content: It is known that IGE FASHION ACCESSORIES(Myanmar) Co.,ltd which locates at Twin Thin Thite Wun U Nyo Street, Shwe lin ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon is operating with more than 400 workers. Those workers said that they are being violated through the facts such as not having an EC (employment agreement between employer and employee) contract, being demanded excessive fabric targets, being directly managed by the foreigners and not being appointed as permanent despite of long term service which have stipulated in the Myanmar Labor Law. The factory own by the Chinese national is manufacturing H&M and Pokémon brands caps and there is no trade union in the factory. “More than 200 among more than 400 workers are day laborers. Some have experience for more than a year as a day laborer. The employer do not assign them as permanent workers. They can’t contribute to social security and loss their benefits. They were not entitled to long term Thingyan holidays. They are fired if there are less tasks and recalled back if there are many. They are being violated in such that way and we seek for a resolvent,” said the worker. More than half of the workers in the workplace are day laborers, some of whom have been working for more than a year, but without being appointed as permanent employees, the workers say they are losing their benefits as other workers. In addition, the worker said that since there is no employer-employee agreement in the workplace, they would like to request that it be signed. Regarding the workplace violations, the workers said that they want to appeal that the foreigners not to manager them directly, to ask only the fabric targets that the worker can sew and to appoint the long-serving day laborers as permanent workers. "There is no union in the workplace. There is a workplace coordination committee called the WCC, but it is made up of only people from the employer's side, so there is no way to help solve workplace violations. Fabrics targets are demanded such as 200 fabric per hours. We can’t even go to toilet or have a break to drink water, to meet the targets they demanded,” said the workers. The working hours are from 8:00 am to 7:00 pm and the break times are 40 minutes for lunch and 20 minutes before overtime but the workers can’t even enjoy the break time as they have to work during it to meet the targets they are demanded. So that the workers said they want to request that fabric targets be reduced to a mutually agreeable amount.
