Content: I am a worker from Wonderful Appeal garment factory which locates in Han City Power Street, Myaung Takar Industrial Zone, Mawbe Township, Yangon. Forgive me for not mentioning my department. They are forcing excessive all light overtimes in the factory which the line supers yell at us in public if we refuse. Although we worked all light overtimes, we are not entitled to the overtime wages but in the name of substitute. They were inspections from the labor office as there were reports and files before but the factory have already chosen the workers who were to answer. The answers we wrote on the paper the inspector gave in the room was not true. We had to lie and wrote nonsenses as the manager to us to look back on the factory. The inspectors from the labor office intimidate the workers saying that “Reporting would make the interests loose”. Agreement letters to work overtime are forced to sign and had to start overtime as soon as the meal fee was given. Overtime is not agreed by the workers but the all supers and factory officers called a meeting and told the workers to work overtime mandatory through the supers. The supers summoned those who are refuse to sign the overtime agreement letter and humiliate and verbally abused them. The factory closed for four days from national day (7th December) to the Sunday (10th December). We had to work substitute days for those off days on Sunday (3rd December) We worked all light overtime on 6th December too. We didn’t get paid overtime wages but in exchange of the working hours. The agreement letters for those days are forced to sign only after the working hours. We worked until 6:30 pm on Saturdays, all light overtime on 6th January which is the substitute for 13th January. No wages were paid. And the same goes to 10th January all light overtime which is the substitute for 12th January. The factory close four days from January 11th to 14th. The workers do not agree with working for substitute days. Although the factory pressured us by breaking the law, we had to sign it as we are not able to be against them. They are also saying that all light overtime for (Today) Saturday, 20th January is the substitute for the next Saturday. The consent of the workers is not asked at all. We are working due to the worriment of losing the attendance bonus if we refuse to work. If the Saturdays are close due to the lack of orders, we have to return our 2 our labor for free from the next overtimes. They cut for substitute days despite working the whole month if we resign. We have to compensate with money if we lost a label or button. We ask for help. Please publish public to let everyone knows. Content: Chairman of the Joint Action Committee on Burmese People's Affairs (JACBA) U Moe Gyo said that a a construction employer from Maesot, Thailand is avoiding paying the wages of 26 Burmese migrant workers. Content: We want to report the issue regarding of the overtime recircuitment at Rong Da Factory. I am a factory worker. In addition of 11 hours of working hours per day, they are forcing us to work overtime until 0:00 am(all night) and 5:00 am(all light). The whole factory have to work all light over time at the night of Janu’6th. I am saying these things as they are planning to call all light overtime again in tomorrow, Saturday, January 20th. It have been a year we are working from 7:30 am to 7:00 pm at the factory. We have to work OT continuously for 7 hours without a break after the meal time. In all night and all light overtimes, we can we also have to work continuously for 8 hours after the dinner break.  The factory doubled the attendance bonus from 30,000 kyats to 60,000 kyats and tied the workers by saying that they would lose their attendance bonus if they did not work overtime. The production manager also told the workers that they should be grateful to work overtime during the current political and economic crisis. Officials from the labor office often come to inspect as many complaints have been made about violations by the factory. But nothing has changed in the factory. The labor office officials did not take any action against the factory and the working conditions did not change at all. Knowing that the most recent brand representative was coming to inspect, the production manager called a WCC meeting and select some workers as representatives and told them that "The life of 1,800 workers are in your hands," forcing them to lie. Workers have to lie for the factory and manager while doing their own work, eating their own food. What can be done to bring justice to the fact that Burmese doing injustice to each other without asking about the hardships of the workers to be accordance with the Chinese boss’s will? Myanmar Labor News has learned that the RONG DA Garment factory was established with foreign investment and is owned by a Chinese national. It is a factory that is often complained because of violations against factory workers. Workers said the the Rong Da factory locates at Min Bandu Phaya Street, War Ta Yar Industiral Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon and manufacturing Logos Park, Beloved and Bekkin brands. Content: "Eliminating child labor in such this country is difficult. Child labor will still exist until the country is developed. So, regarding the child labor we have to consider about the political stability first." According to the 2015 census, there are over 1.1 million child laborers in Myanmar. According to some surveys more than 12 percent are working in the manufacturing sector. At present, factories in Yangon are hiring underage child laborers to work as day laborers and pay lesser than the minimum wage of 4,800 kyats as stipulated in the law and exploiting their labor by forcing to work more than normal working hours without paying overtime wages.  Regarding these situations, damages and reforming conditions Myanmar Labour News asked an official of the Solidarity of Trade Unions Myanmar, STUM. Question. How have you seen the situation of child labor during the last year? Although it is defined as “Job which may have a non-positive impact upon the child’s physical, psychological and social development, job which may interferes the education, job that hinder educational access, job that compel early departure from school and children who work long hours of intensive work while going to school,” do you see the current situations have improvements? Answer. I must answer “No” for this question. Not at all. Question. Can we assume that there are many child laborers among the day laborers in the factories currently? Let us know how these workers are suffering. Answer. Yes. There are many child laborers among the day laborers. Even though they themselves are child laborers, they did not apply as child laborers. Many are not appointed unless they are 18 years old. So that they applied with a fake age. I see that they start working with the registrations of their relatives and neighbors. And they have to act like an adult. They suffer from exhaust as they have to work more like adults although they are child laborers. When the employers found out that they were child laborers, they would intimidate them by saying not only the employer but also the parent would be taken action. They have to be silent as they are told that their parents would be taken actions. In some cases, there are things that disappear as they are keeping silent.  Question. Can it be said that the entrepreneurs knowingly force child labor on purpose? Can their interests be greater by forcing child laborers? Answer. Many entrepreneurs do not want to employ child labor. They employ them only because of the cheaper wages.  Those factories that are intimidating are the factories that does not give, 4,800 mmk daily. In the factory we saw last month where many child laborers are working, they are not paid 4,800 like adult workers. They are hired as their labor price is cheaper. Question. How can we prevent entrepreneurs from exploiting the wages and labor of child workers? Answer. .If workers comply with the child labor regulations set out in the law, they will be able to prevent wage and labor exploitation. The law stipulates that anyone between the ages of 16 and 18 can work with a doctor's certificate. So that they don’t need to work overtime and Working hours are also limited. These can be prevented. But in the case of child labor, the employer will not hire many of them as they have to give them exceptions. Many are dismissed as soon as they are found out as they are child laborers. (Children between the ages of 14 and 16 are defined as child laborers by the law and are allowed to work with some restrictions. For those between the ages of 16 and 18, they need a certificate that they can work like an adult.) Question. Do we need to amend the labor law so that child workers are paid the same wages as other workers and they are not exploited? Or do entrepreneurs need to be ethical? Answer. I see that both are necessary. Laws need to be amended, and entrepreneurs also need to be ethical too. Question. Every time the relevant person inspects the workplace, day laborers and child laborers are suspended from work, fired or told to hide. Does this physically and mentally harm to them? Answer. Yes it does. They came to work and have to go back as there is no works today or there is inspection. They don't get money. They can be affected mentally and physically. Question. There are no effective actions upon child labor violations. Why? How should we proceed? Answer. As mentioned before, they have already intimidated. The actions will be taken to many people regarding child labor issue. The themselves do not want to face it. They don't want to make such complaints. So, it’s void. Question. What do you think both employers and workers need to improve in order for child laborers to have equal rights? Please let me know if there are any points to improve other than these two sides. Answer. I don't want to talk about child labor getting equal rights. Because an 18-year-old child should not be in the workplace at all. Many policies need to be established to eliminate child labors. Just saying no to child labor is not enough. We can’t make a policy in just one perspective but instead from all sides. For example, if a house depends on the child's wages, that child would end up in an illegal workplace. That child will have to face worse situations. It is also related to the situation in the country. It is not easy for child laborers to have equal rights in these times as the politics and economy are not stable. We can't focus on just one issue and promote it. How can we make good policies at a time when the whole country is facing problems? We can’t. Are we ready for to educate them and their education? Who would take responsibility for their parents. These are things to consider alternatively. I think we cannot prioritize only a single project under the name of “To eliminate the child labors and equal rights.” Question. Although it is said that they are working with plans to eliminate child labor, it has not been eliminated, but it has increased. Are the plans and actions have the needs and if so what are those? Answer. A state policy cannot be made by the Ministry of Labor alone. Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Social Welfare, City Municipality etc. need to be involved from all sides. If a family lives in squatter and unemployed, it is sure that the child have to work. What kind of work will they do? Who will be responsible for the elderly and disable people? The government must take responsibility. Therefore, if we plan a project, we can't just do it alone, we need to make a plan that includes all stakeholders. The current situation is not a situation where stakeholders and the relevant ministries have to sit face to face and formulate good policies. So, this issue is difficult to discuss. Question. Rather than eliminating child labor, what do you think should be done for the current child laborers? Answer. In order to eliminate child labor, I think we need to first find out why child labors exist. As I said before, the child have to work mandatorily if the family is facing hard livelihoods. So, what kind of work will protect the child? Suppose that we told the children not to come to the workplace if so, they would to work at illegal business, so will it be safe? One workplace no longer has child labor. One place is succeeded but the next place will be stained with sin. It would not be a good society.  There would be many street child if the Ministry of Labor alone plan the child labor elimination projects. Question. Please add something if you have more to say. Answer. It is difficult to eliminate child labor in such this country. Child labor will exist unless the country is developed. So, regarding how do we consider for about child laborers, we have to think about political stability first. I think we will be able to think about related issues one by one if we have political stability.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: The workers of Sewell Garment Myanmar factory which locates in Ngwe Pinle Industrial Zone, hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon have demanded that the professional fees to be paid back at the rate they were previously paid. Currently, garment workers work from 8:00 am to 6:30 pm and receive 4,800 kyats per day, 1,200 kyats per hour overtime, and 1,000 kyats allowance and ticket fees and the workers are requesting to give the expert fees as before as they are not able to make a living. ‘The price is not set for the ticket price. The seamstress would know the price if it is labeled. I want to be get paid the grade bonus as before. It have been 3 years since it was changed. At first, we e=only earned 170,000 mmk including 2 hours of overtime. So, we have difficulties to survive. The dormitory fee is 60,000 mmk per month so how do we eat. We are struggling although we are working,” said the worker. The worker said that it has been almost 3 years since the previously professional fee was changed to a ticket fee, and it is only received after meeting the targets requested by the employer, so the worker said that they are having a hard time due to the excessive demand for the standard. ‘We got paid 55,000 kyats for A2+,   45000 kyats for A+, 35000 kyats for A, 25000 kyats for B+ and 15000 kyats for C. But it changed to the ticket system without the workers agreement. The ticket fees are not labeled. The targets are the impossible amount for the workers and as we get paid only as much as the employer wants to give, we only earn 10,000 kyats of fabric fee after working a whole month. It is not convenient with nowadays commodity prices. We just want back the old rate,” said the worker.  The worker said that they want the employer to resolve as they are having difficulties going to take the remaining percent at the social security office if they take a social security leave within the workplace as they are only entitled to the 40 percent which have to be given by the employer. The workers said that they want to appeal to set the professional fees as before, to demand only the possible amount, the foreigners and interpreters not to commend them directly, to provide the access of social security benefits and the cold-heat balanced workplace. There was no trade union in the workplace, but the WCC was formed at the discretion of the employer. There are more htan 500 workers working in the Chinese national owned factory manufacturing and exporting Japanese YAMADATATSU ORRIGINAL brands. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: Garment workers of Myanmar Guotai Huasheng Glory Fashion said that they are having to work in a dishonorable manner due to the rude shouting and coercion of the supers and leaders during the work of the garment factory. There are more than 700 workers working in the factory which locates in U Htun Nyo Street, Hlaing Thar Yar Industrial Zone (4), Yangon Division and the factory is manufacturing brands such as INEXTENSO, CORTEFIEL and Sinsay brands soft fabrics and it is known to be Chinese national owned business. "Line 14 Super is the worst. She shouts from the top of the line and yells at the workers who can't deliver the fabric in time. She swears and screams far beyond then the workers can handle. She doesn't care if her insults are posted online. She said that she'll keep yelling and swearing. She treats the workers who she dislike with malice," said the worker. "The manager also knows that the issue of swearing by supers in the workplace is extreme, but he pretends not to know and even encouraging them. The manager himself says that he doesn't care no matter where we report. In fact, swearing in the workplace should be banned," the worker continued. They have to work overtime mandatorily even if they are sick due to the pressure on who refuses to work. The worker said that they are having a hard time as they are being shouted and embarrassed for asking a gate pass on Saturdays.  The worker said that they had to work Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., and until 6:30 p.m. on Saturdays and continue to Sundays without having a day off. In addition, even if they inform to take a leave due to health issues, they are cut for 5,800 kyats for daily wages, 20,000 kyats for attendance bonus and also the professional fees. “In addition to not being able to enjoy legal rights, those who are being harassed are ashamed and distressed as they are yelling and cursing all the time in the workplace. We are tolerating due to the livelihoods. We want these violations to be stopped. In fact, they could assign us in a softer way,” said the worker The workers said that being sworn rudely in the workplace and not receiving the benefits of the law is a violation of the labor law and as the workers who are manufacturing international brands they want to work in accordance with human dignity. The workers appeals are to not swear and yell while asking for fabric targets, to not discriminate the workers, to ask their consents in advance upon calling for overtime and to not hold grudges upon the workers who don’t work overtime. Content: According to the trainees, the recircuiting to train to work as seasonal workers in Korea is increasing. Although the Korean Embassy in Myanmar has stated that the Korean government has not issued any directives or statements regarding Burmese seasonal workers, the Ministry of Labor under the Military Council is announced on the state owned newspaper during the third week of December that they are in talks to send seasonal workers to Korea and trying to sign an MOU. Due to this situation, not only illegal recruitments are increased, but also some agencies are asking for service fees in advance, people close to them said. "My husband is already attending the training. I know that he has to go. About (65) lakhs need to be paid, but now only 28 lakhs MMK have been deposited. Those include medical tests, document and tuition fees. I don’t know exactly. He would have to issue the passport again. That would cost too," said the wife of a person attending the course. Currently, the Myanmar Labor Social Security Center (Korea) has issued an instruction to some regional offices in Korea not to recruit seasonal workers from Myanmar. On December 8, 2023, the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Myanmar announced again that the people who are recruiting either via online or in person to send seasonal workers to South Korea from Myanmar are scamming. “Agencies are still trying. I definitely can't say anything. There are a lot of local people who want to go. It’s the best time for those who want to gouge, it's," said an agency entrepreneur. At present, the two governments of Myanmar and Korea are collaborating to send construction, agriculture and manufacturing male workers.  In 2023, there are also financial frauds under the pretext to go to work in South Korea with the occupation such as nursing, domestic workers and seasonal workers. Content: It is reported that BOHUA FASHION factory which locates A Twin Wun Road, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Yangon is exploiting the labor by demanding the fabric target 2 times of before and forcing to finish within 8 working hours. The workers also said that they have been forced to work like this for more than 3 months. "The factory sews the fabric Intermediumly. It wants to takes the important orders and force the workers 2 times as before. They ask 150/160 pants which only asked for 90 before. Those force us to finish those targets without calling overtime. The deadline is 4:00 pm. It’s labor exploiting. Orders are also excessive, one come after another. The workers become exhaust and can’t withstand in the long term,” said a worker.  The workers said they are suffering from stress and fatigue as they were forced to finish during normal working hours. In addition, he said that workers are facing difficulties as their income was lower than before. "It makes as sweat and thirsty. I want to finish the job quickly and feels that I want to run away from the work place. The income is quite low. It's been 3 months without OT. They called twice on Sunday. That's all. Instead of being able to support my parents, I am struggling myself alone," said one of the workers. The workers said that even though overtime was called every Sunday in accordance with their desire but they were forced to come mandatorily twice. He said that if he they are assigned to work half a day on Saturday, they are not assigned for next week and asked to miss for two days. They usually go back with their own methods as the ferry does not provide transportation. They assigned as mandatory overtimes on Sundays in December and January. The factory closed on the Saturday of the following week and reduced the OT fee for the half day overtime of the previous Saturday. If there is a department that works overtime, they don’t provide transportation for the workers who leave first. They said they would pay for the bus fee, but they haven't paid so far. They missed tp give for three, four or five times already," the workers said. As well as the factory does not allow leaves and cut 60,000 kyats for missing a day, the grade bonuses of the most comfortable people with the line supers who are mean and rude to the workers are set at highest. “The supers don’t give us causal and medical leaves although we inform them. They don’t neither report to the office. Daily wages, attendance bonus and grade bonus; all are cut for an absent. I haven’t been an absent through my service career at here and I still don’t get a leave. Supers set the highest grade bonus for those who are comfortable with them. A2+ is the highest. It can even be called as bribery. Line 5 and line 3 supers are the worst. Both supers and leaders swears far beyond than anyone would dare to listen. They sometime points out their body parts,” said a worker. It is reported that they lost 15,000 kyats to 20,000 kyats of their salary due to the biased grade bonus setting of the supers. They said that even though the WCC group was formed at the BOHUA FASHION factory, they could not solve the problems of the workers. The factory is managed by a Chinese woman and operating with two all supers, four supers and eight leaders together with around 200 workers. Content: According to the supporting team, a woman worker from Muti color painting factory which locates at Block 23, No. 4, Nawaday villa, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon is fired for no reason. "A woman named Ma Moe Moe Oo at that factory returned to the dormitory after finishing a day of work at the factory on January 6th. She went to see her friend around 5:30. Around 9pm, the owner of the Muti factory called her to come back to the dormitory and she had to return to the dormitory late at night. The employer fired her as soon as she arrived back saying that she doesn’t need to come starting from the next day,” said Solidarity of Trade Unions Myanmar. Ma Moe Moe Oo, who was fired, had been working as a leader of Muti (Color painting industry) since May 2023, and was fired for no reason after more than 8 months of service. The STUM group said that they will process for her to be able to return to the workplace and receive benefits as specified in the law. “We are going to resolve the matter starting from today, (January 15th) at the Labor Relations Department," the STUM group said. There are a total of 13 female workers and 2 male workers at the Muti factory, and all workers are working with tap system without EC contracts. Content: The workers from KAIXI MYANMAR FASHION CO,LTD garment factory which locates in Pan Pae Khaung Maung Khat Street, Industrial Zone (4), Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon Region told that they want the employer to inform them openly if the factory is going to close down as there are people transporting and selling the equipment in the factory. There were workers who have left their jobs as the factory have not called OT for more than 1 year due to low orders, and currently, the equipments of the workers who left their jobs are being disassembled and sold each part, so they want the employer to take responsibility if the factory is going to be closed down, the workers said. "Before that there were more than 1,000 workers, and as they did not call OT for more than 1 year, the workers who were not comfortable left and now there are only 600 left. They removed the machines one by one of the workers who left and put them in the parking box and sold them. Also, there are only a few machines left for the cutting part and the machine line in the workplace. We want to be sure to know if the factory will be closed down," said the worker. The workers also said that they are worrying as the employer is transporting and selling equipment without informing them whether the factory will continue to operate or not. In addition, not all workers are entitled to the benefits of the law in the workplace are those who are not entitled to benefits are cut for 4,800 kyats of daily wages and 10,000 kyats of attendance bonus; a total of 14,800 kyats for missing a day of work. “We want them to pay the damages in accordance with the law if they are going to close down the factory. It seems like they are dragging for now. By looking the feat that they are selling the equipments of the workers who resigned as they can’t withstand with daily wages, we feel that there is no honesty. The workers are worrying that if cheat illegally,” said the worker. The workers would like to appeal to allow them to enjoy equal benefits in the workplace and to take responsibilities in accordance with the law if the entrepreneur is to stop operating the business due to various reasons. The Myanmar Labor Law stipulates that the entrepreneurs must pay the workers the remaining wages, notice fees and damages based on the amount of time they have worked, if the factories are closed for various reasons,  It is known that the Chinese national own factory is manufacturing quefairedemesdechats.fr brand clothes, jeans and brassieres and it have been operating for almost 8 years. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: Family members said that they have lost contact with 6 Burmese women who were trafficked in Iraq and are in a critical situation for these women. It is reported that the 6 women arrived in Iraq a month after arriving in Dubai last August.  "They have been physically beaten since they arrived Iraq. They were threatened by a gun and got fed only a meal per day. Now 6 are not together anymore. They all are separated. The last person I contacted said she was in a place with many mountains. She said that on 1st day of this month,” said a family member. The women are said to be around 20 years old and live in Pyin Manar Township, Bago Division. It is reported that a woman named Zaza Aung from Tamwe Township was sent them to Dubai, UAE to work as domestic workers. In August, they left Myanmar with a visit visa, and 4 days before leaving Yangon Airport, they had to sign a contract with terms of compensation to work as domestic workers for 2 years and agreeing not to come back before the period ends. The families said that a man called Htoo Htoo Kyaw came to pick up at Dubai airport and handed to the agency at Dubai. They were sent to Iraq as they didn’t get a job in Dubai for a month. "Critical situations have been going on for a long time. Their bones would be rotted if they would have died. Among the six, some of them are already considered died. They are facing sexual exploitation by both the people involved with the broker and the men at the work. They also faced labor exploitation that they only got 10,000 kyats of their 50,000 kyats salary a day where broker takes the remaining 40,000. They had to go to work at the agencies’ owners’ parents’ house without getting paid on those days they don’t have jobs. They got fed only a meal per day despite they have to work for free. They have to share the meal for 6 people with their wages. They are also forced to work at adult entertainment shops. They are being talked in exclusive language which is hard for a woman to take it. We have all the recordings. It have been a long time. We are worried that they will do something to their selves,” said a member of the support team. Family members said that the 6 Burmese women were taken by a local broker to Yangon-based broker Zar Zar Aung and then sent to Dubai. It is known that the local broker who issued them passports will take a deduction for 2 months' salary, and the cost of travel to Dubai was borne by the Yangon broker. A member of the support organization said that it has been almost 3 months since they reported and notified to Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and embassies including international level organizations such as ICRC and ILO regarding women been trafficked. "We haven't heard anything until now. The police station asked to write a petition. But noting improved. The victims’ side have provided detailed information about the location of the brokers and the women. No progress on that too. I see it as the responsibility of the state to look after the citizens. I'm afraid it would be more difficult if it took longer. Even now, the fact that they are in a place where they don't know where they are, means that the girls are unprotected." said a support member. The supporting organizations said that there are many people those arrived to countries such as Iraq, Omen and Syria after they were told they have to work in Dubai as domestic workers and there are many people who are not get paid for many months and those who are trafficked. In the past few days, the Solidarity of Trade Unions Myanmar (STUM) has announced that one of the women who were sold in Iraq have completely lost contact with them. Content: The workers said that the E&P Fashion Garment Factory which locates at Anawrahta Road, Industrial Zone (5), West Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon Division is demanding excessive fabric targets, and the targets are different from one line to another and they are being discriminated against upon that. The workers said that they have difficulties as they are being demanded excessive fabric targets in the workplace and the supers and all supers scold and intimidate them daily if those targets are not met. "They demand the fabric targets unfairly such as 70 to 80 cloths per hour for a worker. We feel miserable every day as the supers and all supers scold and yell at if those employer’s demands are not met," said a worker who works at that factory. The workers said that the factory force them to sign a warning for mistakes which is not include in the employment contract and the manager screams and intimidates them by saying “This is my age, not yours. You can’t act with your accord. Who do you think I am? A veteran.”   There are issues where we sick or have family member health emergencies after arriving to the work. In such conditions, they did not permit us a gate pass. When the workers call the labor office to seek help the Department of Labor and Department of Workshop and Labor Law Inspection official replied that they could not interfere as this is a business and they could not tell the employer as it is not stipulated in the law.  “They issue the salary at 7:00 pm on the day pay with the grounds of important orders. The workers who have to go back far away have risks. We are worrying for every pay day. The employer said that the salary would be issued only on the next day if we don’t work overtime. We want to let us go back early on that day,” the worker continued. They said that they are suffering as they do not have the right to elect upon the formation of workplace coalition committee but only the heads of the HR department were selected and formed and the WCC do not resolve any of the workers’ difficulties. The workers said that they want to appeal not to call overtime on the pay day and let them go back early, to give the workers who sick while working gate pass, not to discriminate against the workers, not to demand excessive fabric targets but instead a possible target that a worker can sew and the manager not to intimidate them by mentioning the military.  It is also known that more than 200 workers are working in that factory which is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing Sinsay brands shirts. Content: At the Myanmar Bestex garment factory which locates at Min Aya Street, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon Division, workers are asked to sew more than they can sew and if the they have to work overtime for free if the target the employer asked is not met, said a worker working at the factory. It is reported that the Chinese national owned factory employs more than 500 workers and is manufacturing Sinsay brand jackets. The worker also said that there is no labor union formed to deal with labor matters in the workplace. It is said that they forced to work overtime without getting a day off in public holidays. The worker said that despite having to sew international brand clothes, they only received 4,800 kyats as a daily wage and 1,000 kyats as a subsidy, and the professional fees are set at 15,000 kyats for A, 10,000 kyats for B, and 5,000 kyats for C. "They unfairly ask for a target that is impossible for the workers to sew and the line supers scold us and force us to sign a warning if those targets are not met. We have to work 2 hours of overtime for free. We generally have to work from 10 to 20 hours overtime a month without getting paid," said the worker. The worker said that child labors are hired in the workplace, and the workers do not get their legal rights, such as casual and medical leaves, and they face difficulties even if they want to take a social security leave and have to work in the workplace of unbalanced heat and cold. The workers said that they want to appeal to demand only the possible target, the supers to not use verbal abuse, to call overtime only together with the workers’ agreement, to give full overtime wages and to provide a workplace of health in harmony. Content: The rights of day laborers were violated at the Mirae or New Way garment factory owned by a Korean national, which locates at U Tayoke Gyi Street, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon Region. The workers said that they are having a hard time as the interpreter is making a loan business by lending money to the workers at 20 multiples and taking a cut in advance before issuing the salaries. " They didn’t openly do like this when there were unions in the past. Now there are no more unions. We do have a WCC only. The workers who have financial issues loan the money, and it is deducted from the salary at the office as soon as the salary is issued. They extort the salary envelopes. It gets worse month by month, and no action is taken from the manager," said the unsatisfied worker. The worker said that it is difficult for them they sometimes extort the salary envelope to get back the loans. In addition, more than 100 of the more than 400 workers in the workplace are day laborers, and although they have been working for 3 to 7 months, they are working at the rate of 5,200 per day, and do not receive wages on their off days as they are not entitled to day off benefit. "More than 100 are day laborers among the 400 workers, so they do not get the benefits of permanent employment. This is a lot of harm to them. The labor law does not distinguish that. Thet are acting as if the day laborers can be fired whenever they want," the worker said. The workers said that they want to appeal to resolve the lack of medic clinic and safety management and broken toilets, to take action upon the illegal loan business within the workplace, to appoint the day laborers as permanent ones after they have 3 months of service, to calculate with back date wages for the cut Saturday overtime and Sunday daily wages of the workers. It is reported that the factory is manufacturing ziben brand Korean clothes and exporting them to Korea. Content: According to the workers, there are cuts in professional fees in the garment factories in Yangon's industrial zones without telling the reasons. The workers said that their cut professional fees are much lesser than compare to what they received prior to November 2023. "The factory's professional fees have been reduced almost the half. The income of each worker decreased by 1/3 for that. It was still convenient when we got 4,800 kyats. Now the salary is very low even if the subsidy is included. It doesn’t cover the expenses and we can’t support our families anymore," said a worker from Jiashihao (Myanmar). At the Gysen-1 (Myanmar) Apparel Co., Ltd factory in War Ta Yar Industrial Zone, which employs around 800 workers, the expert fee was raised to 30,000 kyats, but the current expert fee has been cut for 25,000 kyats and only 5,000 kyats is being paid, a worker told the Solidarity of Trade Unions Myanmar STUM. The worker has been working at the Finishing Iron position for almost 5 years and received 15,000 kyats for professional fees in 2019 when he started working. He received up to 30,000 kyats as an expert fee after 2 years of service but the expert fee was cut and he received only 15,000 kyats after next 5 months. The worker said that on January 1 of this year, the expert fee was cut by another 10,000 kyats for unknown reasons, so he was only earning 5,000 kyats. "According to the labor laws, the reason for the cut must be presented for cutting the worker’s benefits. There is no right to cut the benefit that the worker is already receiving for no reason. They have to give it back according to the payment of wages act by the office of labor guidance. The workers said that their current professional fees are cut after the Ministry of Labor announced in October to provide 1,000 kyats allowance. "Some cut the professional fee for 5,000 or 10,000 kyats and some entrepreneurs stopped paying at all," said a garment worker. The workers whose wages have been cut said that they are facing difficulties as their set benefits are reduced in addition to the exorbitant increasement of the commodity prices after the military coup,  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: The workers said that the cost of the recommendation letters requested in applying for a job is more than one day's minimum wage. Currently, factories, work place and businesses ask for labor cards, neighborhood recommendation letter, police certificate, etc.  "We have to pay for labor card. We paid 500 kyats at the Shwe Pyi Thar office. We have to 1,000 kyats neighborhood recommendation letter, 1,000 kyats for police certificate. There are other expenses too. 300 kyats for the car bus which is 600 kyats for the round trip. If a youth would like to take her partner it would cost 1,200 kyats. Considering all together it costs more than a day's wages. We only cost this amount as we do it ourselves. People from Hlaing Thar Yar said they costed for two day wages," said one who made the labor card herself. According to the minimum wage law in Myanmar, the wage for 8 working hours a day is 4,800 kyats. Last October, the ministry announced to raise the stipend of 1,000 kyats of the minimum wage, which had not been changed for more than 5 years. Actually, we applied for jobs as we need money. We don't know how the job would be like but we have to spend first. Previously, employers did not ask for letters of recommendation. Now everyone is asking for it back. Actually, it is convenient if they ask for these letters after we are hired, but now it’s not ok," said a worker from Shwe Pyi Thar Township. A job seeker said that charging from departments and administrations are seems to be legitimate after the military coup. We have to queue to give the ID card before 7:00 Am in the morning to get a labor card. It costs a lot of trouble. It's not safe to go to the police station to get a letter of recommendation. As there are so many people who seeks for jobs now, we have to pay everything they ask for. They're asking for letters of recommendation to make businesses for the departments," he said. In addition, job seekers say that there are scammers on internet by claiming that they will search a job for the seekers. Content: A Thai MoU contract company sold 72 Burmese workers to another company, according to WAG, a Myanmar worker support group. The workers said that the Thai Apisit Engineering & Suppiy Part LTD company, sold the workers with two thousand baht per person to the boss of Power Line whom they have signed MOU together. "While signing MOU contracts, the Thais signed more people than it really needs. Even if the construction site really need is 20 workers, they bring in 100. While the workers arrive, they send (sell) exceed workers to other businesses. If such thing happened, the Myanmar companies are responsible as the workers did not arrive to Thailand. Thai companies are also responsible. They do things like reselling them to other agent parties," WAG organization’s official said. It is reported that 72 workers arrived in Thailand on October 17 with an MoU contract from Myanmar agency MOE THIT YAN Co,LTD (Moe Yyan Company) to work at Apisit Engineering & Supply Part LTD in Ban Chang, Thailand. The WAG also warned that it is necessary to verify the types of work to be carried out while signing a MOU contract in Myanmar, and to talk to the agent company if it is to work in construction job. "The embassy cannot deal with labor issues effectively. That's why we have to sue the Thai company every time there is a problem in Thailand. The workers need to check carefully what kind of workplace is in the MOU contract. If it's construction, we want them to be sure to check it,” said the WAG official. There are 10 female workers among the 72 MOU workers who arrived in Thailand. They were supposed to work in Ban Chang according to the contract, but sent to the construction site at Khon Buri.  After encountering difficulties such as not having regular works in the workplace, not being given the wages, not getting to loans and not compliant with the terms of the contract, they were sold by the Thai MOU company. The workers said that they asked the WAG group for assistant as the Myanmar agency does not take any responsibility despite the difficulties they are facing. Content: The  workers said that the Myanmar SINYOUNG FASHION garment factory, which locates next to Yangon-Pathein Road in Htan Tapin Township, Yangon Region, is violating the labor rights including forcing to work overtime and not paying full overtime wages. Although the company operates with around 500 workers to manufacture international brand Sinsey shirts and pants, day laborers and youth workers are hired for short terms and not being paid full wages, the workers said. "They announced that they are hiring day laborers saying that they would pay 5,800 kyats. In fact, they paid only 4,800 kyats. There were young people among those day laborers who were not yet of age. They are only hired for a short term while there was an order, and fired before 3 months," said a worker. In addition to the fact that the day workers are hired just temporarily without an being appointing as permanent, the workers also say that the permanent workers too are often illegally fired and are being directly managed by the Chinese nationals. It is known that the factory is owned by a Chinese national and there is no labor union formed in the workplace.  In the workplace, workers are asking for a target that is much higher than what they can sew. The employer sets a one-sided target of 60 garments per hour for a machine line. The workers are facing the slanders used by the supers and all supers daily for not meeting the targets. Content: It is reported that a worker at G-Yuan Packaging Material (Myanmar) factory was forcibly fired. The factory, which has been open since 2020, is a factory that manufactures cardboard and paper. It is known that there are around 100 workers working in the factory that locates in Nga Moe Yate Street, War Ta Yar Industrial Zone. Solidarity of Trade Union Myanmar, STUM announced that the fired Store/Driver worker had an argument with the security staff of the corresponding factory when he went to deliver goods to a factory on January 1st. It is reported that the worker who was fired for the argument was forced to sign a pledge by the factory owner's brother and the interpreter. On the evening of February 5th, the factory order was damaged due to the argument and as the corresponding factory was forcing to fire the worker saying that they won’t work together in the future if they do not fire him, the factory officials force the Store/Driver worker to submit a resignation letter. “We heard that the argument started by asking for a lighter. It’s not necessary to fire immediately for this issue. The process should include first and second warnings. They can’t immediately fire for these cases,” STUM said. The worker said that he could not submit a letter of resignation. But the factory told him that whether he submit or not he was already fired, so he don’t need to come any longer.  "The worker who was fired was fired without even having a warning before. It's not only a person’s fault when there is a problem. Of course, it could be the other person’s mistake as well. We cannot accept the fact that they would only fire their stuff,” the STUM group said. It is reported that the worker who was fired has been working for more than 2 years, but still receiving only 4,800 kyats for daily wages. The Ministry of Labor announced that starting from October 2023, the minimum wage of 4,800 kyats as well as 1,000 kyats of stipend must be given for workers in enterprises with 10 or more workers. Content: Workers from Great Glowing Investment (JW) (ADK) garment factory which locates in Zay Kabbar Yard, Mingalar Done Township, Yangon Division say that there are violations of labor rights at the workplace, including the absence of statutory holidays and forced overtime without their consents. The workers who work in the workplace are not entitled to casual, seniority and medical leaves which are entitled in 1951 Leave and Working Holidays Act. In this factory casual, seniority and medical leaves which are entitled in 1951 Leave and Working Holidays Act by Labor Guidance are not enjoyable. They gave maternity leave. But for an emergency leave, HR scolds the family of the worker who took it even the super leader approve it. We can’t take leave even if there is a family bereavement and even if we are temporarily disabled due to a workplace injury, we have to come to work wearing a plaster cast. Furthermore, the super leader swear us rudely and physically assault such as knocking the head, throwing with things, twisting the thighs and beating the back. Those who are not comfortable with the Super Leaders are discriminated against by being moved to multiple lines and not given bonuses," said a worker at the factory. The worker said that as they are not entitled to casual leave, 6,000 kyats of daily wage and 15,000 kyats of attendance bonus are cut for missing a day, resulting in a total cut of 21,000 kyats.  The worker said that in the workplace, the supervisors, such as supers and leaders, not only swear and scream at them but also physically assaulted them often. In addition, the worker said that there is difficult for reporting other violations such as no medicine provided for emergency injury, forced collection of money for other issues and forced to working overtime without giving a break. At least 2,000 kyats is deducted for just losing a screw. If we accidently put other fabrics in the AC, 200 kyats will be deducted for each step. The factory has poor ventilation, uneven heat and cold, and if there is an emergency injury, there are no medicine boxes. The medicine boxes are only kept when inspectors come for inspection. When they go back, they announce over the microphone to take back the medicine boxes. Female workers are forced to carry large items of fabric up and down the stairs. They forcefully collect money if there is supers and leaders’ children birthday that we can’t refuse. We have to work overtime from 4:00 p.m. to 6:30 p.m., without a break. In the EC contract, they agreed to give us half an hour break, but in fact they don't give them a break, so we have to work continuously. We are sworn for not working overtime despite without asking our consents. All night overtimes are also called frequently. They swear us even if we take a leave for health issues,” said a worker. The factory which is owned by a Chinese national has a workforce of around 5,000 and it is known for manufacturing Hang Ten and ZARA brands and exporting German, Chinese, and Japanese fabrics.  In July 2022, more than 2,000 workers strike a collective demand as they were not allowed to enjoy legal rights, being demanded excessive clothing standards, and being violated workplace rights. Content: It is reported that a letter of instruction has been issued to regional offices in Korea not to recruit seasonal workers from Myanmar. "The Ministry of Labor of the Military Council is also involved in the issue of seasonal workers. Signing an MOU to send seasonal workers, will indirectly recognize the military regime. That's why the Korean government is also careful," said a labor aid individual. The Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Myanmar announced again on December 8th that it is scamming if whether online or person to person recircuiting on regarding the plan to send seasonal workers from Myanmar. The two governments of Korea and Myanmar are cooperating to send agriculture, manufacturing and construction workers. The Myanmar government previously did not allow the sending of seasonal workers, but after the military coup, the Ministry of Labor has been working to allow it. Currently, there are scams spreading on social networking sites, saying that it will be able to go and work as a seasonal worker in Korea. The Ministry of Labor, under the Military Council, is working to send seasonal workers to Korea, according to the state-owned Myanmar Alin newspaper. Content: At the BEST CHOICE Myanmar Garment Factory, which was opened on Kan Thar Yar Road, Anawrahta industrial zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, workers said that they are having a hard time as the factory is taking back the OT fees paid on the substitute days instead of Saturday which was closed due to lack of orders. According to the labor law, if the factory closes for reasons on the part of the factory, the day fee for that day must be paid at the minimum wage rate. In fact, in addition to not paying the day off allowance for the Saturday, the worker said that OT and daily wages were deducted from the 4 hours per Saturdays and total 16 hours in a month. "Saturday is closed by them as there is no work. We don't accept the deduction of the OT fees from the sisters. Those are our wages that we claimed by sweats. And the drinking water is not pure. There is no water purifier, the toilets are not clean, but the dining room is okay," said the worker. According to the current situation, garment workers do not have to work 4 days a month, losing daily wages for 4 days, and the 2 hours overtime for the rest of the days are also cut off, so they are working overtime almost for free. The labor activist commented that the employer's decision to close the factory with own decision and cut the OT fees without giving workers compensation is a violation of the labor law. “If it's true that the employer closes on Saturday of his own accord, he has to pay the employee the daily wages. If they cut the 4 hours of OT on other days which has to be done on Saturday but as it's closed, this shouldn't be happen. This can be said to be exploitation from the workers without their consents. In other words, if the worker works OT, he has to pay it. It is a violation of the law and exploitation if there is no mutual agreement," said a labor affairs observer. The demands of fabric targets is much higher than what the workers can sew, and even if they take social security leave, they are faced with cuts in wages and there is also lack of clean drinking water, and lack of clean toilets in the workplace They went on to say that there is no solution for labor rights violations like the above and it is difficult to file a complaint. "I do want to report but I don't know whom to report to. I'm afraid I'll lose my job if I do. When the inspectors came, they sent 2 people per line. They told them to lie that there is no overtime, the drinking water was clean and the toilets were clean. The supers and the managers’ subordinates don't dare to tell the truth,” they said.  In the past year, the factory called overtime even on Sundays and have cases that they don’t pay for overtime. But for now, the weekends become off days with the grounds of low orders. "We had to work free for Sundays too. They just stopped calling starting last month as there were no much tasks. They called back than and didn't pay the overtime fees. I don't know whom to report. When the inspectors would come to check up, they hold a meeting. They told us to say that we don’t work down on Sundays. They told us to lie on behave on long term job stability. We have to give 2 people per line. The WCC is not yet organized until the inspectors come. For the workers’ perspectives, we are afraid of losing our jobs if we tell the truth,” said the worker. The workers said that they want the factory to demand only the possible targets, to give full overtime wages, not to deducted for Saturdays, to provide pure water and clean toilets and not to cut for taking social security wages.  It is also known that the factory is owned by a Chinese national and manufacturing 157.FUNK, Vaile Bleue brands with more than 300 workers.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: The workers of the Diamond Sea Sar Garment factory said that they have been working overtime for more than 3 months without a day off, including public holidays. Myanmar Labour News have learnt that the factory is located in Armor Minister U Nyunt Street, Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone 2, Yangon with around 200 workers and manufacturing Chinese-ordered fabrics. The factory is owned by Myanmar people. The manager is a woman. Overtime has to be done until 7:30 every day. We have to work all light and all night overtimes. We only have to work until 4:30 p.m on some Saturdays. But usually until 6:30 p.m. We also have to work overtime on Sunday," the worker said. They said that they had to work continuously from 12 o'clock after lunch until 7:30 o'clock in the night, and every time they had to work overnight, there was no meal plan for the workers at the factory. They said that the factory did not pay wages for Sunday overtime and calculated wages at 4,800 kyats. "Overtime wages are not paid immediately; we have to go to the office and ask for it. The employer replied, "We are not digging out it from a hole." For new workers, they only pay 3,600. The stipend just started from December. It has been just one month we got 5,800 kyats for daily wages," the workers said. Workers at the Diamond Sea Sar Garment factory said they are called for an all night overtime most Saturdays and have to continue to work on Sundays. The factory side asked them to work on public holidays such as National Day, Christmas Day and Independence Day. It was not closed on both Christmas day and National Day on December. All workers are not getting paid overtime wages. We have to work continuously day by day and don’t want to work anymore as it is too tired. We can't tell the leaders. If we went to HR and she said, "If you can do it, then do. If you can't, get out," "said the workers. The workers also said that if the workers are getting a lot of wages due to the card system in the settlement of the salary, there are also cases where the settlement is changed back to the daily wages system. "With the card system, the salary should be above 300,000 kyats. It would be about 400,000 kyats for those who can sew much. Now, even though we am working as an OT for a month, the salary is only 240,000 kyats or 250,000 kyats. I don't know if they want to pay the full salary. We suffered a lot. These need to be openly explained. And we are not entitled to leaves," she said. Upon asking overtime, the factory does not provide meals and neither the transportation. They also have health issues and absents; the workers added. “Those who live far have to walk back to their places. They cut daily wages and attendance bonus for taking absent. Only those who are confident with them are entitled to leaves. Even if we apply for leave, we are still called to work saying that it is not fatal. In long term, the workers can’t handle it. They want to take a leave. Many people have resigned now,” said a worker. Diamond Sea Sar Garment currently has six cavity lines and despite the formation of the WCC group, it is said that the workers are unable to talk about the difficulties they are facing. Content: Labor activists have informed Burmese workers to beware of construction jobs via agents in Thailand. "I want Myanmar MoU workers, Ci and pink card holders to be aware of construction contractors working through the construction industry via agent. If the MoU workers change to the construction job, ask the boss to give appointment letter. Make sure that this boss acknowledge as his worker. Stop working with the contractors after getting the appointment letter. There are good guys as well as bad guys. If the migrant workers don’t get pay, it is sure that those contractors cut the wages. If the workers don’t have appointment letter and have a problem, they would said you are not my employee, you can report to anywhere you like. That is their quotes,” said a person who is assisting Burmese workers in Thailand.  It is reported that the current construction contractors in Thailand are not paying wages to the workers, and they are not getting their wages for one to four months. Therefore, it is suggested that to ask carefully and work directly with the boss if working in construction sector in Thailand. If not working directly under the boss, it is recommended to get an appointment letter. “Agents recircuit by saying how much they would pay. But the workers don’t get paid for one or two or three months. We have to say this as the contractors are not paying. Burmese contractors via the Thai contractors are worse. Burmese exploit Burmese. The Thais pay. Burmese contractors said that Thai contractors haven’t paid. Ask carefully whether you have to work directly under the boss or with direct appointment. If it is contractor, leave as soon as possible. Don’t listen the agents. They will only say about the good parts. As wages are only returned after filing a complaint with the Thai authorities, the workers are facing difficulties in living and eating in the meantime, and there are ongoing requests for help from labor organizations based in Thailand. Content: According to the workers, the Ministry is forming occupational safety and health committees in order to reduce accidents at work in factories and workplaces, but the actual actions are weak. "In the factories, the ventilation is bad, the toilet noisome is also there. Not every factory but almost every factory have insufficient light or over brightness. Also, the toilets are not clean and they are smelly. Some factories don’t have enough stuff and toilet ratio. Sometimes we don't even see it as a problem anymore as we are so used to it. The committees are formed just to show the data to the ministry,” a garment worker said. It is reported that there are accidents in the workplace every day, and there are also cases of people dying. Domestically, the Workplace Safety Act of 1951 has been enacted. According to the law, only the factory and workshops are covered so the Occupational Safety and Health Act was enacted on March 15, 2019, for construction, mining, oil and natural gas industry, communication, transportation, the hotel industry, etc., sectors to follow. "In construction, we often hear news of accidents. Contractors do not do what they are supposed to do. The workers are also taking it easy. I heard falling from high floors every now and then. If safety is done systematically, these things will not happen," said a construction worker. According to the list released by the Workshop and Labor Law Inspection Department, 31 occupational safety and health committees were formed in the workshops and factories with more than 50 workers from November (27) to December (26) of last year. was also reported that during a field study of noise and light availability in factories and workshops in Yangon, Mandalay Bago, Ayeyarwaddy, Magway Divisions and Nay Pyi Taw Council Area, Mon State and Karen State, 35 out of 70 factories did not have the specified light and 23 factories exceeded the specified noise level. Content: It was announced on January 1st that the Honor Apparel garment factory opened in Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone 3 will be closed down.  Honor Apparel Co., Ltd announced after a meeting with the WCC members that the factory will be closed down starting on February 1 due to lack of orders to operate the factory. Now, the period from January 1 to 31 has been designated as a notice period, it was written in the statement. It is also stated that after the end of the notice period, the rights of the factory workers will be given according to the instructions of the law. According to the data of Myanmar Labor News, the factory is located on Pale Road, Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone, and employs around 900 workers. The factory is manufacturing Poland based Sinsay and Piombo and OVS brands and owned by the Chinese national Mr. Pong Xiyong. Content: According to the workers of the Myanmar Chaofa leather bag factory in the War Ta Yar Industrial Zone, Yangon, there are around two hundred workers, and about half of them are child workers. They said that these child laborers are being appointed as day laborers and have no rights under the law and unfairly treated. “Come look at the factory. The day laborers are children. They are small and firm. Most of them are 11, 12, 13 year olds. 14 and 15 year olds too. They don't get paid for the day off. No overtime pay. On Saturday, other workers get 4 hours of OT, but the children who eat that day only get 5,800. It’s the same for other days too," said a senior worker. Myanmar Chaofa Leather Ware Co., Ltd factory is owned by a Chinese man and is said to be making leather goods. Previously, there were around 1,000 workers and it was reported that world-famous brands were also sewn. One of the workers explained that the wages of the workers were reduced by up to 50% on the days when the factory was closed as they could not get orders in the factory. "The last closure was in the 8th month of this year (August) for 10 days. It was rapidly closed such as a month of a month and a half before that too. It's not rare to close like that. They only pay 2,400 kyats to the workers for the day offs. I don't know how it was presented to the labor office," said the workers. All the securities, janitors and office staff are working without pay for overtime, and even though there are inspection organizations, they were taught to lie in advance by the factory officials, the workers added. "There is only one janitor for now but there were 5 before. Now she is cleaning the whole factory alone. Even so, the security women still have to cut the grass. If overtime is until 8 pm, they can go back onlt at that time. In the EC contract, the working hours are from 8 hours to 4 and a half hours. Despite of not getting wages, the have to go back at the same time with us," said a factory worker. The factory's official working hours are set from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but the actual work time is until 4:40 p.m., the workers said. The workers also said that they complained to the labor office several times about not being paid for overtime, but there was no inquiry. “Just calculate 4 hours of overtime on Saturday, there are 16 hours a month. If the overtime is 1,200 as before, workers are suffering 20,000 kyats. I want to talk about this," said a worker. Workers told Myanmar Labor News that the water purifier in the Myanmar Chaofa Leather Ware Co., Ltd factory is located near the toilet and the public toilets are also smelly. Content: The workers said that they prohibit as they saw Full Way Myanmar Garment factory officials moving the sewing machines without informing them while the factory was closed. They said that they found out on today, January 1. “Workers nearby informed us that the factory was preparing to move sewing machines around 1 p.m. We went there and saw that 5 machines were installed. We also saw the factory manager. We said that we would not accept the move without notice to us and without us. Now the sewing machines have been put back,” a worker said.  The factory manager said that the owner of the factory was transporting the sewing machines to another factory for rent, but the workers said that they did not accept the transportation of the sewing machines as they did not trust them. "The factory is closed down and the machines are being carried out. They should have told us before the factory was closed. We can no longer trust the owner of the factory. The machines are canceled before too. This is the last batch. Previously, there were 15 machine lines. From there, it has decreased, and now there are only 4 lines left," the workers said. For that matter, the factory manager told them to meet on January 5th, and the workers they will seek legal actions if they continue transporting the sewing machines. Workers said they were told on December 10 through the supervisors that the factory would be closed for 10 days, and that some rights would be cut. "They will close for 10 days, saying that there is no order. They will give a daily wage and said that they will cut the attendance bonus and professional fee. We ask for the right as it is a need from the factory. If we absent, they are cutting everything. They cut the daily fee of ten thousand kyats for the day offs. We asked not to cut the professional fee, but we didn't get a specific answer," the workers said. As the manager replied that the employer did not accept the workers' request, they negotiated until 3:00 p.m., and the manager told them that they would go to the labor office and ask for professional fees, so the workers went home that day. Since before the Full Way Myanmar garment factory was closed for ten days, the workers were not allowed to take leave and 4,800 kyats of daily wages and attendance bonus of 10,000 kyats; a total of 14,800 kyats are cut for missing a day as well as the expert level. The workers also said that the supers yell them if they did not get the targets they requested in the workplace. The workers of the factory have demanded that to act in accordance with the law if the factory is closed down and not to take out the machines inside the factory during the closed days. The Full Way Myanmar garment factory is located in Min Aya Road, Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone 2, Hlaing Thar Township, Yangon. The workers said that it is owned by a Chinese national and is sewing denim through another factory on Minera Road. It is known that a WCC group has been formed at the factory and currently around 200 workers are working at the factory. Content: According to labor activists, some garment factories have closed in December 2023. The Myanmar Garment Industry Association announced that more than 540 garment factories were operating in the country in last February. "There are closures in Pathein. In Yangon, there are only three closures in Shwe Pyi Thar and one in Hlaing Thar Yar Industrial Zone,” those who are working on labor issues said. DVB news reported that 3 garment factories in Pathein were closed, and nearly 3,000 workers lost their jobs. It is known that the three factories in Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone are 2 garment factories and 1 shoe factory and the factory from Hlaing Thar Yar is a garment factory. A worker who worked at the closed factory said that the closure was due to low orders, power outages in closed factories, imbalance cost-effective to operate with gasoline. "Managers say things like that. We are off for 3 or 4 days if the factory can’t operate due to lack of oil. The electricity also goes out every now and then. Since we have to sew while waiting for the order, it is not benefiting as much. Order fabrics are not coming anymore. Compensation is now due on the 1st day of the month." said the worker. According to people close to the garment industry, factories are closing due to lack of basic needs such as electricity, lack of orders and weak investments. Among the closures of garment factories in Yangon, there are factories that do not comply with the law to ensure that workers are not suffered, said the labor activists. "Factories in Shwe Pyi Thar paid compensation and closed. I am not sure if it's temporary. It is not in accordance with the law. According to the law, compensation must be paid according to the last salary. Now they pay according to the basic salary. 5800 or 4,800 kyats and so on for damages," he said.  As the materials come from the border areas, due to the current situation, there is a shortage of factory supplies and there are currently temporarily closed factories. "Recently, I have heard about the closing of the factory. The closed factory is not much in number yet. I can't predict the future. Now there are less orders for tailors. As the garment materials cannot enter from the northern route, there are also temporary factory closures. There are many workers who go back without overtime. I think that there is a less chance for many factories to be closed,” said a labor activist. In Myanmar's garment sector, China and Hong Kong invest the most at 61 percent, while the domestic sector is in second place with 15 percent, according to the Garment Association. Content: The officials of Dong Sheng Xing Apparel Co., Ltd factory which locates in War Ta Yar Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar township are forcing the workers to work excessive hours. STUM also said that the factory was renamed from GYSen Myanmar (2) Garment Factory. “They called overtime until 12:00 p.m. We had to work all light on Saturday. no pregnant women, mothers with children left. They were forced to quit their jobs if they don’t work overtime and also put various kinds of pressure on them, and discriminated against them. Even when they called the labor office, the team that came to inspect the factory did not check, but turned away at the gate," the workers said, according to the STUM group. When the inspection team visited, the workers were told to hide in the garment heating room of the Packing Department. On December 29, 200 workers from Packing, Iron and QC and cutting machine line department had to work until 12 midnight and they reported to STUM as they can’t handle it anymore. GY Sen (2) Myanmar factory was closed due to low orders, and over a thousand workers lost their jobs with an agreement to rehire former workers if the factory reopens. STUM wrote that after the company changed its name to Dong Sheng Xing Apparel Co., Ltd., there were many former workers who did not get a job because they recruited only those they needed. Content: The workers at the Tianjin Fashion Milestone Garment Factory, which located in Seik Kan Thar Road, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar, said that they are being subjected to labor rights violations, including not being entitled to benefits, being illegally fired, being forced to work overtime, being discriminated against if they refuse and being directly managed by foreigners. The garment factory, owned by a Chinese national, has more than 1,400 workers and manufactures sinsay brand warm fabric shirts and other designs. It is reported that there is no labor union organized for the negotiation and settlement of labor issues at the workplace, where more than a thousand people work. "There are 2 factories in the vicinity of the factory, A and B. If add up, there are about 1,400 workers. The difficulties are the same. They ask for unfair fabric targets. They ask for 90 to 100 fabrics per hour. If we don't meet the standards, the super and all supers change us to other machine lines and points and swear and yell us almost every day," said a worker who is working in the factory. "Another bad thing is that if the orders are important, the workers are immediately hired as salaried employees. But if the orders are finished, they are fired on the grounds that it has not been 3 months. Such things are happening to the workers who are under foreign orders. They are cheating the law” the worker continued. The workers said they are forced to work overtime from Monday to Friday until 8:00 p.m. and also Saturdays and Sundays without giving a day off without prior notice in the workplace. Another worker said, "We have to work overtime even if we are sick. Workers who don't work are discriminated against. Content: The workers said that J-Land Myanmar Garment Factory is violating the minimum wage law and reduced their wages, and some officials are taking a cut of the workers' wages in the name of donations without their will. J-Land Myanmar factory located in No.49, War Ta Yar Industrial Zone, Yangon and manufacturing world wide famous brand “GUESS” with around 800 laborers. “We are employed as day laborers who take monthly salary. Daily wage starts at 4800, 5,000. On Sunday, the working hours are only part of the morning, but OT is not given for the evening working hours. They pay for the fixed day only. These days, those day laborers have become permanent workers. The rest of them are still working as day laborers," a worker told Myanmar Labour News. Although there is no distinction between permanent, day laborers and tap-servicers, the workers said J-Land Myanmar day laborers have to work together the same permanent workers while not being entitled to leaves, overtime wages and attendance bonuses. "Day laborers were not given rights as per the law, and they were not given allowances according to the instructions of the ministry. The instructions are issued in November to give 1000 allowance for that month. But the factory calculates the salary as 5200 for that month. That's what they are giving now until December. They said they would pay 5,800 at the end of the next month but they will also reduce the attendance bonus,” a J-Land Myanmar worker said. 5,200 per day wage is the wage rate that was raised in August, the workers said. They also said that when the wages were raised, the attendance bonus was reduced from 6,000 kyats to 3,000 kyats. In addition, the workers said that there are cuts in the wages of the workers against their will. "For the first time, 3,000 was deducted from the salary with the reason to pay obeisance to the elders. The office cut it. And 5,000 was cut again for Tazaungtine. This is a forced deduction from a worker's salary." he said. The workers said that as the brand representatives are there to come to inspect the J-Land Myanmar factory, they are reforming the factory clinic that was not there before and saw a nurse. The workers said that the factory super and liter did not allow and swears them for taking gate pass and not working overtime due to health issues. A worker also said that the social security clinic allowed her to take leave, but the factory office rejected it as more than 30 days. "The social security leave is full with 30 days because of maternity, taking care of the child and stroked mother. Unfortunately, I got ophthalmalgia. The clinic gave me a leave but the office did not allow it because it was 30 days. It is not suitable to work in a factory with people who are sore eyes. "said a worker who was not allowed to take a leave. J-Land Myanmar factory officials have set rules that are not in line with the law, and around 20 workers have been fired based on those rules, according to aid groups. J-Land Myanmar workers said that they want to appeal to pay minimum wages of 5,800 kyats, to reform the WCC, not to discriminate the workers, to eliminate workplace odors, to provide good ventilation, to be responsible for loss of property and not to deduct workers’ wages against their will.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.
