Content: Xinda Home Textile from Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone has reduced grade bonus on paying wages to the labours who quit their jobs, the workers said. In the last month before resigning, the labours said that they had not made any mistakes and had met fabric the standards, but the wages were reduced. "The supervisors (supers) said that wages will be reduced if we resign. An A+ great grader is reduced to a C. Quitting is an understatement," said the labour who quit his job. It is said that grade specifications in the factory are divided into A+, A, B and C. The labour also said that there is a difference of 15,000 kyats in entitlement money between these great levels.  “When the factory paid my wages, my grade A was reduced to grade B grade. Great A is 37,000 MMK. As for B, it is 22,000 MMK. The other disadvantage is that the daily allowance is 500 MMK for A level. B gets 300 MMK. Here too, around 6,000 MMK have been gapped," said a female labour who quit her job. At Xinda Home Textile, around 20 people leave their jobs every month, and there are monthly interviews to replace those who have left. The female labour said that due to the financial damages, some of her plans to quit her job and study were affected. "I quit my job to attend a distance learning university. I worked hard all month to pay for my studies. Being a big A, the monthly income is convenient for going to school. After leaving the job and paid the salary with a grade B, all my ambitions became hopeless,” she said. The female labour said that there is neither provision nor announcement in the factory rules that the salary will be reduced if she quits like this. Also, one of the female labours who resigned said that the process of resigning was carried out according to the process, and they notified a week in advance.  "I informed that I will quit my job on the 23rd but I worked until 30th. There was no mention in the factory that the salary would be reduced for quitting the job. Not in the EC contract either. The supers said that this grade reduction is caused by resigning,” she said. She also said that although Xinda Home Textile (Myanmar) Co; Ltd Garment factory workers paid daily fee, pocket money and overtime pay, the reduction in salary after leaving the job was a huge loss for the labours. “It is relatable even if the factory side is acting on the information provided by supers. But I can't understand how they reduce the grades of someone who doesn't violate anything like us. I tried to join the university depended on my own salary income but right now I can't predict what kind of difficulties I will face with this cut," the female labour told Myanmar Labour News. According to Myanmar Labour News’ intel, Xinda Home Textile (Myanmar) Co;Ltd is operating near Kan Thar Yar bus stop, Industrial Zone Street 6, No.1 Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon. Myanmar Labour News also got to informed that over 2,000 labours are working there to manufacture Warm Cloths and Jackets. Content: Bago Kfine violates the rights of pregnant workers. Workers are not paid annuities, and the official of the labour office told them not to speak out. The labour office official breaches the ethics by revealing the name of the complainant to the factory. #Letter From worker section (Uncut according to the sender's original dictation) Labours from Kfine International Garment (Myanmar) Co.,Ltd. Factory at Bago city bypass road are forced to work in violation of EC Treaty. In other factories, the annual salary, which is the right of the employees, is calculated once for a full year and the following month. Even they resigned, the factory informed them by phone to come and take the annuity. In our Kfine factory, we do not issue pensions after completing one year of employment. Another is that it is only issued twice a year in April and October but not during the interval period even we resigned. We complained about it when the labour office came to inspect it. The officers from the labour office said that annuity issue doesn’t count in their inspection, so they warned us not to tell anything. When the officials gone back, the HR Manager called us and scolded us. And because of this issue, they scolded us every day until the end of the month, so that I had to quit my job. Even now, pregnant women are forced to submit resignation letters. Even though they paid social security fee for a year, they were forced to quit. Pregnant women are not allowed to leave work early, but Burmese-Chinese interpreters do leave ten minutes early for lunch. And leave early at the evening and aboard the ferry. The interpreter who abroad the seats in the ferry is a homosexual man and always brings a pillow with their and sleeps alone in the two people seat wherever they get to leave in advanced. They did not ask female to sit next to them but males. Pregnant women are always given a seat by the young girls sitting at the back of the ferry.   Burmese-Chinese interpreters eat snacks in the machine line, use smart phone all the time, flirting with girls in every cavity, perverting the girls whom they could, bring snacks for them, hug and touch them during working hours. Cavity all super Daw Zin Mar Myint said to me, "You know that our factory does not accept gravid," and forced me to quit immediately. All Super Jue Myat Naing always swear. She sycophantic with the Chinese woman in the line and become an A Super without any skills. She swears to the employees under her all the time. She doesn’t to know nothing if we ask her. But in front of the Chinese, she scolds and swears in a way that she knows everything. Every time she swears, she highlights with the thing under her dress.   The coming weekend is set as 5 days off for Tha Din Gyut but we were asked to substitute on Sundays. When we asked if they would pay 5,600 MMK for those days, they said “No, its just a substitution”. Our factory has 1,800 employees and 200 day laborers, a total of 2,000 labours.  70 employees have to take a single ferry. No response from the HR for reporting this. All super Daw Sander Win said “Work if you can or leave” when we reported to her. She said to come with our own car if we feel it is tight. They, the higher ranks always make sure a seat to be left for them but pregnant women were to stand up.  There are two shifts in the factory right now. One group who came 16:00 and one who came 7:00. We the one who came 7:00 never got to arrive without missing a single bus stop. They forced us to take a single bus with 80/90 people.  The factory has about 20 cavities and mainly manufacturing Best Seller Brand, Only Brand, and ZARA Brand.  If the officers from the labor office come, the leaders teach us the forms to answer in advance. The officials didn’t take any action even if we answer the truth while having a chance. The officers in the office took what was given to them by the factory and went back. The officials from the government office returned as soon as the Chinese people gave them money. If this continues, the exploitation upon us were continued to be occurred too. (This letter was sent to Myanmar Labor News by the Kfine factory labours via Mail. The labours said that some of them were fired on unsubstantiated allegations that there were violations in the Kfine factory. laboural officials often come to inspect due to the violations, but nothing has changed but only some labours are always fired.) "I even thought that I would get the compensation tomorrow,” a garment labour said. In the today morning, September 6, , the labours in the factory were summoned and said they would pay compensation according to the law as they are closing, but they will not pay the notice wages. “We thought we are also going to get the notice fees, as they said they will pay in accordance with the law. Its not easy for us to get another job after a sudden closure. We will not be convenient as it is the start of a month and as we have some depts too,” said a female labour. The factory announced that they will hire some labours as day labourers to finish the unfinish tasks and labours also said that the labours from final QR and packing departments are still working. YSMM APPAREL Manufacturing Co.; Ltd factory locates in Pan Pae Khaung Mauk Khet Road, Shwe Pyi Thar Industrial Zone 4, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon with more than 600 labours and due to the closure of the factory, more than 400 have been laid off. There were more than 100 left as day laboureres and the factory is known for manufacturing european brands such as Sinsay၊ RAFRAF and Fox & Bunny. Content: EVER SUNNY INDUSTRIAL COMPANY LTD’s subsidiary of Guiding Star Group Company Limited, a food factory, which made (Sunday, Rich, Grand Palace, Shalala) brand coffee is cutting the social security benefits contributions paid by the labours without letting then have the benefits. The FGWM group reported that more than 300 labours are working at the factory locates in Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, and their social security payments are being cut. For private workers, the Social Security Law states that the employee must contribute 2 percent and the employer 3 percent for social security benefits. The cut of the social security fee is the money include that both the employee has to pay and the money that the employer has to pay. We are having to pay that the employer should do. We are getting a cut of 2,880 MMKs for labours’ (2) percent and 4,320 MMK for employer’s (3) percent," expressed in the report. According to the factory's solution dated October 3, the factory has only 180 labours, and the factory has paid both the employer's social security fee and the labours’ social security fees. Here, the labor force mentioned by the factory is only 180, and it is also stated that these workers are earning more than 2 lakhs MMK per month at the rate of 4800 MMK per day. According to the statements of the workers who complained to FGWM, pregnant labours are not allowed to take a leave, no responsibility if there is an injury in the workplace, and labeled some labours as day labourers in order to avoid the employee benefits such as casual leave, seniority leave, medical leave, maternity leave, attendance bonus and professional bonus. It is reported that some of the labours working in the factory are working through an agency, and are not receiving full wages, and are being cut off every month by the agency that helped them hired.  It is known that the labours who work through the agency don’t have the rights to enjoy the benefits and being like the employer rent labours from the agency. It is also said that they wants the officials to resolve the fact that the labours who involved in the domestic food production and distribution business are losing their labor rights and getting cut excessive wages. Content: As HONG MIAO Garment Co; Ltd factory which locates in No.4 Road, Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon Division has been closed, around 300 labours waited overnight in the factory to receive their wages, but the employer neglected and keep transporting the equipment. In addition, the HR has opened a case at the Hlaw Kar police station against 2 of the labours who stayed overnight at the factory last night for stealing linen. Currently, the labours have negotiated to receive their September wages and compensation for the closure of the factory, but they have not yet reached a settlement, and the labours say that they are seeing equipment being taken out of the factory. Two labours were arrested and charged with theft. This is also a fake accusing one. We waited all night, but the employer didn't ask anything. No one came to ask including ministers and heads of the labor office. The employer did not say anything specific. The equipment in the factory is already being transported. The people they summoned were also there all night. They came and asked us frequently. As they were drunk, we sat on the front row and keep the girls behind. They came and asked if we were okay. They keep taking pictures," said a labour. The factory will pay September's wages on October 5th for the departure but the labours wanted September's wages to be issued as soon as the factory closed, and they waited outside at the factory because they wanted to wait two days off and get their wages on October 2nd. But without a solution, it is reported that they are transporting the materials in the factory on the morning of October 3rd. Even though they had to wait overnight in the factory, the employer and the labor office opened a case of theft against the two workers instead of resolving and about 20 administrators and police officers recruited by the employer waited 200 meters in front of the factory workers and questioned them exactly four times. Despite this presence, the employer did not negotiate with the workers, nor did officials from the Ministry of Labor come to ask questions, so the workers had to wait overnight inside the factory, and the employer also called the police. “The factory is closed. Salary will be issued on the 5th of October. Those who could received compensation are told to came and take at 26th. Labours with more than 1 year service will be paid a compensation of 1 month ration and those who work for 6 months will be paid half of a month. The rest of the labours would not get anything. The labours want to get their salary as soon as it closes. The factory is closed, so we are not sure. They didn't tell us exactly where and when they would issue the salary,” said another labour. As upon the factory’s departure the labours are appealing to give compensation for all of them, to give social security benefits to the pregnant women and also to give the tap servicers. Before the closure the factory is manufacturing the Fieldcore Brand and other orders and when the labours formed a union to resolve the violations inside the workplace, the employer didn’t recognize the union and fired the leaders and members and later they issued a statement for the closure. The latest information is that more than 380 labours have not yet been paid their September wages. It was announced on September 26 that the factory would be closed, but operations were suspended on September 29 and no exact details about paying the compensations have not yet expressed. Content: The factory was closed on Friday, and they told me that the salary would be issued on the 5th, and the compensation would be issued on the 26th. All the workers came to ask about it on their own. HR called the police, and there were about 5 fully armed police," the labour said. HONG MIAO Garment Co; Ltd which locates in No.4 road, Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon Division announced in a letter on September 26 that it would close the factory after violations of labor rights, and currently, the factory is calling the police to solve the problem when the workers come to ask questions about salary and compensation issues. The factory was closed this morning. They said that the salary would be issued on the 5th, and the compensation would be issued on the 26th. Those who have over 1 year service will receive a compensation equivalent to one month salary and those who work for 6 months will be paid half a month's ration. The rest of the labours said they didn't get anything. We came on our own and thought we had to know something. The labours have already arrived. Labours want them to give compensation for all labours. Social Security benefits for pregnant women and to pay the tap servicers as before. October 5th is not sure. We want them to give us the day we arrived. There are 11 pregnant labours. We came to request those 4 points,” said a labour. However, in fact, among the more than 380 labours in the factory, there are only a few senior labours, and most of the labours are day laborers, tap servicers and labours who have not reached the age of 6 months. The labours said that since the pregnant workers are also involved, they would like to request some kind of compensation for them.  "Currently, there are also some unfinished fabrics. They said they will be closed on the evening of the 26th. We worked until Friday. The pregnant women are the ones who will get leave in October. I asked them how it would be for them. They said that they will pay as much as they are willing to pay 1o,000 or 30,000. It was very bad. I can’t bare what they said for the pregnant women. They are not accepting anything in the discussion now. It has been one year and 11 months since the factory opened," they said. The factory has committed violations of labor rights in the workplace, and the workers formed a labor union and applied to the head office, but they did not come and inspect it, nor did they provide a form. In fact, 48 labours who formed the union were found out by the employer from the head office and all 48 workers in the union were fired for the reason that they did not have an order. The factory was in trouble because many unionized labours were fired after forming a union due to many violations of labor rights. On September 20th of last month, after negotiations were held, the fired labours returned to the workplace. Despite such intervention, the 9 trade union leaders were not reappointed, and they said they would continue to negotiate with many other violations, but without further resolution, the factory was closed, saying there was no order. This morning, October 2nd, labours appeal four points that to give compensation for all labours, to pay social security benefits for pregnant women, to pay the tap servicers as before and to pay the September’s salary on this Monday, today. The factory manufactures FieldCore brands with around 400 workers and it is said that other orders are also made. After negotiating the dispute, the workers who entered the factory on September 21 made appeals for the workplace where the water entering the factory was too dangerous, the water being used in the factory was too dirty and no insufficient fans but on September 26, they issued a letter of notice to close the factory saying there was no orders. Content: Victims said that there are fake job offers and money scams that will connect people who need jobs through social networks with fake companies’ recruitment. These financial scams have been around for a long time and are now on the rise. Since the beginning of the Covid period, the domestic unemployment rate has increased. Due to the decrease in recruitment, fake job offers and scams become more common. ''I found it online. The job was a WiFi company posting that I had to work at on call service. So, I contacted them. As they said, I submitted the forms and they asked me to pay a service fee of 5,000 MMK. They have not answered the phone since then. When I called back, the announced phones were turned off. That's when I knew I was being scammed,'' said a job seeker living in Shwe Pyi Thar Township. Currently, there are many online services to find and connect with job opportunities, and there are more scammers than ever. In this fraud, the amount of money is paid from five thousand to tens of thousands of kyat, and victims are given an incentive to pay an additional percentage if they get the job, and the job application is accepted online scamming the money. In addition to this, job seekers need to be aware that there are some scammers who sell job applications for 5,000 kyats and saying that they will find a job, accept the CV form and cut off contact. ''I don't want to work in a factory. I prefer that because I can find a job online. At first, I don't think he's a liar because he posted it in the care. Now I know that there are lies. I myself have not been cheated yet. You have to be careful. I'll believe it before,'' said a person trying to find a job. According to the Ministry of Labor, there are 80 licensed employment agencies in the country. Employers also connect with agencies to find workers. They are working on recruiting workers through job fairs and posting job advertisements in job search journals. “There are labor offices that call for workers with advertisements. For factories, notices are posted at the factory entrance. Employees are informed. Also, there are job fairs and calls. You need to be careful when you see a recruitment from online. Some of them posted old posts and called back. There are some who misuse the company's name and make fake job offers,'' said a labor activist. Domestically, there are very few complaints about fake job offers and online financial scams, and awareness of these processes is also weak. Content: The Junta council announced today (September 30) that government employees will receive an additional allowance of 30,000 MMK, but there has been no press release for the private sector. Government employees will receive an additional allowance of 30,000 MMK starting from next October, and day workers working in the respective departments will receive an additional allowance of 1,000 MMK for working 8 hours a day, the Junta has announced. There is no news about this increase for private employees yet. The news that government employees will increase their wages has been coming out for the past few days. "I would say that the time to adjust the minimum wage rate has already passed. The ministry pretends not to know. Now, I see that the increase only for the government employees under the title of additional allowance is just a joke. In fact, what about the government's wage that is equivalent to the times must also be increased for the private sectors," said a former member of the Basic Factory Union. Locally, 4,800 MMK are set for an 8-hour working day, and currently, some factories are increasing it from 5,600 MMK to 7,000 MMK. According to the statutory minimum wage law, wages should be paid according to the times, but the employers are only giving one thousand kyat more. "Actually, people will only comfortable only if they get 10,000 MMK minimum. But right now, even though we work overtime both day and night, we are not comfortable. Now, if the salary of the employees is increased, I am worried about the good prices increasement too. I am seeing that we are going to face the double good price increasement whilst the wages they increase is only 1,000 MMK" said a labour working at a garment factory. Since the coup, local labours have been facing violations of their rights and livelihoods due to insufficient wages. Content: It is reported that there are physical abuses and slanders against workers in the SYNER GARMENT factory which locates between Debayin Secretary Assistant Road, between A Sint Myint and Bogyoke, Hlaing Thar Yar Township. The garment labours at the factory are being forced to work overtime without a day off even on Sunday, which is a holiday. It is reported that only a few labours get overtime pay, and most of them work without overtime pay. “This week, we had to work continuously until 8pm. Even on Sunday too. labours are all exhausted. We are tired. All factory workers have to work on working days. They rest on Sunday and do homework. So that they don’t come on Sunday. Those were told not to come anymore. A girl even demoted to the helper from the cavity. Almost everyone is working for free. They are supposed to let go of us in 18:30 PM but forced us until 20:00. Most cavities don’t get overtime fees except the cutting lines. Some do but most don’t. Always hearing from outside that factory often forced free overtime. Most people don't want to work there,” said a labour. The labours at that factory have been working overtime without pay for a long time, but they fired them for not working overtime on the Sunday weekend. It is reported that the demotions and slanderers have been perpetrated for about two months since the All Super arrived. “Working overtime for free is since the past but slanders and abasements came to happen only after this all super recircuited. It has been two months. There are 3 all supers but only she does like this. Not allowing us gate pass too. She made us sign warning if we don’t work on Sunday and firing and demoting upon that too. Content: According to the labours, more than 2,000 labours at the LAT WAR (3) garment factory which locate in Seik Kan Thar Street, Industrial Zone (2), Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon are being violated. The garment factory was opened more than (1) years ago, and there are days when the working hours are (8) am to 6:30 pm (2 hours overtime) and there are days when the labours work overtime (3 hours) and also the days where they work all night and all light with the ground of the fabric order importance. “Working all light reach until the next day morning. They forced us to work all light 4 or 5 days continuously. We have health issues such as vomiting and fainting for that,” said the labour. It is reported that the factory is owned by a Chinese national, employs more than 2,000 labours and manufactures brands such as REGATTA, KAPALUA, and has formed a Work Coordination Committee (WCC) without a trade union organization. When called for overtime, labours have to work whether they want to or not, he said. There are no lounges for labours who work overtime, and asking twice the standard even the prior is reached. It doesn’t have a normal format for the fabric standards and the Supers, Line Leaders and clerks swear and yell the labours, said by the labour. Pregnant workers are not asked to do works that relieves them but force for the same records as ordinary workers, and they say that pregnant women didn’t allow to get the gate pass even if they are sick. In addition, the labour also said that they are not allowed to take the days off that they are entitled to. "There is no enough cough relieve medicine in a medical clinic where there are more than 2,000 labours. 20 out of 40 toilets in the factory are broken and have not fixed yet. Even if we go to the toilet, the supervisors yell at us," said a labour working in the factory. Although 26th 27th and 28th of Octobers are Tha Din Kyut holidays the employers will close from 26th to 30th but 26th and 27th which are not officially entitled will have to replace by the September 24th where the labours work on Sunday and October 15th Sunday where they have to do the same. Those who don't show up on Sunday have been informed that the professional fee will be reduced to (2) levels, and the Great A person will only get C level. It is reported that the overtime work on the 23rd was only paid for 2 hours, and the remaining 4 hours of work were not paid but made to sign and print fingerprints due to day replacement.  As a result of the above violations, the labours are suffering a lot and feel that their rights are being violated. So that the labours want to request the following points because they are suffering from coercion. Content: HONG MIAO Garment Co; Ltd which locates at the No (4) Road, Thar Dhu Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon closed the factory after committing the highest level of labour rights violations, according to those helping the labours. "The guards were called to the Huan Myung factory. The owner did not come and said the factory would be closed. The boss did not come but sent the HR. Then they called the guards and threatened to sign and then close the work. The labours are not signing but they are planning to pressure and threaten the labours," said a labour. "Hua Myung Factory closed the factory on the grounds that there were no orders on September 26 and sent notice to the workers. The factory has been open for more than a year. This is a factory that the ministry found out because of a series of violations of labor rights in a warehouse where they operated illegally in Thar Dhu Kan industrial zone. Although they conducted inspections in the factory, none of the demands of the workers were implemented because the employers were hand in glove with the inspectors. On September 6, they gave me the forms to register the organization, but the head of the Office of Labour Guidance did not issue Form 6 but ignore. In addition, they are failing to take action to meet the minimum wage. Would the factory really close? Would they cheat and open it again? Whether they want to abolish the formation of the union will have to continue to be monitored,” said an individual helping the labours. As there are many violations in the factory, the labours applied to the head office to form a union, but they did not come and inspect it, nor give the Form 6. The employer found out the list of 48 labours who formed a union from the head office of labor, and fired those on the grounds that they did not have an order.  The 9 labours who were fired prior are also union members. This list of the labours was given to the entrepreneur by the head of the Office of Labour Guidance, and the entrepreneur fired according to this list. Line 2 was not paying by saying that there are no orders. Line 2 labours were sent to lines 3 and 4 but the rewards from those lines were not given to labours who were moved from Line 2. If they send the labours to Line 3 go, they have to pay them the same as the other labours of the line, and those labours sent a message that they can't pay less than one hundred thousand. There are many violations. Essentially, dropping all 48 members from 1 to 48 in the union is the most serious violation,” said the supporter. On September 20, negotiations were held, and the fired labours returned to the workplace and said they would continue to negotiate with other violations, but the 9 union leaders were not reappointed. The HONG MIAO Garment Co; Ltd factory is a factory that manufacture FieldCore brands. After settling the dispute on September 21st, the labours working in the factory are working in a dangerous workplace due to water entering the workplace, said by the supporter. The water used in the factory is not clean and clear, they are using dirty water and there is no fan installed in the workplace, so the workers made demands. On September 26th, with the reasons of saying that there was no order, and they took out a notice to close the factory, said by the people who are helping with the labour issues. Content: At the Amava Apparel Garment Factory in Pathein, Irrawaddy, some labours are suffering from headache and dizziness due to the smell of burning of asphalt around the factory as per the business requirements. Although they say that they are manufacturing asphalt according to business needs, it has been going on for almost a month, and the labours say that they are having difficulty working because of respiratory problems, dizziness, and even headaches. "Asphalt has been making to patch the roof of the factory for almost a month now. Even the regulatory department said that it is not possible to tell because it is according to business requirements. When they came to check on Friday at two o'clock in the afternoon, they said that it is not too bad, and nothing has been done," said the labour. "Because of this pungent smell, the labours are dizzy, swollen, have headaches, shortness of breath, those who have gum disease and wounds are inflamed and those who have had a C-section got stitches,” said a labour. “We wish that they manufacture the asphalt on off days or after the working hours. Now some got swollen gums and those who have had a C-section recently got stitches and headaches,” she continued. The factory is owned by a Sri Lankan citizen and manufacturing the Blaklader brand with around 1,000 labours. Content: The labours of the ibaek Myanmar Co.,Ltd garment factory which locates in Thaike Gyi, Yangon say that they are not allowed to take leaves and the factory even fire if they do. “Firing them saying “don’t come anymore” for missing a day. They are firing 3 or 4 people per month,” said a female labour who is currently working in Gibaek Myanmar Co.,Ltd garment factory.The woman also said that most of the people who were fired were fired because of taking leave. Even though the labours pay social security contributions, they said that they are not given any leave such as medical and casual leave, and if they take a leave, they are informed about the dismissal through the line leaders. "There was even a labour who is not allowed to take leave even with a hospital certificate of appendicitis. Labours are not fired by HR. but by the female all super. It's because it's kind of exposed at the bottom,” a female factory labour said. The labours said that to sign an employment contract (EC) between the garment factory and the the labours require 3 months of services. The Gibaek Myanmar Co.,Ltd garment factory is owned by a Korean citizen and the labours are being managed by the manager/all super (Daw-------). "She said she take two positions and is directly firing employees. She didn’t even warn as first or second attempts but fire immediately,” said the female labour. Gibaek Myanmar Co.,Ltd garment factory manufactures men and women wears and in addition it also produces the brand THE REDFACE based in South Korea. It is said that if they want to go back home from the workplace due to reasons including health, they will not be given a gate pass from the factory and it is informed in a meeting involving all labours. "They told us not to come out of the house if we are sick. They told us that we will not be allowed to return if we get to work," the labour said. Gibaek Myanmar Co., Ltd. is a jacket factory that has been opened in Kan Taw Kan ward, Thaike Gyi Township for only 6 months. Currently, the factory is operating with around 300 labours. Content: STUM state HONG MIAO Garment Co. Ltd which locates at No.4 Road, Thar Du Kan Industrial Zone, Shwe Pyi Thar Township, Yangon as the factory with the highest violation of labor rights. It is also reported that workers who formed a union to collectively solve workplace problems were fired from their jobs with the reasons that the employer saying not having orders.There are many violations of labor rights at the factory, and the workers formed a union to solve the problems at work and applied to the head office, but there was no inspection and no form was given. According to the labour list of the 48 workers that formed the union, the head office informed the employer and began to expel the workers from the union one by one. It is reported that the 2 layoffs at first, 9 layoffs later and the 41 layoffs on September 18th caused union labours to be laid off for the reason that there were no orders. “Nothing clears up the problem. It is only aimed at getting fired without solving. Form 6 is not given to form a union. The labours were fired on the pretext that there was no order. The people who were fired, were unknown unless the labour office inform. All people from the Line 2 are union members. Those who were removed from the other line were also people from the union. The 9 people prior are also people from the union. The head office gave the list of people to the employer, and the employer removed them according to this list. Removing Line 2 by saying there were no orders. People from line 2 are sent to other lines 3 and 4. But the rewards from that line were not given to people from line 2. If they let Line 3 go, Line 3 labours must receive the same as the other labours, and we also sent a letter saying that they can't pay less more than gapping one hundred thousand. A lot of violations. The main thing is firing all 48 people in the union, from 1 to 48, which is the most serious violation," said the person helping the labours. That factory It is also said to be a factory that manufactures Hello and FieldCore brands. “After 48 members of the union were fired, the three heads from the Office of Labour Guidance, Labour Office and Office of Workshop and Labor Law Inspection Department met with the labours when the employer's labor problem broke out. They kicked out all the labours, put the three union leaders in, and slammed the doors shut. And the owner did not sign on the agreement. The owner will remove the entire line where they were union members. He would remove it and make sure it will be mixed in the rest of the places. There is a super one among those fired. The employer didn't sign it, HR signed it. This morning, when I entered the factory, I don't know what all the heads of departments were talking about. The employer said that if Line 2 is not cancelled, no one will enter. The contract does not delete the line. Temporary replacement where necessary. The labours also asked why they had to cancel this line and work on other lines. The labours were fired on the grounds that there was no order," said the helper. "The entrepreneur has agreed to the request of the labours. The head of Office of Labour Guidance cannot be satisfied that it is already convenient. He again asked to go to the place according to the needs of the business. It is no longer the era where he has to agree. It is not only the employers who are involved in violations. It is said that the heads of the divisions are also present." He continued to say. The fired labours have returned to work, but negotiations will continue for many other violations. On September 21, STUM urged that it is time to protest to the GSP of the European Union and condemned the ignorant actions of the Garment Manufacturers Association MGMA as the labours of the factory were working in a bad workplace due to the water entering the factory, and the lives of the labours were considered priceless due to the investments of the inhumane employer. Content: The labours said they reached a negotiated settlement after the work stoppage of more than 250 labours at the Myanmar Huasheng Yashili Fashion Co.Ltd garment factory in Nyaung Inn Industrial Zone, Bago. Myanmar Huasheng Yashili Fashion Co.Ltd garment factory (blue carpet factory) locates at Utha (9) Ward, Nyaung Inn Industrial Zone, Bago and operates with nearly 1,000 workers, and 253 current workers have been laid off. "Fifty thousand kyats for less than 6 months of work experience and half of the monthly salary for 6 months and above. They said it was a mercy fee," said the labour. "The labours work all night and all light overtimes whenever the factory said it is important. So that for of the sudden work stoppage, the labours demand that to take care of them back," said a labor activist. The garment factory gave the workers a month's advance notice, but about 80 workers waited without working on September 21 to talk to officials about the compensation. "It is a mandatory form of payment by the factory. No matter how they call it compensation or mercy fees, it wouldn't have become such a demanding model if they consider priorly. I see that they give just because of asking,” said a labour activist. The Myanmar Huasheng Yashili Fashion Co.Ltd garment labours who will be stopped of work have been paid social security contributions since the month they started working, but they have not yet received social security cards. "If the social security income has been paid for 6 months, I can say that they could have received many benefits. Now the labours have to wait 6 months again if they come to the next job. Since they have been contributing as savings since they joined, they also suffer for the money," said the labour activist. The factory is responsible for obtaining social security cards, and the labours of Myanmar Huasheng Yashili Fashion Co.Ltd, who have been working for 6 months, do not have social security cards until the current work stoppage. The factory said if they get orders again, they will give priority to those who have stopped working, but the activist also pointed out that there is a need to be realistic. "These demanding labours may be blacklisted by the factories. I want to say that this should not happen. Nowadays, there are few jobs and currency doesn’t have value, and the labours are very difficult for the livelihoods. If they encounter a black list, they may not get the next job. It is necessary not to do such things," he continued. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: It is known that a factory is reported for not paying the minimum wage of 4,800 MMK but no actions are taken. “No matter how much the entrepreneur says he paid 4,800, The fact that the basic salary is written as 130,000 MMK on the wage sheet shows that the minimum wage is not paid. The labours don’t know that their salary is more than 200,000 MMK if their overtime and other fees combined. If they give 144,000 as basic salary, it will meet the minimum wage of 4,800 MMK per day. 130,000 is not a basic salary. There is no solution to this yet although it has been reported. It's been more than a month since Taw Win Wood Finishing Mill was reported and nothing has changed,” said by a laboural supporter.  According to STUM, there are 2 complaints from the labours at the Shwe Pyi Thar Township Office of Labour Guidance that they are not able to meet the minimum wage of 4800 kyats per day. A labour from Taw Win Wood Finishing Mill from Shwe Pyi Thar and another labour from Hong Miao Garment reported at the Township Office of Labour Guidance for getting the basic salary only 130,000 MMK. At present, as the commodity prices have risen exponentially, a labour can only be sufficient for livelihood if the daily wage is 10,000 MMK, so there have been requests to increase the current daily wage of 4,800 MMK to 10,000 MMK a day, and there are also statements pointing out that the daily wage should be MMK based on the price of goods and the dollar. "Yes, even though there have been requests for an increase in the minimum wage, the current minimum wage of 4,800MMK is still not being paid. Some factories do not want to pay the labours even 4,800 MMK. Therefore, they only hire them as day laborers. They even hire the children who are not yet of age with 3,600 MMK," said a labor affairs support worker. Currently, the factories pay 4,800 MMK per day to the workers, but there are cases where Sunday's wages are deducted, and violations such as calculated the wages by days and not paying on holidays and paying only 3,600 MMK instead of the minimum wage of 4,800 MMK per day. Content: On September 18, at around 5:00 p.m., a labour of the Fuhin (Shwe Khayu) Garment Factory died and twoA Shwe Khayu garment others were injured in a car accident near Shwe Rin Aye gold Shop, Old 86 gate, Anaw Rahtar Ratha Road, Ward 20, Hlaing Tharya West Township. Among the 3 died and 5 injured in the collision, 20 years old Ma May Thu Han, a resident of Ward 20, Hlaing Tharya West Township died and a 26 years old woman and a 27 years old woman who also live in Ward 20 were injured. All of them are the labours from the Fuhin (Shwe Khayu) Garment Factory from Shwe than Lwin Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar. "Three people were killed and five were injured. From the point of view, it was not a bus, but that goes to Kyai Lat or Pyar Phone. They said it was a ferry car. During the incident, there were no people in the car. It may have been the ferrying picking up the passengers. It is not known exactly. The driver is still running away," according to a charity association. The car which is also said as a ferry was from the Tha Ma Di Passenger Transport Line going towards Pyar Phone, and the driver, who rents a house in Hlaing Thar Yar West Township, is still on the run. Content: The Chinese-owned S-M MYANMAR Garment CO,LTD factory which locates in Shwe Than Lwin Industrial Zone (4) Hlaing Thar Yar Township has violated labours’ rights and forced them in workplace, according to the labours.  The employer violated the labours’ legal rights such as not providing casual leave, social security medical leave and if the labours miss a day of work due to illness, they will be cut daily wages 7,000 MMK, 5200 MMK, and attendance bonus 20,000 MMK. The labour said that the employer pressured them to resign their own if they take leaves. The factory has over 200 labour forces and manufacturing Mayrol brand Jackets. The labours were getting professional fees such as 90,000 MMK for A++, 70,000 MMK for A+, 50,000 MMK for A, 30,000 for B and 20,000 for C grades and the daily wages raises were ranges from 5,200 MMK to 7,000 MMK. But the labour gets less paid even though the daily wages were raised but because of the professional fees are reduced for 70,000 MMK such as 20,000 MMK for A++, A+ and A and 10,000 for B and C grades And the labours are also forced to manufacture the impossible fabric standards they ask, to produce 35 fabric units in a cavity with 40 people including the super, to manufacture the difficult jackets, resign if they can’t meet the standards and not having a break time due to unfair workload and men power. The all super and supers discriminate and swears them if they don’t meet the standards too. The underage day labourers are hired as HP and reassign to day labours if they take a leave just a day after promoting to monthly-labours and pay their salary with the rate of 3,600 MMK per day, not calculating the Sunday wages as the raised rates, paying only 4,800 a day and not paying for the Sunday too. It is also reported that the workers were told that if they do not work overtime on their days off which means they do not comply with the rules set by the factory, they have to quit of their own volition. Due to the violations, the labours appeals are to give the professional fee with previous rates, to survey their desire upon calling overtime, not to force it, the supers and all supers to not use slanders and discriminate the labours, to calculate the Sunday wages on the salary and to give the salary in the working hours. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: It is said that the minimum wage of 4,800 MMK per day is not enough due to the increase in commodity prices, but there are still some factories that do not pay even the minimum wage. At present, as the commodity prices have risen exponentially, and a labour can be comfortable only if the minimum wage is 10,000 MMK. There have been requests to increase the current daily wage of 4,800 kyats to 10,000 MMK a day, and critical statements are also on the rise. "Yes, even though there have been requests for an increase in the minimum wage, the current minimum wage of 4,800 MMK is still not being paid in everywhere. Some factories do not want to pay the labours even 4,800 MMK so they only hire them as day laborers and hiring under age labours with 3,600 MMK. Even they don’t want to raise the wages, they at least should give the full current wages. There are some places which pay 5,600 MMK a day so that 3600 should not be paid anymore. The labours don't complain anymore because of the oppressions and arrests,” said a laboural supporter. In addition, there are 2 complaints from labours at the Shwe Pyi Thar Office of Labor Guidance that did not meet the minimum wage, according to STUM. One letter of complaint was filed by a labour from the “Taw Win” Wood Finishing Mill because getting paid only a basic salary of 130,000 MMK and the another is from a labour of Hong Miao Garment Factory with the same issue of getting paid only 130,000 MMK. STUM said, "No matter how much the employer claims to have paid 4,800 MMK, the fact that the basic salary is written as 130,000 kyats instead of the basic salary on the wage sheet clearly shows that the minimum wage has not been paid. According to the labours, most of the employers refused to raise their wages, and some factory owners did not even pay 4,800 MMK a day and appointed them as day labourers and only paid them 3,600 MMK a day. Content: Jia Xin (Myanmar) Garment Co; Ltd in Shwe Pyi Thar is forcing a 7-month pregnant labour to work without giving a rest period, according to a labour aid person. The pregnant labour was sick on September 9, so she asked for a gate pass. It is reported that Line Super Ma---- said "Just leave if you can’t handle" without giving. She didn't work overtime as she was sick and returned home. After visiting the welfare clinic on the 11th, she was on medical leave for 3 days and was off work until 13.9.2023. When she returned to the work on 14.9.23 the line super call her to the corner of the line and humiliate her by yelling at her “Don’t work here furthermore if you can’t work overtime. Resign with your perception. What are you expecting form here? You didn’t even meet the hourly demands. And you don’t want to work evening overtime all night, all light and 20:00. If you want to just chill at your house, then do it. Don’t come here. Resign with self-intuition,”  On September 15, she was not allowed a break on lunch time and forced to work instead of it while other employees were having their lunch. She was told to eat only after she met the hourly demands. Although the labour is 7 months pregnant, she has not taken a single day of pregnancy leave, and she is not allowed to use the one day leave per month to visit the antenatal clinic until she is now 7 months pregnant. According to the labour laws, pregnant workers are entitled to social security leave and other benefits such as maternity leave, to be assigned to work only light tasks with full pay. In fact, assigning pregnant labours the same work load with other workers, such as demanding for the same standard, is being committed in factories and is violating the law, the labor activist said. In addition, among the many violations in the factory, the HR manager takes the roles of both, the position of interpreter and production, handling tasks and decisions in the workplace. forced to work without OT pay, cheating the labours' signatures by signing resignation papers without the knowledge of the parties involved. This is also the factory where a dispute broke out with 12 labours for the above violations. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: According to the labor law, factories working hours is 8 hours a day. Although overtime is set at 20 hours per week, most factory labours have about 2 hours of overtime during their normal working hours, and the minimum working day is 10 hours.  According to the labours, they are currently working from 12 to 16 hours a day due to the reasons of getting much orders in the garment industry. Sometimes, they have to go to work all day and night, go back home in the morning, take a shower, and go back to work. "All night means working until 1 o'clock or 2 o'clock, or all lin (all light) means you have to go down all night until dawn. There is no time limit," said a labour. According to the labours, if their health is affected due to such long working hours and no rest time, they will not receive health benefits and welfare benefits, and they will even lose more benefits. "Recently, labours have been working more hours unfairly. If they want to take day off because of sick, tired and sleep irregularly, they can't. The employers don't allow it. They said they can’t allow without reporting in advance or without having a prescription. Even so, they are cut off. Working 20 hours a day can harm in long term. There are quite a lot of labour who are fired because they don't work overtime," said the laboural supporter. "Factory, in the guidelines on the procedures to be followed” expressed by the Junta’s Ministry of Labour in last year June stated the working overtime in workshops, specifying that any labour may not work more than 44 hours per week without overtime, and overtime is 3 hours a day and 15 hours for Monday to Friday. 5 hours for Saturday. Only 20 hours per week are set to work. Currently, most of the factories are aggressively recruiting overtime, and if the labours want to take leave due to ill health, they required approval of the Social Security Office. Content: It has been reported that workers and brokers are falsifying the documents required to apply for an overseas employment identification (OWIC) card. In the past, 22 workers were blacklisted because they submitted forged documents to the Department, and their permission to travel abroad was blocked, and some of the participants were taken action.  At present, they have heard of illegal entrances to other countries by applying for OWIC, claiming to be Macau, so they will thoroughly check the fake documents. In the past, because there were so many OWIC card applicants, it was not possible to verify the authenticity of the document, and some brokers and workers took advantage of this and made fake paper documents. An official from the Ministry of Labor of the Junta said that they will be allowed to print an OWIC card after the documents have been thoroughly verified. Currently, the OWIC card must be applied for at the Ministry of Labor in Nay Pyi Taw with the necessary documents, and it is said that they are being issued at the North Dagon Labor Training School and the 8 Mile Labor Office in Ma Yan Gone Township. Content: "I haven't taken off day for a whole month even on holidays and special occasions. I have to work overtime all evening and all night. Sometimes, if we miss overtime, the super and all super (supervisors) get angry and discriminate by not calling overtime for the whole month," said the unnamed labour.  Jun Sheng Garment Co., Ltd., a garment factory located om Wet Ma Swet Assistant Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar, is operating with around 400 labours and the labours are appealing to give some off days as they have been working full month with no off days. The factory is owned by Chinese nationals, manufacturing pants, shirts, and warm clothes of RESERVED QUIKSILVER, GEMO LOGOSDAYS, Pedro del Hierro ZARA etc Brands. The labours, who did not want to be named, said that they would like to ask for a day off because they have been working without a day off for a whole month. The working hours starts at 8:00 Am and does not have specific ending time and having to work overtime for whole night and until morning. Garment labours have to go to work from the end of the day, called all-nighters, and have to work from night to dawn, and they have to work overtime without rest the next day, causing health problems. "I don't even have time to sleep anymore. I don't get enough sleep. My health is ruined. If I miss 1 day of work, I will be cut off my daily allowance and extra pay," said the labour. He said that even though he was forced to work overtime, he did not receive full overtime pay in the payment of wages and was being cut off every month. Labours are told that they will be given casual medical leave and seniority leave, but if they are sick from work and take leave, daily fee of 5,600 kyats, attendance bonus of 20,000 kyats, grade fee (20,000 kyats for A) a total of 45,600 kyats was cut. It is said that the total of 45,600 kyats that is deducted if 1 day of work is missed is 5,600 kyats, which is the factory labours’ wages for 8 days. He said that if there is a workplace inspection or audit, the labours are threatened to answer as they were told, and the labour who answered the truth was fired in the past. "The manager and super-supervisor pressure labours to answer as they were told in an inspection. As they fired the labour who answered the truth before, the labours no longer dare to tell the truth. That's why the truth is hidden that workplace violations do not appear," the worker said. Day laborers are also employed in the workplace, and if they refuse to work overtime, they are fired. He also said that if an injury occurs in the workplace, they are dismissed from work without medical treatment. It is known that there is no labor union in the workplace, but the WCC has been formed and is selected by the employer. The labour said that there was no negotiation of any topic with the employer and coordinate the needs. "They 10,000 each from the labours. They told us it is to prostrate the mentors in Thadingyut. In addition, they would ask more in the name to prostrate supers and all supers.  We can’t refuse. They are forcing me to pay as much as they asked," the labour said. Also, in demanding fabric standards, the fabric used changes frequently, so the requests become more and more day by day without regular fabric standards. If the labours don’t meet the record, they are forced and pressurize by the Super and all Supers. They are forced to work without taking a break and have to work free if the fabric quality drops. The labours said that they want to appeal to the factory to avoid asking overtime unfairly. to ask the consent of the labours, to allow the labours to choose the workplace bargaining committee, to demand only a standard that labours could make, to not force overtime for free, to provide holiday benefits, to take responsibility in the event of an injury in the workplace, and to not allow the supervisors to abuse the workers and to not ask for any fees.  To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: According to the Federation of Solidarity Unions (STUM), which is supporting the issue, a hearing has been scheduled for October 6 regarding the lawsuit filed by the labour against the officials of the Pepsi soft drink factory in Mawbe Township. Last August 14th, at 10:00 a.m. in the morning of the division court, there was a trial negotiation but no settlement was reached, so a further hearing was scheduled for September 14th at the Mawbe District Court. "At today's trial, the documents do not arrive back to the district court, so the 6th trial was scheduled for October 6th. One month after the division trial (14-8-2023), the process has not yet arrived at the lower office, so it's the next appointment," STUM informed.  On July 28th, as the third trial of the worker's lawsuit, the district judge accepted both sides of the employer and labour and interrogated them. The entrepreneur delegated the legal representative to HR on behalf of the CEO and HR, and the two parties negotiated in the district court according to the legal negotiation procedure. U Thaung Han, the aggrieved labour who filed the lawsuit, was fired on October 31, 2022 due to his old age in violation of the employment agreement, so he sued for 10,040,000 MMK in legal damages in the Mawbe District Court. On November 2022, U Thaung Han, who was fired, filed a complaint to Department of Labour Guidance and transferred it to the township negotiation, which negotiated 3 times. Although the council's decision was accepted, it was transferred back to Department of Labour Guidance, so Department of Labor Guidance and the regional office negotiated three more times to resolve the issue, but there was no solution. It is reported that the labour was instructed to file a lawsuit only in the middle of March 2023, only after the victim worker repeatedly requested the supervisor to issue an order to file a lawsuit against the victim. If the fired labour who worked for up to twenty years is fired because of his age he must get the severance of 4,050,000. It is reported that this kind of lawsuit started because the labour issued a letter of intent to file a lawsuit after a long time of the employer's agreement on the negotiation. The labour who worked at the Pepsi factory for 20 years and was fired on 31 October 2022 in violation of the employment contract. According to seniority laws, he will receive severance pay of over 50,000 kyats. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: A male worker at the BOHUA Garment Factory was fired himself told Myanmar labour news that his normal argument with a supervisor were accused as skirmish.  “I retaliate as the supervisor is scolding and they accused it as a skirmish in the workplace,” said the male labour. The supervisor told him that “How you guys useless? Can’t even do this,” when he appointed them to move a 20 fabric rolls which has around 150 meters to four stories and the labours told “Its not possible with only two people,”. “We can’t carry it to 4 stories height. Its not the level our height reach. Its super heavy even with two people. The slur he used is too rude. He left and came back to scold again telling that we don’t work professionally in front of other people,” the labour explains the details. After a few words between the male worker and the warehouse supervisor (super), the super complained to the office. The male labour said that he was fired after that.  “They said that they could fire me because of my service is only 1 month old. As written in the dismissal letter, there was no conflict. As per their words that I don't follow the management, its means I have to risk my life for mismanagement. It is fair to make us carry the over buy light fabrics. But it's linen rolls. Before that I refused some warehouse works that they assigned me to do at house. I think that I was fired because of that,” said the labour. He said that the day before September 14, when the argument occurs, he refused the work that the warehouse supervisor told him to cut about a thousand adhesive tapes. "A thousand piece of adhesive tape takes about an hour even if it is cut by an expert. You can make an appointment at the factory.  I can cut it than. As soon as I got home, I had to do housework. It is not easy to take a factory job home. No wages for that. We only get 4,800 per day," he said. When BOHUA FASHION Co,.ltd started recruiting, they said they would pay 5,600 per day. The labours complain about this when the found out that the according to the EC contract they would only get paid 4,800 MMK but they were told that “don’t work if you don’t like,”.  "In EC information, it is classified as ordinary and serious mistakes. Even if it's wrong, I think it should be only be a warning with reasons. Now, the factory is biased and discriminated between senior and junior positions," said the male worker. According to Ma Aye Aye, who is handling the labor dispute, it is not a fair decision to fire only one person in the conflict between the two sides. "Being fired at a time when jobs are scarce will be difficult for labours. The labour’s service is also low, so the factory's decision becomes "adding insult to injury". The factory also pays a notice, but it is good to decide according to the wishes of the labour." Ma Aye Aye said. The labour told Myanmar Labor News that on September 15, the factory paid him who only have a service of a little over a month old, a month notice fee and wages based on the days he worked. BOHUA Fashion Co.,ltd factory located in Ban Maw Secretary Street, Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar Township, Yangon was reported in September for labor rights violations. It is known that the owner of the factory is a Chinese national, having around 300 laboursers and manufacturing clothes from other factories. The brands that the factory manufactures are Sinsay, Protection CROPP, P&VV and reserve. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. Content: According to the labours, most of the factories in Yangon division say in last June that they will pay the labours a minimum wage of 5,600 MMK a day instead of 4,800 MMK a day, but they are still paying only 4,800 MMK as before.   Due to the high domestic good prices, the current rate that the labours receive is not enough to live on. International investments such as garment factories had announced that the daily wage will be increased from last June to 5,600 to 5,900 MMK. But as the government have not officially announced yet, there are still violations with various reasons. “That’s true. Most factories don’t give 5,600 MMK. Some do and some only pay if the fabric meet the standards. Its only 4,800 MMK. Some factories even appoint on prohibition 3,600 MMK.  As the laws don’t make these issues clear, the employers give only 3,600 MMK,” said a laboural activist. In some workplaces, only day laborers are hired and paid only 4,800 kyats, and young workers and helpers 3,600 kyats. “Some said that can't raise the price because the government has officially set it at 4,800 MMK. The law stipulates that you can pay a minimum of 4,800 MMK. There is no such things that forbit paying more than that,” said a female garment labour. Most of the factories in Yangon announced in last May and June saying that they will pay the labours 5,600 MMK but only little increase from 4,800 to 5,600 MMK while most of them still paying as before. Furthermore, prohibition labours are only paid 3,600 and 5,600 is only paid when the labours meet their heavy standard demands. Paying 1,400 MMK for an hour of overtime doesn’t fit for the overtime fee if the daily wages if 5,600 MMK. In addition, even though the factory pays 5,600 MMK, if a labour is fired for any reason, the factory only pays 4,800 MMK severance pay for wages and legal damages, according to the workers. “If they define daily wages as 5,600 MMK, overtime fee should be paid more than 1,400 MMK. We can say that getting only 1,400 MMK is not getting full wages. The labours are tolerating as only they don’t want to have any problems,” they continue.  “It would be comfortable only if we got minimum 10,000 MMK per day. I think we are working for 5,600 MMK more than 5 years. The government don’t watch over the labours and employers are taking advantages from this, exploitering.   The labours do report about paying only 4,800 while 5,600 is stated and paying the severance with 4,800 rates but as the domestic labours are being arrested, tortured and threatened, they have no choice rather than tolerating. Content: It is reported that labours are suffering from many rights violations in BOHUA Fashion factory which locates in Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone, Hlaing Thar Yar. The factory is owned by Chinese national and operated by more than 300 workers manufacturing brands such as Sinsay, CROPP, P&VV and PROTECTION. BOHUA Fashion Co.,ltd factory blatantly violates labor rights. Legal benefits such as medical leave are strictly forbidden by the HR and all supers with various reasons, the labours got cut for daily wages 5,600 MMK, Attendance Bonus 15,000 MMK and other grade fees if they miss for a day as they can’t take a leave. "If we are asked for fabric good fabric as a whole line today (25) units, the next day is (30); If we get 35 units the next day, we are asked for 40 units the next day. They are taking far more than we can do," the labour informed.  Supers and leaders are threating and pressuring that labours who do not receive clothing records will not be paid a stipend (5,600 kyats). (4,800 kyats) and swear to the labours who don’t get the demands. The labours are sworn by using rude words daily and forcing 3 or 4 hours of overtime a day without informing in advanced. The working hours start at 8:00 Am and not giving any break time from 12:30  after lunch to 20:30. Due to the lack of adequate food, they suffer from stomach aches, hunger, and health problems.In addition, there is no clinic inside the factory, and if the workers have dizziness and headache, if they go to ask for medicine, there super store said they don’t have and to buy from outside for the outside health issues.  Furthermore, the employer calls for overtime they wish without prior notice, lack of break time, not enough dining tables, pretend not knowing the labours needs, assign more than 50 labours as day labours. Day laborers were paid a wage of 4,800 kyats, labours who quit their jobs will only be paid 4,800 as the government has only officially state 4,800 kyats, so the workers who quit their jobs are not entitled to benefits, the Supercommittee said that too. They said that they will pay 5,600 MMK for daily wages and highest grade wages but they pay like they wish to and the Chinese woman yells and scolds the labours too. The labours are pressured to work in other sections and having to work overtime for those sections too. They also have to work Overtime from Monday to Friday (8:30) to (9:30) and until the next morning in every Saturdays. The labours also suffer from health issues for overtime overloads. The brands that are manufactured in the factory are taken as sub-orders from other factories, Sinsay and Protection from peach Garden factory near Shwe Pyi Thar, CROPP from JIANGSU SAINTY GLORIOUS TRADE CO,LDT factory and P&VV from a factory in South Dagon. It is reported that the factory does not have a trade union, nor has the WCC been formed, so if the workers have any issues, there is no way to lead a discussion and negotiation. Therefore, the labours have appealed to allow their medical and causal leaves which they are entitled to, not to let the Chinese woman to manage them directly, to ask their consent when calling overtime, not to pressure them if they refuse, not to discriminate, to assign the day labours as permanent after 3 months, to give daily wages and grade bonuses properly and to not call overtime for until morning. To uphold the rule of law needed to improve the social-economic life of the working class in Myanmar. To help the transition to democracy as media role in the workforce gender equity.

Content: Labours at the Myanmar Guotai Huasheng Glory Fashion Garment Factory say that the factory is committing labour rights violations without resolving workplace issues. The factory is located in U Htun Nyo Street, Hlaing Thar Yar Industrial Zone 2, Yangon.  According to the labours, the issues occurring are forcing the fired labours to write that they resigned with their desire and if not intimidate about the wages, forcing C and D grades labours to meet the A and B standards even the standards are classified as A, B, C and D in the workplace. supervisors using to slanders to subordinates while asking for the fabric demands, not resolving the labour and workplace issues although reported.  More than 700 labours are employed and owned by Chinese national. The factory is also manufacturing PRIMARK, esmara and Inextenso brands. “26 of us have to work to get the standards that 33 of us used to in the past. They take far more than our best.  Even though the grades are divided into A, B, C, and D according to the skill level, they force those with low skill fees to manufacture big points.  It is reported that if there is any work-related problem during the work, there is no trade union formed to solve it, and there is no solution even when they go to inform the currently formed work coordination committee WCC. In the demand for the fabric standard of the individual labours, they yell at the substandard labours, especially the Line 12 Super and Line 5 Super. In line 5, each labour was asked to shout for the record at each step, and the labour said that they are also taking actions to pressurize and fight.  "They made the labours to yell at each other for asking fabric standards which means inciting them. Asking for a record is Super's job, and the workers should not be doing this,” said a labour. There are also other violations such as even if there are various reasons, they are not allowed to use the phone during working hours, they are not allowed to return if they are sick, and the labours who quit are prohibited from saying that they quit because of heavy workload, the ferry is not on time, monitoring the labours having sneak on break time and forcing them to sign warning and not taking responsibilities by not checking CCTV if there is a loss of phones and money in the factory.   As they don’t take any responsibilities in the workplace and never consider the labours appeals, the labours want the factory side to resolve these issues. Content: According to the labours, the Ford Glory factory which is located in School Street, Shwe Pyi Thar is intimidating the labours and calling for unfair overtime.  It is also known that because of labours working overtime every day without a day off, their health is affected and they are cut off without permission for a leave, and if they can’t work overtime, the factory holds grudges and find fault and are fired. The working hours are only until half past four. Even today, we can't go back home. We have to work not only all night but also all day. If we said we can’t work overtime, they would fire us. Also, it is not just one day but every day. We humans are not robots. There is even no time to sleep. We reported to many individuals but they stop calling only that day and they would call back later," said a labour. Currently, they are preparing to call for two shifts in the morning and night, and it is convenient for the day workers by ferry support, but it is not convenient for the night shift workers as they don’t have. I heard that they will arrange morning week and night week for a week. Those who work in the morning have a ferry and those who work at night don’t and they have to go by bus. We don’t like that. And overtime hours are always different from our timestamps and theirs. They never resolve that even if we point out.  We get back home at 4 Am if we work all day and all night and have to go back to work at 8. Getting back home at 00:00 Am if only all night. We work all day and all night for today. We don’t even get an off day in a weekend. We want it,” said the labour. “We are not allowed for a leave if our health breaks down because of consecutive overtime Workers who do not work overtime are fired. Not without cause but with various reasons. There is no WCC in the factory. I reported this to the manager and super, but nothing happened. Even reporting the labour prevent only that day,” said a labour. It is reported that the factory is a Chinese-owned factory, and with 500 labours, it sews over-bought warm clothes and exports them to China. In addition, the factory often changes its name and operates according to the worker. In this factory, it is reported that SINSAY and other stamps are being sewn. Content: It is reported to Myanmar Labour News that the labor supervisor of each level of the Bego-based KFINE garment factory Verbal Abuse the subordinate labours. The factory labours say that most of the leaders who oversee the machine lines are swearing at the subordinates. 'They swear in every morning meeting. Abusing even our parents that makes us suffer. No one would love to hear that," said a female labour. The KFINE garment factory has around 20 machine lines, and each line has a supervisor (super). The labours said that one leader and four machine lines are supervised by an all super.A total of 50 sewing labours and assistants are working on the machine lines, and discuss business plans in the form of a meeting every morning. "In a morning which is not too far long, Line 10 Super sworn a young female worker insulting that she was born from unintegrated family. How embarrassed she would feel. She than left work. If the super and leaders swear, the words aren’t any rather than lower body parts" said a woman working at the factory. The labours said that the All Super and Leader from line 10 , Super from Line 8 and the Leader from Line 5 cursed the subordinates violently. “Some supers swear badly. They always use in profanities. Insult the families and downgrade by comparing with the body parts too. How young women could withstand. They all resigned. Furthermore, supers said as the factory told as they get paid three or four times more than average labours. The factory sides also favored supers who swear,” said a female labour. Myo Myo Than said that although the supers do not intend to make some labours who are uncomfortable with them in the machine line leave their jobs, they may also speak in an insulting way. Most of the labours said that even though the managers saw that the supers were Verbal Abuseing the workers, they acted as if they didn't know. KFINE Garment forced some pregnant workers out of work. This is a factory that has been complained about for not paying specific overtime pay and not appointing probationary labours according to the specified month. The labours also said that because there were such complaints, when the township officials of the Ministry of Labor inspected the factory, they were not allowed to tell about the factory's violations as the manager was near the inspectors. After this inspection, the Ministry of Labor took action with some articles that there were violations in the KFINE factory. After the complaint and investigation, four young female labours in the factory were fired for making complaints about the factory, a labour who worked in the factory told Myanmar Labor News. The labour said that the factory interrupts the four women who were fired to work in the next factory. KFINE International Garment (Myanmar) is located in A Wyne Village, Bago City Bypass Road, Bago. According to the website of Nantong KFINE, the company that owns the factory, it is located near the Pagoda, and operates with around 1,000 labours. According to the workers, Bago Kfine Myanmar Garment can produce more than three million garments a year, mainly producing jackets, but they also sew British-based RESERVED brand. Nantong Kfine, the parent company of Kfine International Garment (Myanmar), is a China-based company that has offices in some countries around the world and manufactures garments from five factories owned by the company.
